packs.name: Words & Everyday Life
packs.tagline: 21 pages · fill the notebook, word by word

chapters.text: Name an interjection or exclamation

krillion.quip: From Old French "grant merci" — once both a thank-you and a gasp of surprise.

quips.Crikey: A Victorian minced oath — a polite dodge around swearing by Christ.
quips.Strewth: Squashed down from "God's truth" — beloved of Australians.
quips.Cowabunga: Born on 1950s kids' TV (Howdy Doody) long before surfers and turtles took it.
quips.Gadzooks: A 1600s minced oath — basically polite cursing.
quips.Odds bodkins: A softened "God's body" — Elizabethans were masters of the minced oath.

chapters.text: Name a word that rhymes with "cat"

krillion.quip: A stepped Mesopotamian temple tower — and a perfect rhyme for cat.

quips.Cravat: Named after Croatian soldiers whose neckties dazzled 1600s Paris.
quips.Requiescat: Latin for "may he rest" — a prayer for the dead, and a sneaky rhyme.
quips.Cushat: An old Scots name for the wood pigeon.

chapters.text: Name a color or shade

krillion.quip: The orange-red of a wild poppy — it's simply the French word for poppy.

quips.Puce: French for "flea" — literally the colour of a flea.
quips.Eigengrau: German for "intrinsic grey" — what your eyes see in total darkness.
quips.Gamboge: A mustard-yellow tree resin, named after Cambodia.
quips.Glaucous: The dusty blue-grey bloom you can rub off a plum.

chapters.text: Name a job or occupation

krillion.quip: Makes arrows — from Old French "flèche", meaning arrow.

quips.Cordwainer: A maker of new shoes — cobblers were only allowed to mend them.
quips.Knocker-upper: Before alarm clocks, they tapped on windows with long poles to wake workers.
quips.Tosher: Victorian scavengers who searched London's sewers for lost coins.
quips.Luthier: A maker of stringed instruments — from the French for lute.
quips.Fuller: Pounded wool cloth to thicken it, often by trampling it underfoot.

chapters.text: Name something you'd find in a bathroom

krillion.quip: A stick of alum that stops tiny shaving nicks from bleeding.

quips.Loofah: It's not a sea sponge — it's the dried fibre of a gourd from the cucumber family.
quips.Bidet: French for 'pony' — you sit astride it like one.
quips.Toilet: From French 'toilette', a little cloth used while dressing.
quips.Strop: A leather strap barbers use to hone a straight razor's edge.

chapters.text: Name a piece of furniture

krillion.quip: In Britain it's a small writing desk; in America, a big sofa.

quips.Tallboy: A double-height chest of drawers — Americans call its cousin a highboy.
quips.Teapoy: A small tea table whose name comes from Hindi for "three-footed".
quips.Prie-dieu: French for "pray God" — a kneeling desk for private prayers.
quips.Tuffet: A low seat or footstool — Little Miss Muffet's famous perch.

chapters.text: Name an item of clothing

krillion.quip: From Persian "kamarband" — literally a loin-band.

quips.Cardigan: Named after the 7th Earl of Cardigan, who led the Charge of the Light Brigade.
quips.Balaclava: Named after the Crimean War battle where British troops wore knitted versions.
quips.Farthingale: A hooped underskirt that made Tudor dresses spread like bells.
quips.Spencer: A cropped jacket named after the 2nd Earl Spencer in the 1790s.

chapters.text: Name a collective noun for a group of animals

krillion.quip: Like many of these, it was popularised by the 15th-century Book of Saint Albans.

quips.Murder (of crows): Folklore tied crows to death and omens — hence the grim name.
quips.Crash (of rhinos): Rhinos can charge at around 30 mph, so a crash feels earned.
quips.Flamboyance (of flamingos): A modern coinage, but too perfect not to catch on.
quips.Bloat (of hippos): Hippos spend most of the day wallowing in water — bloat suits them.

chapters.text: Name a toy

krillion.quip: A Victorian spinning disc that merges two pictures — like a bird into its cage.

quips.Teddy bear: Named after US President Theodore 'Teddy' Roosevelt, who spared a bear on a 1902 hunt.
quips.Slinky: Invented by an engineer who watched a torsion spring tumble off a shelf.
quips.Silly Putty: A failed attempt at synthetic rubber that turned into a bestselling toy.

chapters.text: Name a type of bag

krillion.quip: A tiny drawstring handbag of Regency ladies — mocked at the time as a 'ridicule'.

quips.Sporran: The pouch worn with a kilt — because kilts have no pockets.
quips.Gladstone bag: Named after the Victorian prime minister William Gladstone.
quips.Bum bag: Americans call it a fanny pack, a phrase that makes Brits blush.
quips.Carpetbag: Made from old carpet — and the origin of 'carpetbagger' in post-Civil War America.

chapters.text: Name a word or phrase English borrowed from French

krillion.quip: "Staircase wit" — the perfect comeback you only think of on the way out.

quips.Denim: Short for "serge de Nîmes" — sturdy cloth from the French city of Nîmes.
quips.Cul-de-sac: Literally "bottom of the bag" in French.
quips.Mal de mer: French for seasickness — "sickness of the sea".
quips.Courgette: British English took the French word; Americans borrowed Italian "zucchini".

chapters.text: Name a type of hat

krillion.quip: The broad sun hat of ancient Greece — Hermes wore one with wings.

quips.Bowler hat: Designed in 1849 to stop gamekeepers' hats being knocked off by branches.
quips.Stetson: Named after John B. Stetson, who made his first 'Boss of the Plains' in 1865.
quips.Fez: Named after the Moroccan city of Fez, once the main source of its crimson dye.
quips.Mortarboard: Named for its likeness to a bricklayer's board for holding mortar.

chapters.text: Name a type of shoe or footwear

krillion.quip: Venetian platform shoes up to 50 cm tall, worn to keep dresses out of the mud.

quips.Wellingtons: Named after the Duke of Wellington, who had his Hessian boots modified.
quips.Espadrilles: Named after esparto, the tough grass used to make their rope soles.
quips.Plimsolls: Their rubber band reminded people of the Plimsoll line painted on ships.
quips.Geta: Japanese wooden sandals raised on two wooden 'teeth'.

chapters.text: Name a fabric or textile

krillion.quip: Cheap cloth made from recycled wool rags — which is how the word became an insult.

quips.Calico: Named after Calicut in India, where the cotton cloth was traded.
quips.Muslin: Named after Mosul in modern-day Iraq.
quips.Bombazine: A silk-and-wool cloth Victorians wore for mourning.
quips.Denim: Its twill weave goes back to 'serge de Nîmes' in southern France.
quips.Byssus: Sea silk spun from the threads clams use to anchor themselves.

chapters.text: Name a palindrome (word, name or phrase)

krillion.quip: James Joyce's word for a knock on the door — the OED's longest palindrome.

schooler: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama
Was it a car or a cat I saw
rare: Able was I ere I saw Elba
Rats live on no evil star
Go hang a salami, I'm a lasagna hog
Mr. Owl ate my metal worm
Was it a cat I saw
Eva, can I see bees in a cave
Ma is a nun, as I am
Murder for a jar of red rum
A nut for a jar of tuna
Was it a rat I saw
Too bad, I hid a boot
Eva, can I stab bats in a cave
deepcut: Sit on a potato pan, Otis
Never a foot too far, even
Pull up if I pull up
Dog as a devil deified, lived as a god
Was it Eliot's toilet I saw
Cigar? Toss it in a can, it is so tragic
Ten animals I slam in a net

A man, a plan, a canal: Panama: A man a plan a canal Panama
Was it a car or a cat I saw: Was it a car or a cat I saw?

quips.Racecar: Spell it backwards and you get… racecar. Spaces aside, it never fails.
quips.Kinnikinnik: A Native American smoking blend of leaves and bark — and an 11-letter palindrome.
quips.Redivider: One of the longest everyday English palindromes, at nine letters.
quips.Malayalam: A language of southern India whose very name reads the same both ways.

chapters.text: Name a hairstyle or haircut

krillion.quip: Invented in the 1870s by Parisian hairdresser François Marcel with heated tongs.

quips.Mullet: "Business in the front, party in the back" — a phrase popularised in the 1990s.
quips.Pompadour: Named after Madame de Pompadour, mistress of King Louis XV.
quips.Mohawk: Named after the Mohawk people, though the style is linked to other nations too.
quips.Beehive: Created by Chicago hairdresser Margaret Vinci Heldt in 1960.

chapters.text: Name a word ending in "-ology"

krillion.quip: The study of birds' eggs — a word made almost entirely of O's.

quips.Campanology: The art of bell-ringing — from Latin 'campana', meaning bell.
quips.Psephology: The study of elections, from the Greek pebble ('psephos') ancient Athenians voted with.
quips.Tegestology: Collecting beer mats — from Latin 'teges', a mat.
quips.Vexillology: The study of flags, from 'vexillum', a Roman military banner.
quips.Apology: Not a field of study — it comes from Greek 'apologia', a speech in one's defence.

chapters.text: Name a car brand

krillion.quip: A Spanish luxury marque whose flying-stork mascot honoured a WWI fighter squadron.

quips.Lamborghini: Ferruccio Lamborghini built tractors before he took on Ferrari.
quips.Audi: Latin for 'listen!' — a pun on founder August Horch, whose surname means 'hark'.
quips.Subaru: The Japanese name for the Pleiades star cluster — hence the stars on the badge.

chapters.text: Name a household chore

krillion.quip: Polishing a cast-iron range with graphite paste — a weekly Victorian chore.

Walking the dog: Taking the dog for a walk

quips.Donkey stoning: Scrubbing doorsteps with a 'donkey stone' to keep them gleaming — a Northern English pride.
quips.Mangling: Squeezing wet laundry through rollers — 'put through the mangle' comes from this.
quips.Turning collars: Unpicking a worn shirt collar and sewing it back on upside down.

chapters.text: Name a punctuation mark or typographic symbol

krillion.quip: A ?! fused into one mark, dreamed up by an American ad executive in 1962.

quips.Octothorpe: A jokey name for # coined by Bell Labs engineers in the 1960s.
quips.Pilcrow: The ¶ mark — medieval scribes used it to start new trains of thought.
quips.Ampersand: Comes from 'and per se and', how children once recited & at the end of the alphabet.
quips.Manicule: The little pointing hand that medieval readers doodled in margins.

chapters.text: Name a holiday or celebration

krillion.quip: Shetland's fire festival, where a replica Viking longship is torched each January.

quips.Boxing Day: Named for the 'Christmas boxes' of money once given to servants and tradespeople.
quips.Festivus: Born in a TV writer's family and made famous by Seinfeld — complete with an unadorned pole.
quips.Hogmanay: Scotland's New Year, when first-footers bring coal, shortbread or whisky for luck.
quips.Groundhog Day: If Punxsutawney Phil sees his shadow, folklore says six more weeks of winter.

chapters.text: Name a Super Mario character

krillion.quip: Mario's bossy rival from 1985's Wrecking Crew who sabotages his demolition jobs.

quips.Pauline: The original damsel from 1981's Donkey Kong, now mayor of New Donk City.
quips.Birdo: A bow-wearing dinosaur who first appeared as a boss in Super Mario Bros. 2.
quips.Fawful: A Mario & Luigi villain famous for lines like 'I have fury!'

chapters.text: Name a social media app or platform

krillion.quip: A 2002 social network that later reinvented itself as a gaming site in Asia.

quips.Vine: Every video was capped at six seconds, and it still launched careers.
quips.Musical.ly: The lip-sync app that was merged into TikTok in 2018.
quips.Myspace: Everyone's first friend there was Tom, the site's co-founder.

chapters.text: Name a board game

krillion.quip: An ancient Egyptian race game; Tutankhamun was buried with several boards.

rare: Betrayal at House on the Hill
deepcut: Game of Thrones: The Board Game

quips.Monopoly: It grew out of The Landlord's Game, designed in 1904 to criticise landlords.
quips.Diplomacy: A strategy game with no dice at all, famous for wrecking friendships.
quips.Mancala: A family of seed-sowing games played for over a thousand years.

chapters.text: Name a Mario Kart course

krillion.quip: A spooky Super Circuit track on a rickety boardwalk full of holes.

quips.Baby Park: A tiny oval where seven laps of item chaos never let up.
quips.Coconut Mall: Its famous parked cars stopped driving in the Booster Course Pass version.
quips.Big Blue: A F-Zero course that turned into Mario Kart 8's water-slide DLC track.

chapters.text: Name a Minecraft block

krillion.quip: A pink flower that hangs from lush-cave ceilings, raining green spores.

quips.Bedrock: Unbreakable in survival, it forms the very floor of every Overworld.
quips.Sponge: It soaks up water around it and can be dried out in a furnace.
quips.Barrier: An invisible block map makers use to fence players in.

chapters.text: Name a Street Fighter, Mortal Kombat or Tekken fighter

krillion.quip: Street Fighter's joke fighter, created to mock a rival game's copycat karate guys.

quips.Yoshimitsu: A sword-wielding ninja who has changed his look in nearly every Tekken.
quips.Goro: A four-armed Shokan prince and Mortal Kombat's very first boss.
quips.Dhalsim: A yoga master whose limbs stretch across the screen.

chapters.text: Name a Sonic the Hedgehog character

krillion.quip: An eerie Tails puppet from Sonic R that inspired a famous internet legend.

quips.Big the Cat: A gentle giant whose whole story in Sonic Adventure is fishing for his frog.
quips.Chip: Sonic's chocolate-loving amnesiac buddy who is secretly the god Light Gaia.
quips.Shadow: The 'Ultimate Life Form,' created by Gerald Robotnik aboard Space Colony ARK.

chapters.text: Name an item from The Legend of Zelda games

krillion.quip: A Majora's Mask item that makes nearby animals march behind Link like a parade.

quips.Deku Leaf: A giant leaf that lets Link glide and blow gusts in The Wind Waker.
quips.Majora's Mask: An ancient cursed mask that nearly drops the moon on Termina.
quips.Cane of Somaria: It conjures solid blocks out of thin air in A Link to the Past.

chapters.text: Name a card game

krillion.quip: A French card game where you race to drive 1,000 kilometres before anyone else.

deepcut: The Lord of the Rings: The Card Game

quips.Uno: Invented in 1971 by an Ohio barber after a family argument over Crazy Eights.
quips.Hanafuda: Japanese flower cards — and Nintendo's very first product back in 1889.
quips.Durak: Russia's favourite card game, where the last player holding cards is the 'fool'.

chapters.text: Name a named location on a Fortnite map

krillion.quip: A pizza-themed town with a giant tomato mascot that later became Tomato Temple.

quips.Tilted Towers: The busiest hot drop ever, wiped out by a meteor and rebuilt more than once.
quips.Loot Lake: Its island house famously bounced players around after Kevin the Cube melted in.
quips.Dusty Depot: A trio of warehouses flattened by a meteor into Dusty Divot.

chapters.text: Name a Roblox game

krillion.quip: A classic Roblox facility sim where players race to stop — or cause — a meltdown.

deepcut: Welcome to the Town of Robloxia

quips.Work at a Pizza Place: A 2008 classic where players take shifts cooking, delivering and running the till.
quips.Natural Disaster Survival: Survive meteors, tsunamis and tornadoes on a randomly picked map.
quips.Doors: A hotel full of monsters where every door you open could be your last.

chapters.text: Name a video game franchise

krillion.quip: Roll a sticky ball over everything until it's big enough to become a star.

quips.Tetris: Created in 1984 by a Soviet engineer on an Elektronika 60 computer.
quips.Pac-Man: Its shape was reportedly inspired by a pizza missing a slice.
quips.Halo: Originally pitched as a real-time strategy game for the Mac.

chapters.text: Name a Grand Theft Auto character

krillion.quip: A chatty music manager who pops up in both Vice City and San Andreas.

quips.Big Smoke: Famous for his gigantic fast-food order at Cluckin' Bell.
quips.Chop: Franklin's loyal Rottweiler, who you can train with a phone app in GTA V.
quips.Lazlow: A radio host who appears in almost every 3D-era GTA game.

chapters.text: Name a Dark Souls or Elden Ring boss

krillion.quip: A Shadow of the Erdtree boss that is, quite literally, a giant golden hippo.

schooler: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon
rare: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin

quips.Bed of Chaos: Dark Souls' most hated boss: a giant root-tree you beat by falling down holes.
quips.Ornstein and Smough: A spear-wielding dragonslayer and a hammer-swinging executioner fought together.
quips.Malenia, Blade of Miquella: Her line 'I am Malenia, Blade of Miquella' still haunts players.

chapters.text: Name a Call of Duty map

krillion.quip: An Infinite Warfare zombies map set in a 1970s New York kung-fu world.

quips.Shipment: A tiny square of shipping containers built for pure spawn-trap chaos.
quips.Nuketown: A 1950s-style nuclear test town with mannequins that keep coming back.
quips.Rust: A small oil-rig desert map made famous by 1v1 quickscope duels.

chapters.text: Name a fighter in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate

krillion.quip: A flat 2D fighter whose every move comes from 1980s Game & Watch handhelds.

quips.Piranha Plant: A surprise DLC fighter given free to early buyers of Ultimate.
quips.Sora: The final fighter added, completing a roster of 89 fighters.
quips.Steve: He can mine blocks and craft tools mid-fight, just like in Minecraft.

chapters.text: Name a Pokémon move

krillion.quip: A move that does nothing at all except let two Pokémon hold hands.

quips.Splash: Magikarp's famous move: it flops around and absolutely nothing happens.
quips.Sketch: Smeargle's signature move permanently copies the last move used against it.
quips.Celebrate: A move that literally just congratulates you — it has no battle effect.

chapters.text: Name a video game company or studio

krillion.quip: A tiny Japanese studio behind cult classics like Gunstar Heroes and Ikaruga.

quips.Nintendo: Founded in 1889 to make hanafuda playing cards, long before video games.
quips.Valve: The Half-Life studio that went on to build Steam.
quips.Mojang: Named after the Swedish word for 'gadget'.

packs.name: Comics & Anime
packs.tagline: 7 panels · capes, strips and Ghibli

chapters.text: Name a Studio Ghibli film (feature or short)

krillion.quip: Miyazaki's first CGI short, about a newborn caterpillar — screened only at the Ghibli Museum.

schooler: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind
The Tale of the Princess Kaguya
deepcut: The Day I Bought a Star
Mr. Dough and the Egg Princess

Ponyo: Ponyo on the Cliff by the Sea
Mei and the Kittenbus: Mei and the Baby Cat Bus

quips.Spirited Away: The first anime ever to win the Oscar for Best Animated Feature.
quips.The Boy and the Heron: Won the Best Animated Feature Oscar in 2024, two decades after Spirited Away.
quips.On Your Mark: A six-minute Miyazaki music video made for the J-pop duo Chage and Aska.

chapters.text: Name an anime series

krillion.quip: A ballet fairy tale where a duck becomes a girl who dances as a magical heroine.

rare: Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex
The Rising of the Shield Hero
Snow White with the Red Hair
Rascal Does Not Dream of Bunny Girl Senpai
That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime
The Disastrous Life of Saiki K.
A Place Further than the Universe
Is It Wrong to Pick Up Girls in a Dungeon?
deepcut: Dragon Quest: The Adventure of Dai

Re:Zero: Re:Zero - Starting Life in Another World
KonoSuba: Kono Subarashii Sekai ni Shukufuku wo
Anohana: Anohana: The Flower We Saw That Day

quips.Cowboy Bebop: A space-bounty-hunter jazz opera whose name comes from the bebop jazz style.
quips.Neon Genesis Evangelion: The 1995 mecha series that changed anime, with a famously strange finale.
quips.Mushishi: A slow, quiet series about a wanderer who studies strange life forms called mushi.

chapters.text: Name a manga series

krillion.quip: Makoto Yukimura's story of space-debris collectors, written before he made Vinland Saga.

rare: Nausicaa of the Valley of the Wind
That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime
deepcut: Dragon Quest: The Adventure of Dai

quips.Dr. Slump: Akira Toriyama's hit before Dragon Ball, starring a super-strong robot girl named Arale.
quips.Astro Boy: Osamu Tezuka's robot boy, a founding series of the modern manga and anime style.
quips.Doraemon: A robot cat from the future with a gadget pocket, one of Japan's best-loved characters.

chapters.text: Name a DC superhero

krillion.quip: A talking chimpanzee in a deerstalker hat who solves mysteries — a genuine DC hero.

quips.Krypto: Superman's dog, with the same Kryptonian powers as his owner.
quips.Mogo: A Green Lantern who is an entire living planet.
quips.Matter-Eater Lad: A Legion hero whose one power is eating absolutely anything.

chapters.text: Name a Marvel villain

krillion.quip: A Daredevil foe who commits his crimes on telescoping metal stilts.

quips.Galactus: A cosmic being who has to consume entire planets to survive.
quips.Taskmaster: Can copy any fighting move after seeing it once, thanks to photographic reflexes.
quips.MODOK: His name stands for Mental Organism Designed Only for Killing.

chapters.text: Name a Peanuts character

krillion.quip: An early Peanuts girl who famously said she hated Charlie Brown, back in the 1950s.

quips.Pig-Pen: Always trailed by a cloud of dust that he insists is 'the dust of ages'.
quips.Snoopy: Doubles as the World War I Flying Ace, Joe Cool, and a would-be novelist.
quips.Woodstock: A tiny yellow bird whose chirps are drawn as little tick marks, and Snoopy's best friend.

chapters.text: Name a newspaper comic strip

krillion.quip: A surreal strip starring a polka-dot-muumuu-wearing pinhead who speaks in non sequiturs.

Slylock Fox: Slylock Fox and Comics for Kids

quips.Peanuts: Charles Schulz drew all 17,897 strips himself over nearly fifty years.
quips.Calvin and Hobbes: Bill Watterson ended it in 1995 at its peak and refused to license any merchandise.
quips.Krazy Kat: George Herriman's 1913 strip about a cat in love with a brick-throwing mouse.

packs.name: Sports
packs.tagline: 21 games · run the gauntlet, court to podium

chapters.text: Name a sport that has featured at the Olympics

krillion.quip: An Olympic sport until 1920 — Britain's champions were a team of London police officers.

quips.Modern pentathlon: Coubertin designed it around a cavalry officer stranded behind enemy lines.
quips.Breaking: Debuted at Paris 2024 — and was promptly left off the LA 2028 programme.
quips.Cricket: Played once, in 1900: Great Britain beat France in the only Olympic match ever.
quips.Ski mountaineering: Skimo debuted at Milan–Cortina 2026: race uphill on skis, then rip back down.
quips.Rope climbing: A gymnastics event until 1932 — first up the rope, judged on speed and style.

chapters.text: Name a club that has played in the Premier League

krillion.quip: Swindon's one Premier League season, 1993–94, ended with 100 goals conceded.

quips.Oldham Athletic: A founder member of the Premier League in 1992 — relegated two seasons later.
quips.Wimbledon: The 'Crazy Gang' won the 1988 FA Cup, then the club moved to Milton Keynes.
quips.Blackpool: One thrilling 2010–11 season under Ian Holloway, then straight back down.

chapters.text: Name an NBA team, past or present

krillion.quip: Owned by its own players — Kentucky's 1948 Olympic gold-medal stars.

quips.Chicago Packers: The franchise that became the Wizards started life as the Packers in 1961.
quips.Seattle SuperSonics: Moved to Oklahoma City in 2008 — Seattle fans are still waiting.
quips.Toronto Huskies: Hosted the very first BAA game in 1946, which became NBA history's first.

chapters.text: Name a sport played with a ball

krillion.quip: Volleyball with feet and head only, played over a net with a woven rattan ball.

quips.Bossaball: Volleyball on an inflatable trampoline court, dreamed up in Spain in 2004.
quips.Calcio storico: Florentine football from the 1500s — half rugby, half brawl, still played every June.
quips.Kin-Ball: Three teams at once, one ball over 1.2 metres wide.
quips.Cuju: Ancient Chinese kickball — FIFA credits it as the earliest form of football.
quips.Eton wall game: Played along a brick wall at Eton since 1766 — most games end 0–0.

chapters.text: Name a martial art

krillion.quip: A Victorian gentleman's martial art — Sherlock Holmes uses it (as 'baritsu').

quips.Capoeira: Brazil's fight-dance hybrid is played in a circle to the twang of a berimbau.
quips.Lethwei: Burmese 'art of nine limbs' boxing — headbutts are perfectly legal.
quips.Bokator: Cambodia's ancient bokator joined UNESCO's heritage list in 2022.
quips.Kalaripayattu: From Kerala and often called one of the oldest fighting systems still practised.
quips.Glima: Icelandic wrestlers grip each other's belts and must stay upright the whole time.

chapters.text: Name a Formula 1 driver, past or present

krillion.quip: Still the only woman to score in F1 — half a point at the shortened 1975 Spanish GP.

quips.Maria Teresa de Filippis: The first woman to start a world championship Grand Prix, in 1958.
quips.Jim Clark: Won the 1965 Indy 500 and F1 title in the same year — a feat nobody has repeated.
quips.Jochen Rindt: Formula 1's only posthumous world champion, crowned in 1970.
quips.Kimi Antonelli: Mercedes promoted the Italian teenager straight into Hamilton's seat for 2025.

chapters.text: Name a famous boxer

krillion.quip: Became a world champion in 1976 aged just 17 — still the youngest ever.

quips.Daniel Mendoza: A Georgian-era champion who turned brawling into a science of footwork.
quips.Jack Broughton: Wrote boxing's first set of rules in 1743.
quips.Teófilo Stevenson: Won three Olympic golds and turned down millions to stay in Cuba.
quips.Buster Douglas: A 42-to-1 underdog when he knocked out Mike Tyson in Tokyo in 1990.

chapters.text: Name a tennis Grand Slam singles champion

krillion.quip: Ranked 212th when he won the 1976 Australian Open — he'd been working as a cleaner.

quips.Goran Ivanišević: Won Wimbledon 2001 as a wildcard ranked 125th in the world.
quips.René Lacoste: Nicknamed 'the Crocodile' — hence the logo on his shirts.
quips.Lottie Dod: Won Wimbledon in 1887 aged 15, and still holds the record as its youngest champion.
quips.Don Budge: Completed tennis's first calendar Grand Slam, in 1938.
quips.Maureen Connolly: 'Little Mo' won all four majors in 1953, the first woman to do so.

chapters.text: Name a famous footballer (soccer player)

krillion.quip: Scored 13 goals at the 1958 World Cup — a single-tournament record that still stands.

quips.Lev Yashin: The only goalkeeper ever to win the Ballon d'Or, in 1963.
quips.Garrincha: Born with a bent spine and legs of different lengths — and still a world champion twice.
quips.Roger Milla: Became the oldest World Cup goalscorer in 1994, aged 42.
quips.Pep Guardiola: Before the trophies as a manager, he anchored Cruyff's Barcelona midfield.

chapters.text: Name a winter sport (on snow or ice)

krillion.quip: Pirouettes and flips on skis to music — a demonstration event at two Winter Olympics.

quips.Bandy: Ice hockey's older cousin: a ball, curved sticks and a pitch the size of a football field.
quips.Elfstedentocht: A 200 km Dutch skating race held only when the canals freeze hard enough — last in 1997.
quips.Yukigassen: Competitive snowball fighting from Japan, with castles, flags and 90 pre-made snowballs.
quips.Cresta Run: St. Moritz's head-first ice chute, raced since 1885 — the ancestor of skeleton.

chapters.text: Name a yoga pose

krillion.quip: Named after the sage Ashtavakra, said to have been born with eight bends in his body.

quips.Corpse pose: The hardest pose to master, teachers say — lying perfectly still and letting go.
quips.Lion pose: Tongue out, eyes wide, roar — yes, it's a real pose.
quips.Firefly pose: An arm balance with both legs stretched forward, named after a tiny insect.
quips.Monkey pose: Named for Hanuman, the monkey god who leapt from India to Lanka in one bound.

chapters.text: Name a chess opening, defence or gambit

krillion.quip: Tartakower named 1.b4 after an orangutan he visited at New York's zoo in 1924.

quips.Bongcloud Attack: Walk your king out on move two — a meme that Carlsen and Nakamura once played for real.
quips.Fried Liver Attack: From the Italian 'fegatello' — the black king ends up cooked in the middle.
quips.Halloween Gambit: White simply gives up a knight on move four, just to scare Black.
quips.Ruy López: Named after a 16th-century Spanish priest who analysed it in 1561.

chapters.text: Name a golf term

krillion.quip: Four under par on one hole — a hole-in-one on a par 5, recorded only a handful of times.

quips.Albatross: Three under par on a hole — rarer than a hole in one.
quips.Mulligan: An unofficial do-over, possibly named after a 1920s Canadian golfer called David Mulligan.
quips.Snowman: Golf slang for an 8 on a hole, because of the shape of the number.
quips.Stymie: Before 1952 you couldn't lift a ball blocking your opponent's putt — you had to chip over it.
quips.Fore: Shouted to warn players ahead; probably short for 'before' or 'forecaddie'.

chapters.text: Name an athletics (track and field) event

krillion.quip: Ray Ewry, who had polio as a boy, won eight Olympic golds in the standing jumps.

quips.Steeplechase: Borrowed from horse racing, where riders once raced from church steeple to steeple.
quips.Marathon: The odd 42.195 km distance comes from the 1908 London Olympic course.
quips.Ekiden: Japan's beloved road relay, where runners pass a sash instead of a baton.
quips.Two-handed javelin: At the 1912 Olympics you threw with your right hand, then your left, and added them up.
quips.Club throw: A Paralympic throwing event using a wooden club shaped like a bowling pin.

chapters.text: Name a sports equipment or sportswear brand

krillion.quip: Gilbert has stitched rugby balls since 1823, right next door to Rugby School.

quips.Mikasa: The Japanese firm behind the official Olympic volleyball for decades.
quips.Lonsdale: Named after the Earl of Lonsdale, whose belts still crown British boxing champions.
quips.Hummel: The Danish brand's name is German for bumblebee — hence the logo.
quips.Asics: An acronym of the Latin 'anima sana in corpore sano' — a sound mind in a sound body.
quips.Puma: Founded by Rudolf Dassler after he fell out with his brother Adi, who started Adidas.

chapters.text: Name an extreme or adventure sport

krillion.quip: Ride a plank down Nicaragua's active Cerro Negro volcano, in a jumpsuit and goggles.

quips.Extreme ironing: Ironing a shirt on a cliff, a mountain or underwater — a real (if tongue-in-cheek) sport.
quips.Zorbing: Rolling downhill inside a giant inflatable ball, invented in New Zealand.
quips.Highlining: Slacklining between cliffs or towers, often hundreds of metres up.
quips.Coasteering: Born in Wales: scramble, swim and leap your way along a rocky coastline.

chapters.text: Name a cricket term

krillion.quip: Slang for a five-wicket haul: a 'fifer', as in Michelle Pfeiffer.

quips.Nelson: A score of 111 is 'Nelson' — and umpire David Shepherd famously hopped on one leg through it.
quips.Doosra: Hindi/Urdu for 'the other one' — the off-spinner's ball that turns the wrong way.
quips.Bodyline: England's 1932–33 tactic of bowling at the batter's body to stop Don Bradman.
quips.Jaffa: An unplayable delivery — named, some say, after the perfect Jaffa orange.
quips.Bunsen: Rhyming slang: a Bunsen burner is a turner, a pitch that spins.

chapters.text: Name a sports trophy, cup or award

krillion.quip: Made from the melted-down silver rupees of a disbanded Calcutta rugby club.

rare: Laureus World Sportsman of the Year
BBC Sports Personality of the Year
Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year Award
deepcut: PFA Players' Player of the Year

quips.Stanley Cup: Every member of the winning team gets a day with the Cup — it's been to a lot of parties.
quips.Jules Rimet Trophy: Stolen in England in 1966 and found under a hedge by a dog called Pickles.
quips.Floyd of Rosedale: A bronze pig — the trophy Iowa and Minnesota play for, born of a 1935 bet on a real hog.
quips.Wooden spoon: The 'prize' for finishing bottom — Cambridge once awarded a real one to its worst maths student.
quips.Green jacket: The Masters champion keeps it for a year, then it lives in the Augusta clubhouse.

chapters.text: Name a famous racehorse

krillion.quip: 100/1 winner of the 1967 Grand National after a pile-up — a fence is now named after him.

quips.Shergar: The Derby winner kidnapped from an Irish stud in 1983 and never seen again.
quips.Devon Loch: Mysteriously belly-flopped 50 yards from winning the 1956 Grand National for the Queen Mother.
quips.Kincsem: Hungary's wonder mare won all 54 of her races in the 1870s.
quips.Eclipse: 'Eclipse first, the rest nowhere' — unbeaten in 18 races in the 1760s and 70s.
quips.Phar Lap: Australia's 1930s champion; his huge heart is on display in Canberra.

chapters.text: Name a football (soccer) stadium

krillion.quip: Bolivia's national stadium sits about 3,600 m up in La Paz — visiting teams gasp for air.

quips.Estadio Centenario: Built for the first World Cup in 1930 and named for Uruguay's 100th birthday.
quips.Maracanã: Nearly 200,000 packed in for the 1950 World Cup decider — and watched Brazil lose.
quips.Hampden Park: Once the world's biggest stadium; the 1937 Scotland–England game drew 149,000.
quips.Highbury: Arsenal's old home is now flats — the marble halls and pitch became a garden square.

chapters.text: Name a city that has hosted the Summer or Winter Olympics

krillion.quip: At St. Louis 1904, the first marathon 'winner' had secretly hitched a ride in a car.

quips.Antwerp: 1920 saw the Olympic flag flown and the athletes' oath taken for the first time.
quips.Squaw Valley: Walt Disney staged the 1960 opening ceremony.
quips.Melbourne: Quarantine rules sent the 1956 equestrian events all the way to Stockholm.
quips.Cortina d'Ampezzo: Hosted in 1956, then again 70 years later as Milan's 2026 co-host.
quips.London: The only city to host three Summer Games — 1908, 1948 and 2012 — until Paris matched it in 2024.

packs.name: Geography
packs.tagline: 21 expeditions · around the world in seven answers

chapters.text: Name a landlocked country

krillion.quip: One of only two doubly landlocked countries, alongside Uzbekistan.

quips.Lesotho: Entirely surrounded by South Africa, and every inch of it sits above 1,000 m.
quips.Bolivia: Lost its coast in the War of the Pacific but still keeps a navy.
quips.Kazakhstan: The largest landlocked country on Earth.
quips.Uzbekistan: The other doubly landlocked country: every neighbour is landlocked too.

chapters.text: Name a country in Africa

krillion.quip: Africa's last absolute monarchy, renamed from Swaziland in 2018.

quips.Ethiopia: Runs on its own calendar, roughly seven to eight years behind everyone else's.
quips.Seychelles: Africa's smallest country by both area and population.

chapters.text: Name a US state

krillion.quip: The only US state whose name has just one syllable.

quips.Alaska: Has more coastline than all the other states put together.
quips.Hawaii: The only state made up entirely of islands.
quips.Rhode Island: The smallest state, which once had the longest official name.
quips.Wyoming: The least populous state in the union.

chapters.text: Name a European capital city

krillion.quip: Capital of Liechtenstein, a country without a single airport.

quips.Edinburgh: Scotland's capital, built around an extinct volcano.
quips.Reykjavík: The world's northernmost capital of a sovereign state.
quips.Vatican City: A capital city that is also an entire country.
quips.Tórshavn: Capital of the Faroe Islands, home to one of the oldest parliaments still meeting.

chapters.text: Name an island in the Mediterranean Sea

krillion.quip: An Italian island that sits closer to Tunisia than to Sicily.

quips.Sicily: The largest island in the Mediterranean.
quips.Stromboli: Has been erupting almost nonstop for over 2,000 years.
quips.Île d'If: Home of the island prison from The Count of Monte Cristo.
quips.Gozo: Malta's greener sister island, said to be Calypso's isle in the Odyssey.

chapters.text: Name a river in Europe

krillion.quip: Prague's river, which Smetana turned into a famous orchestral piece.

quips.Danube: Flows through ten countries, more than any other river on Earth.
quips.Volga: Europe's longest river, emptying into the Caspian Sea.
quips.Vjosa: Became Europe's first wild river national park in 2023.
quips.Tagus: The Iberian Peninsula's longest river, meeting the Atlantic at Lisbon.

chapters.text: Name a desert

krillion.quip: A genuine patch of shifting sand dunes in southern Poland.

quips.Atacama: The driest non-polar desert on Earth; some weather stations have never logged rain.
quips.Antarctic Desert: The largest desert in the world: deserts are about dryness, not heat.
quips.Namib: Often called the oldest desert on Earth, at 55 million years or more.
quips.Tabernas: Spain's desert, where dozens of spaghetti westerns were filmed.

chapters.text: Name a country with at least one star on its flag

krillion.quip: Its 12-pointed star sits just below a gold line for the equator, just like the island.

quips.Brazil: Its 27 stars show the sky over Rio on the morning the republic was declared.
quips.Malaysia: Its 14-pointed star and 14 stripes stand for the states plus the federal government.
quips.Bosnia and Herzegovina: Its stars are meant to run on forever, off the top and bottom edges.
quips.Croatia: Look closely: the crown on its coat of arms hides a gold star over a crescent.
quips.Moldova: There's a star tucked between the horns of the aurochs on its coat of arms.

chapters.text: Name a country beginning with S

krillion.quip: The equator runs straight through one of its tiny islets, Ilhéu das Rolas.

quips.Suriname: South America's smallest country, and the only one where Dutch is official.
quips.Scotland: A country within the UK, so it counts here, but it has no UN seat of its own.
quips.San Marino: Claims to be the world's oldest surviving republic, founded in 301 AD.
quips.Seychelles: Africa's smallest country by both area and population.

chapters.text: Name a volcano

krillion.quip: A volcano that burst out of a Mexican farmer's cornfield in 1943.

quips.Tambora: Its 1815 eruption gave the world 1816's 'Year Without a Summer'.
quips.Olympus Mons: It's on Mars, and it's the largest known volcano in the solar system.
quips.Mauna Kea: Taller than Everest if you measure from its base on the seafloor.

chapters.text: Name a jazz musician

chapters.text: Name a fruit

krillion.quip: Brazilian grape-like berry that sprouts straight out of the tree trunk.

quips.Durian: So pungent it's banned on Singapore's trains and in many hotels.
quips.Ugli fruit: Jamaican citrus hybrid sold proudly on the strength of being ugly.
quips.Miracle fruit: Makes sour things taste sweet for about an hour after you eat it.
quips.Buddha's hand: A citron split into finger-like segments — almost all peel, no pulp.
quips.Ackee: Jamaica's national fruit — toxic until ripe, then cooked with saltfish.

chapters.text: Name a cheese

krillion.quip: Orange French cheese whose pitted rind is nibbled by cheese mites on purpose.

quips.Casu marzu: Sardinian sheep's cheese ripened by live fly larvae — eaten while they wriggle.
quips.Pule: Serbian donkey-milk cheese, often called the priciest cheese on Earth.
quips.Stinking Bishop: Washed in perry — it's the cheese that revives Wallace in Curse of the Were-Rabbit.
quips.Gjetost: Norwegian 'brown cheese' made by boiling whey until it caramelises.
quips.Wensleydale: Wallace & Gromit's favourite — the film is credited with saving its creamery.

chapters.text: Name a pasta shape

krillion.quip: Means 'priest stranglers' — legend says greedy priests choked on it.

quips.Orzo: Looks exactly like rice — the name is Italian for barley.
quips.Gnocchi: Technically potato dumplings, but Italy files them under pasta.
quips.Su filindeu: Sardinian 'threads of God' — so tricky only a handful of people can make it.
quips.Ptitim: Invented in 1950s Israel as a rice substitute — it's toasted pasta, not couscous.
quips.Radiatori: Designed to look like old radiators — all ridges, perfect for trapping sauce.

chapters.text: Name a cocktail

krillion.quip: Gin, Lillet, Cointreau and lemon — a 1930s 'hair of the dog' cure.

quips.Monkey Gland: A 1920s gin cocktail named after a dubious goat-gland rejuvenation surgery.
quips.Death in the Afternoon: Absinthe topped with Champagne, invented and named by Ernest Hemingway.
quips.Zombie: Tiki pioneer Don the Beachcomber limited customers to two each.
quips.Ramos Gin Fizz: So much shaking that its New Orleans creator hired relays of 'shaker boys'.
quips.Kalimotxo: Basque party staple: cheap red wine mixed half-and-half with cola.

chapters.text: Name a fast food chain

krillion.quip: The world's biggest hot dog chain — and it doesn't sell schnitzel.

quips.White Castle: Founded in Wichita in 1921 — usually called the first fast food burger chain.
quips.Wimpy: Named after J. Wellington Wimpy, Popeye's burger-loving pal.
quips.Jollibee: Filipino chain famous for sweet spaghetti topped with hot dog slices.
quips.In-N-Out Burger: Prints tiny Bible verse references on the bottom of its cups and wrappers.

chapters.text: Name a vegetable

krillion.quip: Lime-green cauliflower cousin whose spiralling florets form a natural fractal.

quips.Samphire: Salty, crunchy coastal plant nicknamed 'sea asparagus'.
quips.Kohlrabi: Its name is German for 'cabbage turnip' — and it tastes like both.
quips.Salsify: A root nicknamed 'oyster plant' for its faintly oyster-like flavour.
quips.Celtuce: Grown for its thick, crisp stem rather than its leaves.
quips.Kalettes: A modern cross of kale and Brussels sprouts — little frilly sprouts.

chapters.text: Name a herb or spice

krillion.quip: Peppery West African seed once sold in Europe as a pricey pepper stand-in.

quips.Saffron: Each crocus flower gives just three stigmas — hence the eye-watering price.
quips.Asafoetida: Smells like rotten garlic raw, then melts into savoury magic in hot oil.
quips.Mastic: Resin from a Greek island shrub, chewed as gum since ancient times.
quips.Tonka bean: Vanilla-almond seed loved by pastry chefs — and banned as a food in the US.
quips.Sumac: Crimson berries ground into a lemony powder, used before lemons reached the Levant.

chapters.text: Name a dessert

krillion.quip: Breton pastry whose name simply means 'butter cake' — and it's mostly butter.

quips.Pavlova: Australia and New Zealand still squabble over who invented it.
quips.Eton mess: Legend says it began with a pavlova dropped at an Eton cricket match.
quips.Spotted dick: The 'spots' are just currants dotted through a suet sponge.
quips.Croquembouche: Its name means 'crunch in the mouth' — a tower of caramel-glued choux buns.
quips.Baked Alaska: The ice cream survives the oven because meringue's trapped air insulates it.

quips.Injera: Spongy Ethiopian teff flatbread that doubles as your plate and cutlery.

quips.Pão de queijo: Brazilian cheese puffs made with cassava starch, so naturally gluten-free.
quips.Matnakash: Armenian loaf whose name means 'finger-pulled', after its grooved top.

quips.Ulu: Inuit crescent knife used for everything from skinning fish to chopping food.

quips.Crayola: Crayola's name blends craie, French for chalk, with 'oily'.

chapters.text: Name a sneaker or shoe brand

krillion.quip: Veja makes sneakers using wild Amazonian rubber and organic cotton.

quips.Puma: Puma and Adidas were founded by feuding brothers Rudolf and Adi Dassler in the same German town.
quips.Crocs: Crocs debuted in 2002 at a Florida boat show as a boating shoe.
quips.Converse: The Chuck Taylor All Star launched in 1917 and later took a basketball player's name.

chapters.text: Name a shampoo, soap or toiletry brand

krillion.quip: Pears' amber transparent soap traces back to Andrew Pears's London shop of 1789.

quips.Colgate: Colgate was selling starch, soap and candles in New York as far back as 1806.
quips.Vaseline: Vaseline began when Robert Chesebrough saw oil workers rubbing rod wax on their cuts.
quips.Head & Shoulders: Head & Shoulders was one of the first mass-market anti-dandruff shampoos, launched in 1961.

packs.name: Animals & Nature
packs.tagline: 21 sightings · a field guide to the weird

chapters.text: Name a dog breed

krillion.quip: Italy's truffle-hunting specialist, with a curly coat that barely sheds.

quips.Basenji: Africa's 'barkless' dog yodels instead of barking.
quips.Norwegian Lundehund: Has six toes on each foot, built for scrambling up cliffs after puffins.
quips.Xoloitzcuintli: An ancient hairless breed linked to the Aztec god Xolotl.

chapters.text: Name a bird

krillion.quip: Its chicks have claws on their wings, and the adults smell like manure.

quips.Kakapo: A flightless, night-roaming parrot from New Zealand, and the heaviest parrot alive.
quips.Shoebill: Stands statue-still for hours, then lunges at lungfish with its clog-shaped bill.
quips.Oilbird: Navigates pitch-black caves using echolocation clicks, like a bat.

chapters.text: Name a type of tree

krillion.quip: Known only from fossils until a ranger found living ones in 1994.

quips.Baobab: Can store thousands of litres of water in its swollen trunk.
quips.Ginkgo: A living fossil whose lineage predates the dinosaurs.
quips.Bristlecone pine: Some are nearly 5,000 years old, among the oldest living things on Earth.

chapters.text: Name a type of lizard

krillion.quip: Bites its own tail and curls into an armoured ball when threatened.

quips.Horned lizard: Can squirt blood from its eyes to startle predators.
quips.Basilisk: Sprints across water on its hind legs, hence the 'Jesus Christ lizard' nickname.
quips.Sandfish: A desert skink that 'swims' through loose sand.

chapters.text: Name a flower

krillion.quip: Blooms only every few years, and smells of rotting meat to lure beetles.

quips.Rafflesia: The world's biggest single flower, up to a metre across, and it smells like carrion.
quips.Ghost orchid: A leafless orchid that seems to float in Florida's swamps.
quips.Moonflower: Opens at dusk and closes by morning, pollinated by night-flying moths.

chapters.text: Name a gemstone

krillion.quip: California's state gem glows bright blue under ultraviolet light.

quips.Painite: Once ranked the rarest mineral on Earth, with only a handful of crystals known.
quips.Alexandrite: Looks green in daylight and turns red under lamplight.
quips.Moldavite: Green glass forged when a meteorite hit Germany about 15 million years ago.
quips.Ammolite: Cut from the shimmering shells of fossil ammonites.

chapters.text: Name a type of shark

krillion.quip: May live around 400 years, the longest-lived vertebrate known.

quips.Goblin shark: Its jaws shoot forward like a slingshot to snatch prey.
quips.Cookiecutter shark: Bites neat round plugs out of whales, dolphins and even submarine sonar domes.
quips.Epaulette shark: Can 'walk' across reefs on its fins and cope with very little oxygen.

chapters.text: Name a cat breed

krillion.quip: Nicknamed the werewolf cat for its patchy, wolfish coat, a natural mutation.

quips.Turkish Van: Nicknamed the swimming cat for its unusual love of water.
quips.Singapura: One of the smallest cat breeds, often weighing under 3 kg.
quips.Peterbald: A Russian breed that can be born bald, velvety or with a brush-like coat.

chapters.text: Name an insect

krillion.quip: Defends itself by blasting a boiling-hot chemical spray from its rear.

quips.Bullet ant: Its sting is often rated the most painful of any insect.
quips.Periodical cicada: Spends 13 or 17 years underground, then emerges in its millions all at once.
quips.Atlas moth: One of the largest moths, and the adults have no working mouth.

chapters.text: Name a type of snake

krillion.quip: Flattens its body into a ribbon to glide between treetops.

quips.Titanoboa: An extinct giant around 13 metres long, about the length of a bus.
quips.Inland taipan: The most venomous land snake known, yet it's shy and rarely bites.
quips.Tentacled snake: Uses two little face tentacles to sense fish in murky water.

chapters.text: Name a weather phenomenon

krillion.quip: A tube-shaped cloud up to 1,000 km long that rolls over northern Australia.

quips.Ball lightning: Glowing orbs that drift through the air for seconds, still not fully explained.
quips.Snow roller: Wind rolls snow into hollow logs, like nature's own snowman starters.
quips.Thundersnow: A thunderstorm that drops snow instead of rain.

chapters.text: Name a mushroom or other fungus

krillion.quip: One in Oregon spreads across nearly 10 square km, among Earth's biggest organisms.

quips.Ghost fungus: Glows a soft green in the dark in Australian forests.
quips.Zombie-ant fungus: Hijacks an ant, steers it up a plant, then sprouts out of its head.
quips.Penicillium: The mould that gave us penicillin, the first widely used antibiotic.

chapters.text: Name a horse breed

krillion.quip: Its coat can have a natural metallic sheen that makes it look golden.

quips.Falabella: One of the smallest horse breeds, often under 80 cm at the shoulder.
quips.Icelandic horse: Has an extra smooth gait called the tölt, so riders barely bounce.
quips.Knabstrupper: A Danish breed famous for its leopard-spotted coat.

chapters.text: Name an animal native to Australia

krillion.quip: A striped termite-eater that can slurp up around 20,000 termites a day.

quips.Platypus: Lays eggs, has venomous ankle spurs and senses electricity with its bill.
quips.Lord Howe Island stick insect: Thought extinct for 80 years until found clinging to a lone sea stack.

chapters.text: Name an animal with stripes

krillion.quip: Looks half zebra, but it's actually the giraffe's only living relative.

quips.Aardwolf: A striped hyena relative that eats almost nothing but termites.
quips.Quagga: A half-striped zebra that went extinct in the 1880s.
quips.Thylacine: The striped 'Tasmanian tiger' was actually a carnivorous marsupial.

chapters.text: Name a whale, dolphin or porpoise

krillion.quip: The rarest marine mammal on Earth, with only about ten left in Mexico.

quips.Bowhead whale: Can live over 200 years, longer than any other known mammal.
quips.Narwhal: Its 'tusk' is really a long spiral tooth packed with nerve endings.
quips.Baiji: China's Yangtze river dolphin, declared likely extinct in 2006.

chapters.text: Name a primate

krillion.quip: Taps on wood, listens for grubs, then hooks them out with one skinny finger.

quips.Human: Yes, you count: humans are great apes, alongside chimps and gorillas.
quips.Slow loris: One of the few venomous primates, with a toxin gland on its elbow.
quips.Pygmy marmoset: The smallest monkey on Earth, light enough to perch on a finger.

chapters.text: Name a type of rock

krillion.quip: Lava from Earth's youth that erupted near 1,600°C, far hotter than any today.

quips.Pumice: So full of gas bubbles that it can float on water.
quips.Kimberlite: The volcanic rock that carries diamonds up from deep in the mantle.
quips.Chalk: Built from the tiny shells of countless ancient marine plankton.

chapters.text: Name a freshwater fish

krillion.quip: Gulps air at the surface and can grow to around 3 metres long.

quips.Electric eel: Not a true eel but a knifefish that can zap around 600 volts.
quips.Mekong giant catfish: One of the biggest freshwater fish, sometimes topping 250 kg.
quips.Bichir: An ancient fish with lungs that can wriggle across land on its fins.

chapters.text: Name an amphibian

krillion.quip: A blind cave salamander that can go up to a decade without eating.

quips.Glass frog: Its belly skin is see-through, so you can watch its heart beating.
quips.Darwin's frog: Dads raise tadpoles in their vocal sacs, then cough up tiny froglets.
quips.Hairy frog: Breaks its own toe bones to make claws when threatened.

chapters.text: Name a crustacean

krillion.quip: Discovered in 2005, it grows bacteria on its hairy arms near deep-sea vents.

quips.Coconut crab: The largest land invertebrate, strong enough to crack open coconuts.
quips.Mantis shrimp: Punches so fast it makes bubbles that collapse with a tiny flash of light.
quips.Tongue-eating louse: Replaces a fish's tongue and then lives on in its mouth.
quips.Japanese spider crab: Its legs can span nearly 4 metres from claw to claw.

packs.name: Science & Space
packs.tagline: 21 experiments · from atoms to galaxies

chapters.text: Name a chemical element

krillion.quip: The first element ever made artificially; its name is Greek for 'artificial'.

quips.Hafnium: Named after Copenhagen, whose old Latin name is Hafnia.
quips.Gallium: Melts in your hand: it turns liquid at about 30 °C.
quips.Oganesson: The heaviest element known, and only a handful of atoms have ever existed.

chapters.text: Name a bone in the human body

krillion.quip: A tiny wrist bone whose name literally means 'pea-shaped'.

quips.Hyoid: The only bone in your body not attached to any other bone.
quips.Stapes: The smallest bone in the body, shaped like a stirrup in your ear.
quips.Fabella: A little sesamoid bone behind the knee that only some people have.

chapters.text: Name a planet, dwarf planet or moon in our solar system

krillion.quip: A tiny Neptune moon found in old Hubble photos, named for a mythical sea-horse.

quips.Enceladus: Saturn's icy moon sprays water geysers into space from a hidden ocean.
quips.Titan: The only moon with a thick atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane.
quips.Dactyl: The first moon ever found orbiting an asteroid, spotted by Galileo in 1993.

chapters.text: Name one of the 88 official constellations

krillion.quip: The giraffe: Greeks described it as a camel with leopard spots.

quips.Ophiuchus: The serpent bearer: the Sun passes through it, yet it never made the zodiac.
quips.Mensa: The table mountain, named after Table Mountain above Cape Town.
quips.Coma Berenices: Named after a real Egyptian queen's hair, offered to the gods.

chapters.text: Name an organ of the human body

krillion.quip: The fold holding your gut in place was only reclassified as an organ in 2016.

quips.Skin: Your biggest organ, weighing roughly as much as a bowling ball.
quips.Liver: The only internal organ that can regrow from just a quarter of itself.
quips.Appendix: Once called useless, it may store good gut bacteria for emergencies.

chapters.text: Name a famous scientist

krillion.quip: Her pulsing-star rule gave astronomers their first ruler for measuring galaxies.

quips.Rosalind Franklin: Her X-ray Photo 51 revealed DNA's double helix shape.
quips.Mary Anning: A self-taught fossil hunter who found the first full ichthyosaur at about 12.
quips.Hypatia: A mathematician and astronomer who taught in Alexandria around 400 AD.

chapters.text: Name a dinosaur

krillion.quip: An armoured ankylosaur named after the demon dog in Ghostbusters.

quips.Brontosaurus: Sunk as a mistake for a century, it was revived as a real genus in 2015.
quips.Yi: The shortest dinosaur name ever: a small bat-winged climber from China.
quips.Argentinosaurus: Possibly the heaviest land animal ever, at around 70 tonnes.

chapters.text: Name a unit of measurement

krillion.quip: MIT students measured a bridge using fellow student Oliver Smoot's body length.

quips.Barn: A tiny area used in nuclear physics; physicists joked a nucleus was as big as a barn.
quips.Shake: Ten nanoseconds, named after a 'shake of a lamb's tail'.
quips.Sverdrup: Measures ocean currents: one sverdrup is a million cubic metres of water per second.

chapters.text: Name a programming language

krillion.quip: Its programs are abstract pixel paintings, named after the artist Piet Mondrian.

quips.Malbolge: Designed to be nearly impossible to program; its first 'Hello World' took two years.
quips.Plankalkül: Designed by Konrad Zuse in the 1940s, arguably the first high-level language.
quips.Whitespace: Only spaces, tabs and line breaks count; every other character is ignored.

chapters.text: Name a disease caused by a virus

krillion.quip: Studying this plant blight in the 1890s led scientists to discover viruses.

quips.Smallpox: The only human disease ever fully wiped out, declared eradicated in 1980.
quips.Rinderpest: A cattle plague that became only the second disease ever eradicated, in 2011.
quips.Myxomatosis: Deliberately released in Australia in 1950 to control rabbit numbers.

chapters.text: Name a type of cloud

krillion.quip: Added to the cloud atlas in 2017 after amateur sky-watchers campaigned for it.

quips.Morning Glory: A huge rolling tube cloud that sweeps over northern Australia each spring.
quips.Noctilucent: The highest clouds on Earth, glowing at night about 80 km up.
quips.Virga: Rain that evaporates before it reaches the ground, like wispy streaks.

chapters.text: Name a branch of science ending in -ology

krillion.quip: The scientific study of clouds, from the Greek 'nephos', meaning cloud.

quips.Oology: The study of birds' eggs, once a hugely popular Victorian hobby.
quips.Areology: Geology, but for Mars: named after Ares, the Greek god of war.
quips.Dendrochronology: Dating events by counting and comparing tree rings.

chapters.text: Name a phobia

krillion.quip: The fear of peanut butter sticking to the roof of your mouth.

Nomophobia: Fear of being without a phone
Arachibutyrophobia: Fear of peanut butter sticking to the roof of your mouth
Domatophobia: Fear of being in a house
Pteronophobia: Fear of being tickled by feathers

quips.Hippopotomonstrosesquippedaliophobia: The fear of long words, cruelly given one of the longest names possible.
quips.Nomophobia: Fear of being without your phone, short for 'no-mobile-phone phobia'.

chapters.text: Name a famous space mission or spacecraft

krillion.quip: Lost in 1999 because one team used pound-force and the other used newtons.

quips.Voyager 1: The farthest human-made object, now cruising through interstellar space.
quips.Ingenuity: The first aircraft to make a powered, controlled flight on another planet.
quips.Luna 9: The first spacecraft to soft-land on the Moon, in 1966.

chapters.text: Name a tech company

krillion.quip: A real London phone maker founded by Carl Pei, so 'Nothing' scores here.

quips.Fairchild Semiconductor: Its founders spun off so many startups they became known as the 'Fairchildren'.
quips.Nokia: Started in 1865 as a paper mill in Finland before it ever made phones.
quips.Nintendo: Founded in 1889 to make hand-made playing cards.

chapters.text: Name an invention of the 20th century

krillion.quip: Percy Shaw got the idea for reflective road studs from a cat's glowing eyes.

quips.Velcro: Inspired by burrs that clung to George de Mestral's dog after a walk in the Alps.
quips.Microwave oven: Discovered when radar engineer Percy Spencer noticed a chocolate bar melting in his pocket.
quips.Bubble wrap: Originally sold as textured wallpaper, which flopped.

chapters.text: Name a muscle in the human body

krillion.quip: Your smallest skeletal muscle, steadying the tiniest bone deep in your ear.

quips.Sartorius: The longest muscle in the body, named after tailors who sat cross-legged.
quips.Palmaris longus: Missing from one or both arms in about one person in seven.
quips.Masseter: Pound for pound, one of the strongest muscles you have: it powers your bite.

chapters.text: Name a mineral (the geology kind)

krillion.quip: Found in Serbia in 2006 with almost the exact formula of Superman's kryptonite.

quips.Bridgmanite: Earth's most abundant mineral, hidden in the deep mantle and only named in 2014.
quips.Ice: Yes, ice counts: it is naturally occurring, crystalline and inorganic.
quips.Painite: Once the rarest gem on Earth, with fewer than two dozen crystals known in the 2000s.

chapters.text: Name a geometric shape (2D or 3D)

krillion.quip: A convex 3D shape with one stable resting point; it always rolls itself upright.

quips.Reuleaux triangle: A curved triangle of constant width; it can drill nearly square holes.
quips.Apeirogon: A polygon with infinitely many sides.
quips.Szilassi polyhedron: Seven faces, and every single face touches every other one.

chapters.text: Name a star other than the Sun

krillion.quip: Spotted in 2022 about 12.9 billion years back in time: the most distant single star seen.

quips.Polaris: Not the brightest star, but it sits almost exactly above Earth's North Pole.
quips.Keid: The real star Star Trek picked for Spock's home planet, Vulcan.
quips.Algol: The 'Demon Star' visibly dims every three days as its partner star eclipses it.

chapters.text: Name a piece of science lab equipment

krillion.quip: A three-bulb glass gadget that makes gas on demand and stops when you shut the tap.

quips.Bunsen burner: Popularised by Robert Bunsen in 1855, though his technician did much of the design.
quips.Petri dish: Named after Julius Petri, an assistant to germ pioneer Robert Koch.
quips.Leyden jar: One of the first devices to store electricity, invented in the 1740s.

packs.name: Body & Health
packs.tagline: 21 check-ups · the doctor will see you now

chapters.text: Name a part of the face

krillion.quip: The groove above your upper lip — its name comes from the Greek for 'love charm'.

quips.Glabella: The smooth patch between your eyebrows — doctors tap it to test a reflex.
quips.Cupid's bow: The double curve of your upper lip, named after the archer god's weapon.
quips.Buccinator: The cheek muscle trumpeters rely on — its name comes from the Latin for trumpeter.

chapters.text: Name a type of doctor or medical specialty

krillion.quip: A rehab-medicine doctor — not a psychiatrist, and definitely not a podiatrist.

quips.Veterinarian: Vets train on many species — a GP for humans only has to learn one.
quips.Optometrist: An eye-exam specialist; ophthalmologists are the ones who do eye surgery.
quips.Podiatrist: A foot specialist — the name comes from the Greek for 'foot' and 'healer'.

chapters.text: Name a vitamin or dietary mineral

krillion.quip: You need only a pinch, but it powers enzymes that break down sulfites.

quips.Vitamin C: Humans are among the few mammals that can't make their own vitamin C.
quips.Vitamin D: Your skin makes it from sunlight, which is why it's nicknamed the sunshine vitamin.
quips.Cobalt: It sits at the heart of the vitamin B12 molecule — the only vitamin with a metal core.

chapters.text: Name a gym or bodyweight exercise

krillion.quip: Bruce Lee's signature core move — your whole body levers up off a bench like a flag.

quips.Burpee: Named after physiologist Royal Burpee, who invented it in the 1930s as a fitness test.
quips.Jumping jack: Legend credits US Army general John 'Black Jack' Pershing with popularising it.
quips.Planche: A gymnast's hold where your whole body hovers flat, balanced only on your hands.

chapters.text: Name something you'd find in a first-aid kit

krillion.quip: A tiny hooked tool that twists ticks out cleanly — a staple of hikers' kits.

quips.Plaster: The Band-Aid was invented in 1920 by a Johnson & Johnson employee for his accident-prone wife.
quips.Triangular bandage: One cloth, a dozen uses: sling, pad, tie or even a makeshift tourniquet.

chapters.text: Name a part of the human eye

krillion.quip: The pink fold in your eye's inner corner — a leftover of a third eyelid.

quips.Cornea: It has no blood vessels at all — it takes its oxygen straight from the air.
quips.Optic disc: No photoreceptors sit here, so your brain quietly paints over the blind spot.
quips.Dua's layer: A thin layer of the cornea first described only in 2013.

chapters.text: Name a sleep disorder or something that can happen in your sleep

krillion.quip: Sleep groaning: long, eerie moans on each out-breath that the sleeper never hears.

quips.Narcolepsy: Some people with it collapse when they laugh, as strong emotions switch their muscles off.
quips.Exploding head syndrome: A harmless but startling 'bang' heard as you drift off — no headache involved.
quips.Hypnic jerk: That falling-feeling twitch as you drop off — most people get one now and then.

chapters.text: Name a hormone in the human body

krillion.quip: Named after Hershey's Kisses — it was discovered in Hershey, Pennsylvania.

quips.Oxytocin: Nicknamed the 'cuddle hormone' — it's released during hugs and childbirth.
quips.Ghrelin: Your 'hunger hormone': levels climb before meals and fall once you've eaten.
quips.Melatonin: Your body releases it as darkness falls, nudging you toward sleep.
quips.Irisin: Released by exercising muscle, it's named after Iris, the Greek messenger goddess.

chapters.text: Name a part of the brain

krillion.quip: Latin for 'tree of life' — the branching white matter inside your cerebellum.

deepcut: Bed nucleus of the stria terminalis

quips.Hippocampus: Named after the seahorse, which early anatomists thought it resembled.
quips.Amygdala: From the Greek for 'almond' — it's an almond-shaped hub for fear and emotion.
quips.Claustrum: A thin sheet of neurons that Francis Crick suspected might help bind consciousness.
quips.Pineal gland: Descartes called it the seat of the soul; it actually makes melatonin.

chapters.text: Name a joint in the human body (or a type of joint)

krillion.quip: The peg-in-socket joint that anchors each of your teeth in the jaw.

quips.Saddle joint: Your thumb's base sits in a saddle joint — the secret behind gripping with opposable thumbs.
quips.Pubic symphysis: It loosens during pregnancy, helped along by the hormone relaxin.
quips.Suture: Skull bones meet at wiggly suture joints that fuse slowly as you age.

chapters.text: Name a piece of medical equipment or a medical instrument

krillion.quip: A trumpet-shaped tube midwives press to the bump to hear a baby's heartbeat.

quips.Stethoscope: Invented in 1816 by René Laennec, whose first version was a rolled-up tube of paper.
quips.Iron lung: A whole-body breathing chamber that saved thousands during the polio epidemics.
quips.Defibrillator: It doesn't restart a stopped heart — it resets one that's quivering out of rhythm.

chapters.text: Name a sports injury

krillion.quip: A sudden calf-muscle tear named after the sport where lunging so often causes it.

quips.Tennis elbow: Most people who get tennis elbow have never picked up a racket.
quips.Cauliflower ear: Blood pools under the ear's skin after repeated blows and hardens into bumps.
quips.Turf toe: A big-toe sprain that became common once American football moved onto artificial turf.

chapters.text: Name a part of the ear

krillion.quip: A small bump on some people's ear rim that Darwin wrote about as an evolutionary leftover.

quips.Stapes: The smallest bone in your body — about the size of a grain of rice.
quips.Otoliths: Tiny calcium crystals in your inner ear that tell your brain which way is down.
quips.Tragus: The little flap in front of your ear canal — press it to muffle sound.

chapters.text: Name a nerve in the human body

krillion.quip: A tiny vagus branch nicknamed 'criminal' for letting ulcers return after surgery.

deepcut: Medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm
Lateral cutaneous nerve of the forearm
Medial cutaneous nerve of the arm
Dorsal cutaneous branch of the ulnar nerve

Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve: Lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh
Posterior femoral cutaneous nerve: Posterior cutaneous nerve of the thigh
Arnold's nerve: Auricular branch of the vagus nerve
Superficial radial nerve: Superficial branch of the radial nerve

quips.Ulnar nerve: Hitting your 'funny bone' is really whacking this exposed nerve at the elbow.
quips.Vagus nerve: Its name means 'wandering' — it meanders from your brainstem all the way to your gut.
quips.Sciatic nerve: The longest and widest nerve in your body — about as thick as your thumb at its widest.
quips.Terminal nerve: Sometimes called 'cranial nerve zero', it was discovered after the other twelve were numbered.

chapters.text: Name a gland in the human body

krillion.quip: Tiny glands at the back of your tongue that rinse your taste buds clean between bites.

quips.Liver: The body's largest gland as well as its largest internal organ.
quips.Pineal gland: It's shaped like a tiny pine cone, which is how it got its name.
quips.Thymus: It trains your T cells, then slowly shrinks and turns to fat after puberty.

chapters.text: Name a type of cell in the human body

krillion.quip: Brain cells that fire when you're in one particular spot — your built-in GPS.

quips.Red blood cell: They ditch their nucleus as they mature, leaving more room for oxygen-carrying haemoglobin.
quips.Egg cell: The largest cell in the human body — just about visible to the naked eye.
quips.Osteoclast: A bone-dissolving cell that constantly remodels your skeleton.
quips.Grid cell: Neurons that fire in a hexagonal grid pattern as you move around — Nobel-winning stuff.

chapters.text: Name a reflex or involuntary body action

krillion.quip: Poking inside your ear makes some people cough, thanks to a branch of the vagus nerve.

quips.Yawn: Yawning is contagious — even reading about it can set you off.
quips.Photic sneeze reflex: Bright light makes roughly one in four people sneeze — it's nicknamed ACHOO syndrome.
quips.Diving reflex: Cold water on your face slows your heart — a built-in trick for holding your breath.

chapters.text: Name a part of the hand or foot

krillion.quip: The hollow at the base of your thumb, named for where people once rested a pinch of snuff.

deepcut: Ulnar collateral ligament of the thumb

quips.Lunula: The pale half-moon at the base of your nail — its name is Latin for 'little moon'.
quips.Fingerprint: Even identical twins have different fingerprints.
quips.Pisiform: The pea-shaped wrist bone sits inside a tendon, just as your kneecap does.

chapters.text: Name a medical test or scan

krillion.quip: A paper strip hooked under your lower eyelid measures how many tears you make.

quips.X-ray: Wilhelm Röntgen's first X-ray photo showed his wife's hand — wedding ring and all.
quips.Heel prick test: A few drops from a newborn's heel can screen for several rare but treatable conditions.
quips.Pap smear: Named after Georgios Papanikolaou, the Greek doctor who developed it.

chapters.text: Name a medicine (generic or brand name)

krillion.quip: A heart drug made from foxglove, a plant whose heart effects were described back in 1785.

quips.Penicillin: Alexander Fleming spotted it in 1928 when mould spoiled one of his bacteria dishes.
quips.Aspirin: Its ancestor, salicin, comes from willow bark — used for pain since ancient times.
quips.Quinine: Extracted from cinchona bark, it's what gives tonic water its bitter bite.

chapters.text: Name an artery or vein in the human body

krillion.quip: A deep brain vein named after Galen, the Roman-era Greek doctor who dissected apes.

quips.Aorta: Your body's biggest artery — at its start it's about as wide as a garden hose.
quips.Great saphenous vein: The longest vein in your body, running from the top of your foot to your groin.
quips.Pulmonary artery: Unlike most arteries, they carry oxygen-poor blood — from the heart to the lungs.

packs.name: History & Myth
packs.tagline: 21 relics · dust off the old stories

chapters.text: Name a US president

krillion.quip: The first president born a US citizen — and he grew up speaking Dutch.

quips.William Henry Harrison: He served just 31 days — the shortest presidency ever.
quips.Grover Cleveland: For over a century the only president with two non-consecutive terms.

chapters.text: Name a Greek god or goddess

krillion.quip: Primordial goddess of night — Homer says even Zeus feared to anger her.

quips.Hecate: Goddess of crossroads and witchcraft, often shown with three faces.
quips.Nike: Goddess of victory — the sportswear brand borrowed her name.
quips.Momus: God of mockery, so critical the gods threw him out of Olympus.

chapters.text: Name a famous painter

quips.The Grinch: Seuss said he spotted a very Grinchish face in his mirror the morning after Christmas.

krillion.quip: Barnaby Rudge's locksmith's daughter whose name became a style of dress and hat.

deepcut: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come

Nicholas Nickleby: The Life and Adventures of Nicholas Nickleby
The Pickwick Papers: The Posthumous Papers of the Pickwick Club
Dombey and Son: Dealings with the Firm of Dombey and Son
Martin Chuzzlewit: The Life and Adventures of Martin Chuzzlewit

quips.A Christmas Carol: Dickens wrote it in about six weeks in 1843, partly to ease his money worries.
quips.Uriah Heep: He keeps insisting he's 'umble' — Dickens's shorthand for a thoroughly slimy hypocrite.

chapters.text: Name an Agatha Christie novel, play or story collection

krillion.quip: A late spy thriller published for Christie's 80th birthday, with no Poirot or Marple.

tooclever: The Mirror Crack'd from Side to Side

The Mystery of the Spanish Chest

quips.The Mousetrap: The longest continuously running play in history, in London since 1952.
quips.And Then There Were None: Christie's biggest seller — the best-selling mystery novel of all time.
quips.Curtain: Written in the 1940s, then kept in a bank vault for about thirty years before publication.

krillion.quip: T. S. Eliot's feline criminal mastermind, later a showstopper in the musical Cats.

quips.Ozymandias: Shelley wrote it in a friendly sonnet contest with Horace Smith, who wrote his own version.
quips.Jabberwocky: Most of it is made-up words, yet 'chortle' and 'galumph' really entered English.
quips.The Raven: Poe said he chose the refrain 'Nevermore' for its sound, then built the poem around it.

chapters.text: Name a Beatrix Potter book or character

krillion.quip: A newt in a waistcoat from Jeremy Fisher, and Potter's pun on the famous scientist.

schooler: The Tale of Two Bad Mice
The Tale of Mr. Jeremy Fisher
The Tale of the Flopsy Bunnies
The Tale of Ginger and Pickles
rare: The Story of a Fierce Bad Rabbit
The Tale of Little Pig Robinson
deepcut: The Tale of the Faithful Dove

The Tale of Samuel Whiskers: The Tale of Samuel Whiskers or The Roly-Poly Pudding

quips.The Tale of Peter Rabbit: Potter first told it in a picture letter to a sick child, then printed it herself in 1901.
quips.Jemima Puddle-Duck: A fox charms her into a nest; collie Kep and two foxhounds come to the rescue.
quips.Mr. McGregor: The grumpy gardener whose vegetable patch Peter Rabbit just can't resist.

chapters.text: Name a Mr. Men or Little Miss character

krillion.quip: Does everything back to front, one of Roger Hargreaves' original Mr. Men.

quips.Mr. Tickle: Roger Hargreaves invented the Mr. Men after his son Adam asked what a tickle looks like.

chapters.text: Name a character from a Jane Austen novel

krillion.quip: Persuasion's poetry-loving, grieving sailor who ends up marrying Louisa Musgrove.

quips.Mr. Darcy: The famous lake scene from the 1995 TV serial isn't in Austen's novel at all.
quips.Mr. Collins: Heir to Longbourn through the entail, which is exactly why Mrs. Bennet panics.

chapters.text: Name a Stephen King book or story

krillion.quip: A deliberately unsolved mystery, published in 2005 as a Hard Case Crime paperback.

rare: The Girl Who Loved Tom Gordon
deepcut: The Man in the Black Suit
The Ballad of the Flexible Bullet

Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption: Rita Hayworth and the Shawshank Redemption
The Stand: The Stand: The Complete and Uncut Edition

quips.Carrie: King threw the first draft in the trash; his wife Tabitha fished it out and urged him on.
quips.The Running Man: Published under King's pen name Richard Bachman, like The Long Walk and Thinner.
quips.The Body: The novella behind the film Stand by Me, a story of four boys searching for a body.

chapters.text: Name a classic novel first published before 1900

krillion.quip: Charles Kingsley's 1863 fantasy about a chimney sweep who becomes a water-baby.

schooler: Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
Around the World in Eighty Days
Journey to the Center of the Earth

From the Earth to the Moon

Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde: Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde

A Journey to the Center of the Earth
