Hans Brinker: Hans Brinker, or The Silver Skates
The Narrative of Arthur Gordon Pym: The Narrative of Arthur Gordon Pym of Nantucket

quips.Frankenstein: Mary Shelley began it at 18, during a rainy ghost-story contest by Lake Geneva.
quips.Don Quixote: Often called the first modern novel, published in two parts in 1605 and 1615.
quips.Alice's Adventures in Wonderland: Carroll first told it on a July 1862 river trip to Alice Liddell and her sisters.

chapters.text: Name a famous novelist

krillion.quip: Wrote the Gormenghast trilogy and illustrated Treasure Island and Alice.

quips.Mark Twain: Real name Samuel Clemens; 'mark twain' is riverboat slang for two fathoms deep.
quips.George Eliot: Mary Ann Evans chose a male pen name so her novels would be taken seriously.

chapters.text: Name a classic children's book character

krillion.quip: The widowed field mouse who asks the clever rats of NIMH to help move her home.

Mike Mulligan: Mike Mulligan and His Steam Shovel

quips.Winnie-the-Pooh: Named for Winnipeg, a real Canadian black bear that lived at London Zoo.
quips.Peter Pan: Barrie signed over the play's rights to Great Ormond Street Hospital for sick children.
quips.Paddington Bear: Michael Bond spotted a lone toy bear on a London shop shelf on Christmas Eve, 1956.

packs.name: Cars & Transport
packs.tagline: 21 journeys · are we there yet?

chapters.text: Name a car model

krillion.quip: Trabants had Duroplast bodies made from resin and recycled cotton waste.

quips.Isetta: The Isetta's entire front end swung open as the door, steering wheel and all.
quips.Peel P50: The Peel P50 holds the record for smallest production car ever made.
quips.Model T: Ford sold over 15 million Model Ts between 1908 and 1927.
quips.Countach: Countach drivers famously reversed by perching on the sill with the scissor door up.

chapters.text: Name a type of car (body style or category)

krillion.quip: Shooting brakes began as horse-drawn wagons carrying hunting parties and their guns.

quips.Fastback: The Ford Mustang made the fastback roofline a pop-culture icon.
quips.Kei car: Japan's kei cars are limited to 660 cc engines and a tiny footprint.
quips.Gull-wing: The 1954 Mercedes 300 SL's gull-wing doors were needed because of its tubular frame.

chapters.text: Name something with wheels

krillion.quip: Curiosity's wheel treads stamp 'JPL' in Morse code into the Martian dust.

quips.Zamboni: Frank Zamboni built the first ice resurfacer in 1949 for his California rink.
quips.Lunar rover: Apollo's lunar rover folded up and rode to the Moon bolted to the side of the lander.

chapters.text: Name an airline

krillion.quip: Loganair's Westray to Papa Westray hop is the world's shortest scheduled flight.

quips.Pan Am: Pan Am's Clipper flying boats linked California to Asia in the 1930s.
quips.Laker Airways: Freddie Laker's cut-price Skytrain helped invent cheap transatlantic flying.
quips.Qantas: Qantas was founded in 1920 as the Queensland and Northern Territory Aerial Services.

chapters.text: Name an international airport

krillion.quip: At Princess Juliana, jets skim Maho Beach so low that sunbathers feel the blast.

quips.Kai Tak: Kai Tak's approach had pilots banking low over Hong Kong rooftops to line up the runway.
quips.Tempelhof: Tempelhof's 1930s terminal was once among the largest buildings in the world.
quips.Heathrow: Heathrow began in 1929 as a small airfield called the Great West Aerodrome.

chapters.text: Name a type of boat or ship

krillion.quip: A coracle is so light and round that one person can carry it on their back.

quips.Currach: Irish currachs are made of tarred canvas stretched over a wooden frame, once animal hide.
quips.Hovercraft: Christopher Cockerell tested his hovercraft idea using a cat-food tin and a vacuum cleaner.
quips.Dromon: Dromons were the Byzantine navy's main warships, famous for hurling Greek fire.

chapters.text: Name a part of a ship

krillion.quip: Said 'gunnel': it began as the plank that supported a warship's guns.

quips.Plimsoll line: Samuel Plimsoll campaigned for the load line that curbed overloaded 'coffin ships'.
quips.Binnacle: The binnacle is the stand that holds a ship's compass, often with a built-in lamp.
quips.Poop deck: It comes from the Latin puppis, meaning stern, and not from anything rude.

chapters.text: Name a motorcycle brand

krillion.quip: T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, died riding his Brough Superior in 1935.

quips.Hildebrand & Wolfmüller: Their 1894 machine is regarded as the first production motorcycle.
quips.Britten: John Britten hand-built his radical V1000 superbike in a New Zealand workshop.
quips.Vincent: Vincent's Black Lightning set motorcycle speed records on the salt flats in 1948.
quips.Hesketh: Lord Hesketh also ran a Formula One team, with a young James Hunt driving.

chapters.text: Name a type of aircraft (not a specific model)

krillion.quip: An autogyro's rotor spins freely in the airflow while a propeller pulls it forward.

quips.Ornithopter: Ornithopters flap their wings like birds; Leonardo da Vinci sketched one in the 1480s.
quips.Rozière balloon: A Rozière balloon pairs hydrogen with hot air; it killed its inventor, Pilâtre de Rozier.
quips.Flying wing: Flying wings drop the tail and fuselage entirely; the B-2 stealth bomber is one.

chapters.text: Name a famous train or railway

krillion.quip: The Darjeeling 'Toy Train' runs on 2-foot gauge track and is a World Heritage Site.

quips.Jupiter: Jupiter met Union Pacific's No. 119 nose to nose at Promontory Summit in 1869.
quips.Tren Maya: Mexico's Tren Maya loops around the Yucatan Peninsula past Chichen Itza.
quips.Rocket: Stephenson's Rocket won the 1829 Rainhill Trials at about 30 miles per hour.

chapters.text: Name a part of a car

krillion.quip: A Panhard rod stops an axle sliding sideways; it's named for the French maker Panhard.

quips.Differential: A differential lets the outer wheel spin faster than the inner one in a turn.
quips.Crumple zone: Béla Barényi, a Mercedes engineer, patented the crumple zone in 1952.
quips.Bonnet ornament: Rolls-Royce's flying lady mascot was modelled on Eleanor Thornton.

chapters.text: Name a city with a metro or subway system

krillion.quip: Tashkent opened Central Asia's first metro in 1977, with stations decorated like palaces.

quips.Budapest: Budapest's Line 1 opened in 1896, the first underground railway on mainland Europe.
quips.Glasgow: The Glasgow Subway's nickname is the Clockwork Orange, for its orange trains.
quips.Pyongyang: Pyongyang's metro stations are among the deepest in the world, and ornately decorated.
quips.Haifa: Haifa's Carmelit is a funicular and counts as Israel's only subway.

chapters.text: Name a type of bicycle

krillion.quip: The 1817 draisine had no pedals; riders pushed along the ground with their feet.

quips.Penny-farthing: The big wheel of a penny-farthing meant a bigger gear, but a longer fall.
quips.Velomobile: A velomobile is a pedal-powered recumbent trike wrapped in an aerodynamic shell.
quips.Boneshaker: Boneshakers had iron-rimmed wooden wheels, hence the name.

chapters.text: Name a famous racing circuit

krillion.quip: Brooklands, opened in 1907, was the world's first purpose-built motor racing circuit.

Imola: Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari Imola

quips.Brooklands: Brooklands' banked concrete oval was built in 1907 near Weybridge, Surrey.
quips.Targa Florio: The Targa Florio ran on Sicilian mountain roads from 1906 and was one of motorsport's oldest races.
quips.Pikes Peak: Pikes Peak's hill climb has run to a 14,000-foot summit since 1916.
quips.Nürburgring: Jackie Stewart nicknamed the Nordschleife 'the Green Hell'.

chapters.text: Name a military aircraft

krillion.quip: Slow, fabric-covered Swordfish biplanes crippled the Bismarck's rudder in 1941.

quips.Fairey Swordfish: Despite its antique look, the Swordfish sank more Axis shipping than any other British aircraft.
quips.XB-70 Valkyrie: The XB-70 flew at Mach 3 by riding its own shockwave under folding wingtips.
quips.Avro Arrow: Canada scrapped its Mach 2 Avro Arrow interceptor in 1959, and the debate still rages.
quips.Fokker Dr.I: Manfred von Richthofen, the Red Baron, scored his last victories in a Fokker Dr.I.

chapters.text: Name a space rocket or launch vehicle

krillion.quip: Britain's Black Arrow put the Prospero satellite in orbit in 1971, then was cancelled.

quips.Black Arrow: Britain remains the only nation to have orbited a satellite and then dropped its rocket programme.
quips.V-2: In 1944 a V-2 became the first human-made object to reach space on a suborbital flight.
quips.N1: The Soviet N1 Moon rocket never reached orbit; all four test launches failed.
quips.Starship: Starship is the tallest and most powerful rocket ever launched.

chapters.text: Name a horse-drawn vehicle

krillion.quip: A droshky is a light open Russian cab, drawn by horses around old St Petersburg.

Surrey: Surrey with the fringe on top

quips.Shooting brake: Before it described a car body, a shooting brake carried hunters and their guns by horse.
quips.Hansom cab: Joseph Hansom patented the cab in 1834; the driver sat on a perch behind.
quips.Gold State Coach: The Gold State Coach has carried every British monarch to their coronation since 1831.

chapters.text: Name a famous car from the movies or television

krillion.quip: The Blues Brothers' Bluesmobile is an ex-police 1974 Dodge Monaco.

Bandit's Trans Am: Smokey and the Bandit Trans Am
Bond's AMC Hornet: Man with the Golden Gun AMC Hornet

quips.Bluesmobile: Elwood bought the old cop car at auction, and the brothers were on a mission from God.
quips.DeLorean: The real DeLorean DMC-12 had a stainless-steel body and gull-wing doors.
quips.Pursuit Special: The Pursuit Special was a customised Australian Ford Falcon XB GT Coupe.
quips.Mr. Bean's Mini: Mr. Bean's lime-green Mini was a 1976 Leyland Mini 1000.

chapters.text: Name a vehicle or machine you'd see on a building site

krillion.quip: Skid steers turn by braking one side's wheels, so they spin on the spot.

quips.Skid steer: The first skid-steer loader was built in 1957 by the Keller brothers in North Dakota.
quips.Franna crane: Franna cranes pick up a load and then drive with it, a trick called pick-and-carry.
quips.Tunnel boring machine: Tunnel boring machines are usually lowered in pieces and assembled in a shaft.
quips.Telehandler: A telehandler is a forklift with a telescopic boom that can reach over walls.

chapters.text: Name an electric vehicle model

krillion.quip: The Citroën Ami is a tiny electric quadricycle you can drive from age 14 in France.

quips.Citroën Ami: The Ami tops out at 45 km/h, which is why 14-year-olds can drive it in France.
quips.GM EV1: General Motors leased the EV1 in the 1990s, then famously reclaimed and crushed most.
quips.Sinclair C5: Sir Clive Sinclair's 1985 C5 was an electric trike with a top speed of 15 mph.
quips.Rimac Nevera: The Rimac Nevera hit 60 mph in under two seconds and set a string of EV records.

chapters.text: Name a model of passenger airliner

krillion.quip: The Soviet Tu-144 flew supersonic two months before Concorde, on 31 December 1968.

Twin Otter: De Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter

quips.Tupolev Tu-144: The Tu-144 was nicknamed Concordski, but a 1973 Paris Air Show crash dented its career.
quips.Boeing 314 Clipper: Pan Am's Boeing 314 Clipper flying boats crossed the Atlantic and Pacific in the late 1930s.
quips.Boeing 747: The 747's upper-deck hump was designed so its nose could swing open as a freighter.
quips.Concorde: Concorde cruised at Mach 2 and flew London to New York in about three and a half hours.

packs.name: Home & Hobbies
packs.tagline: 21 weekends · find a new obsession

chapters.text: Name a hobby

krillion.quip: Mudlarkers comb the Thames foreshore at low tide for centuries-old lost treasures.

quips.Geocaching: A worldwide treasure hunt: you use GPS to find hidden containers called caches.
quips.Pigeon racing: Racing pigeons can find their way home from hundreds of miles away.
quips.Kendama: A Japanese cup-and-ball skill toy with competitions around the world.
quips.Pinball: Early pinball machines had no flippers at all, so skill was nearly impossible.

chapters.text: Name something you'd find in a toolbox

krillion.quip: A weight on a string — builders have used it to find true vertical for millennia.

quips.Spokeshave: A woodworker's two-handled blade for shaping curves like chair legs and wheel spokes.
quips.Bradawl: A small pointed tool that starts screw holes in wood without splitting it.
quips.Feeler gauge: A fan of thin steel strips used to measure tiny gaps, such as in engines.
quips.Vice grips: The original Vise-Grip was invented in 1924 by William Petersen of Nebraska.

chapters.text: Name a craft

krillion.quip: Japanese 'floating ink' marbling, with roots reaching back to around the 12th century.

quips.Kintsugi: Japanese artisans mend broken pottery with gold, so the cracks become the feature.
quips.Pysanky: Ukrainian eggs are decorated with wax-resist designs, layer by layer, in rich dyes.
quips.Origami: Origami comes from the Japanese 'ori' (folding) and 'kami' (paper).
quips.Furoshiki: Furoshiki is the Japanese art of wrapping gifts and goods in a square of cloth.

chapters.text: Name a dance or dance style

krillion.quip: Filipino dancers hop between clacking bamboo poles, imitating the tikling bird.

quips.Haka: The haka is a Māori ceremonial dance, famously performed by New Zealand's All Blacks.
quips.Moonwalk: Michael Jackson unveiled it on TV in 1983, though others had glided backwards before him.
quips.Can-can: The can-can first shocked audiences in 1830s Paris music halls.
quips.Capoeira: Capoeira, an Afro-Brazilian art, blends dance, acrobatics and fighting set to music.
quips.Kecak: Bali's kecak has a huge circle of men chanting 'cak' instead of using instruments.

chapters.text: Name a type of knot

krillion.quip: A decorative woven ring that sailors wrap around rails, handles and ship's wheels.

rare: Round turn and two half hitches

quips.Monkey's fist: Sailors tie it round a ball so a light line can be thrown a long way.
quips.Prusik knot: Climbers use it to slide up or lock onto a rope; it's named after Karl Prusik.
quips.Bimini twist: An anglers' knot that creates a doubled line, said to keep nearly full line strength.
quips.Zeppelin bend: Strong, yet easy to untie even after heavy loading.

chapters.text: Name a houseplant

krillion.quip: Lithops, the 'living stones', mimic pebbles to hide from hungry animals.

quips.Venus flytrap: A flytrap snaps shut only after two touches within about 20 seconds, saving energy.
quips.Ponytail palm: Not a true palm: it stores water in its swollen trunk base like a succulent.
quips.Spider plant: Spider plants grow dangling baby plantlets that you can simply snip off and pot up.
quips.Mother of thousands: It sprouts hundreds of tiny plantlets along its leaf edges, ready to drop and root.
quips.Lucky bamboo: Despite the name, lucky bamboo is a Dracaena, not a true bamboo.

chapters.text: Name a gardening tool

krillion.quip: This Japanese digging knife is named by saying the word for 'dig' twice.

quips.Dibber: A pointed wooden peg that makes the perfect hole for seedlings and bulbs.
quips.Scythe: Scythes have been used to cut grass and harvest grain for well over a thousand years.
quips.Billhook: A hooked blade used for hedge laying and trimming small branches.
quips.Strimmer: The weed trimmer was invented in the 1970s by George Ballas, inspired by car-wash brushes.

chapters.text: Name a household appliance

krillion.quip: A clamp that presses a crease into trousers overnight — still a hotel-room classic.

quips.Mangle: Victorian mangles squeezed water out of laundry between two heavy rollers.
quips.Samovar: A samovar is a traditional Russian urn that keeps water hot for tea.
quips.Microwave: The microwave oven was invented after a candy bar melted in a radar engineer's pocket.
quips.Twin tub: A twin tub has separate drums for washing and spinning, so you move the clothes yourself.

chapters.text: Name something you'd take camping

krillion.quip: Australian campers boil their tea in this tin pot, called a 'billy'.

quips.Billycan: The word 'billy' for a bush kettle goes back to 19th-century Australia.
quips.Ferro rod: A ferrocerium rod throws sparks around 3,000°C, even when it is wet.
quips.Marshmallows: Marshmallows were first made from the root sap of the marshmallow plant.
quips.Hammock: Hammock camping keeps you off wet, lumpy ground, if you can find two good trees.

chapters.text: Name a type of puzzle

krillion.quip: Also called Picross, Griddlers or Hanjie — number clues reveal a hidden picture.

quips.Tangram: Tangram's seven flat pieces can be arranged into thousands of different shapes.
quips.Seven Bridges of Königsberg: Euler's 1736 solution to this puzzle founded graph theory.
quips.Tower of Hanoi: Solving it with n discs takes at least 2^n minus 1 moves.
quips.Rubik's Cube: Erno Rubik invented the Cube in 1974 as a teaching tool for his architecture students.

chapters.text: Name something you'd find in a playground

krillion.quip: Spring riders are the bouncy animals on a coil, also called spring rockers.

quips.Seesaw: Seesaw physics: a lighter child sits farther from the pivot to balance a heavier one.
quips.Monkey bars: Brachiating, swinging hand over hand, is how gibbons travel through the trees.
quips.Hopscotch: Hopscotch is said to date to ancient Rome, where children copied soldiers' drills.

chapters.text: Name a fishing term or piece of fishing gear

krillion.quip: In Scotland a ghillie guides anglers on the river, helping them find and land fish.

quips.Tippet: Fly anglers tie a fine, nearly invisible tippet between the leader and the fly.
quips.Berley: Berley is what Australians call the chopped bait thrown out to attract fish.
quips.Spey casting: Spey casting takes its name from Scotland's River Spey.

chapters.text: Name a party game

krillion.quip: Hide-and-seek in reverse: one person hides and everyone else squeezes in with them.

plankton: Pin the tail on the donkey

I spy: I spy with my little eye

quips.Sardines: Sardines is hide-and-seek in reverse: everyone ends up crammed into one hiding place.
quips.Charades: Charades began as a 1700s French parlour game acted out in rhyme or riddle form.
quips.Pass the parcel: In pass the parcel, each unwrapped layer of paper might hide a small prize.
quips.Limbo: Limbo comes from Trinidad, where it began as a wake ritual.

chapters.text: Name an unusual pet

krillion.quip: A rainforest relative of the raccoon with a very long tongue, nicknamed 'honey bear'.

quips.Axolotl: Axolotls can regrow lost limbs, and even parts of their hearts and brains.
quips.Fennec fox: A fennec's huge ears help it shed heat in the Sahara.
quips.Sugar glider: Sugar gliders can glide up to about 50 metres between trees on a skin membrane.
quips.Pet rock: Gary Dahl sold over a million Pet Rocks in 1975, complete with a training manual.
quips.Sea-Monkeys: Sea-Monkeys are brine shrimp that hatch from dried eggs when you add water.

chapters.text: Name a knitting, crochet or sewing term

krillion.quip: A steek is a deliberate cut through finished knitting, used for Fair Isle cardigans.

quips.Frogging: Knitters call ripping out work 'frogging', because 'rip it, rip it' sounds like a frog.
quips.Kitchener stitch: Kitchener stitch grafts two live edges together so it looks like unbroken knitting.
quips.Amigurumi: Amigurumi is the Japanese art of crocheting or knitting small stuffed creatures.
quips.Selvage: A fabric's selvage is its self-finished edge; the word comes from 'self-edge'.

chapters.text: Name a magic trick or sleight of hand

krillion.quip: A Victorian glass-reflection illusion; Disney's Haunted Mansion ghosts still use it.

Rabbit out of a hat: Pulling a rabbit out of a hat
Walking through a wall: Walk through the Great Wall of China
Out of this world: Paul Curry's Out of This World

quips.Bullet catch: The bullet catch has claimed the lives of several performers over the centuries.
quips.Zig-zag girl: Robert Harbin's 1965 Zig Zag Girl slices a boxed assistant into three offset sections.
quips.Elmsley count: Alex Elmsley's count shows four cards as four while hiding the odd one out.
quips.Vanishing elephant: Houdini made a live elephant disappear on stage at New York's Hippodrome in 1918.

chapters.text: Name an art supply or technique

krillion.quip: Painters rest their brush hand on this stick to keep it steady for fine detail.

quips.Sfumato: Sfumato, Leonardo's smoky blending, comes from the Italian for 'vanished like smoke'.
quips.Pointillism: Pointillists like Seurat built images from tiny dots of pure colour.
quips.Trompe l'oeil: Trompe l'oeil is French for 'deceives the eye': painting made to look 3D.

chapters.text: Name a type of cake

krillion.quip: Germany's 'tree cake' is baked layer by layer on a spit, so slices show tree-like rings.

quips.Jaffa cake: A UK tax tribunal ruled in 1991 that Jaffa Cakes are cakes, not biscuits.
quips.Lamington: Lamingtons are Australian sponge squares dipped in chocolate and rolled in coconut.
quips.Battenberg: Battenberg's pink and yellow checkerboard is wrapped in marzipan.
quips.Panettone: Panettone is a tall Italian Christmas bread-cake studded with candied fruit and raisins.

chapters.text: Name something you'd find in a garage

krillion.quip: Mechanics lie on this low wheeled board to roll under cars.

quips.Creeper: Mechanics lie back on this low wheeled board to slide under cars.
quips.WD-40: WD-40 stands for 'Water Displacement, 40th attempt', the formula that finally worked.
quips.Axle stands: Never work under a car held up by a jack alone; axle stands keep it safe.

chapters.text: Name a woodworking term

krillion.quip: The kerf is the slot a saw blade removes — it shares a root with 'carve'.

quips.Kerf: The kerf is the slot a saw blade removes — it shares a root with 'carve'.
quips.Birdsmouth: A birdsmouth is a V-notch cut in a rafter so it sits snugly on the wall plate.
quips.Spalting: Spalting is the dark lines fungi leave in wood; turners prize them.
quips.Dutchman: A Dutchman is a patch of wood glued into a damaged spot, shaped to match.

chapters.text: Name a photography term

krillion.quip: Focus at this distance and everything from half of it to infinity looks sharp.

quips.Camera obscura: Latin for 'dark chamber', this pinhole-image idea is far older than photography.
quips.Bokeh: Bokeh comes from the Japanese 'boke', meaning blur or haze.
quips.Daguerreotype: The first practical photo process, announced in 1839, used a silvered copper plate.
quips.Sunny 16 rule: On a sunny day, set f/16 and a shutter speed of 1/ISO for a good exposure.

packs.name: Odds & Ends
packs.tagline: 21 rummages · the junk drawer of the deep

chapters.text: Name something that is yellow

krillion.quip: Native sulfur crystallises bright yellow around volcanic vents and hot springs.

quips.Io: Jupiter's moon Io is splashed yellow by sulfur from its hundreds of volcanoes.
quips.Banana slug: Banana slugs grow up to 25 cm long, and many of them are bright yellow.
quips.22-spot ladybird: The 22-spot ladybird is lemon yellow and eats mildew instead of aphids.
quips.Brimstone butterfly: Brimstone butterflies hibernate as adults and can live for nearly a year.

chapters.text: Name something that is round

krillion.quip: Marimo are living algae that curl into soft green balls and roll along lake beds.

quips.Sand dollar: A sand dollar is the flat, round skeleton of a burrowing sea urchin.
quips.Atomium: Brussels' Atomium is a 102 m model of an iron crystal in nine steel spheres.
quips.Puffball mushroom: A giant puffball can top a football in size and puff out trillions of spores.
quips.Moon jellyfish: A moon jelly's four pale horseshoe rings are its reproductive organs.

chapters.text: Name something with a shell

krillion.quip: Glyptodons were car-sized Ice Age relatives of armadillos in a domed bony shell.

quips.Armadillo: Armadillo is Spanish for 'little armoured one'.
quips.Geoduck: A geoduck's siphon is so long the clam can't fully pull it back into its shell.
quips.Horseshoe crab: Horseshoe crabs have blue blood and have been around longer than the dinosaurs.
quips.Coconut crab: Coconut crabs are the largest land arthropods and can crack coconuts with their claws.

chapters.text: Name something that has keys

krillion.quip: Sweden's nyckelharpa is a fiddle whose notes come from a row of wooden keys.

quips.Ophicleide: The ophicleide is a keyed brass instrument that the tuba later replaced.
quips.Hurdy-gurdy: A hurdy-gurdy makes its drone by cranking a rosined wheel against its strings.
quips.Calliope: A calliope is a steam-powered organ with a keyboard, heard at fairs and on riverboats.

chapters.text: Name something you'd find at the beach

krillion.quip: Those leathery black pouches on the shore are empty egg cases of skates or sharks.

quips.Sea glass: Sea glass is broken bottle glass tumbled smooth and frosted by years of waves.
quips.Cuttlebone: A cuttlefish's chalky cuttlebone is a gas-filled float, often sold for pet birds.
quips.Tombolo: A tombolo is a sandbar that links an island to the mainland.

chapters.text: Name something that runs on batteries

krillion.quip: A modern pacemaker's tiny lithium battery can power it for around ten years.

quips.Lunar Roving Vehicle: The Apollo moon buggy ran on non-rechargeable silver-zinc batteries.
quips.Sputnik 1: Sputnik 1's beeping radio ran on silver-zinc batteries that lasted about three weeks.
quips.Metronome: Mechanical metronomes use clockwork, but most modern ones run on batteries.

chapters.text: Name something that floats

krillion.quip: Pumice is so full of gas bubbles that this volcanic rock floats on water.

quips.Fire ant raft: Fire ants link their bodies into a waterproof raft that can float for weeks.
quips.Sea otter: Sea otters hold paws while they sleep so they don't drift apart.
quips.Kon-Tiki: Thor Heyerdahl's 1947 balsa raft Kon-Tiki drifted 8,000 km across the Pacific.

chapters.text: Name something people collect

krillion.quip: Hobbyists who hoard matchbooks and matchbox labels are called phillumenists.

quips.Fabergé eggs: Of the 50 imperial Fabergé eggs made for Russia's tsars, 43 survive today.
quips.First day covers: A first day cover is an envelope stamped on the very day a new stamp is issued.
quips.Netsuke: Netsuke are carved toggles once used to hang pouches from Japanese kimono sashes.
quips.Sugar packets: Collecting sugar packets is called sucrology.

chapters.text: Name something sticky

krillion.quip: Sundew leaves glisten with sticky droplets that trap insects.

quips.Gecko feet: Gecko toes cling using tiny molecular forces, no goo required.
quips.Propolis: Propolis is the sticky resin bees collect to seal gaps in their hive.
quips.Butterwort: Butterwort leaves are slick with sticky mucilage that traps gnats.

chapters.text: Name something with teeth (not an animal)

krillion.quip: The little perforated edges around a postage stamp are literally called its teeth.

quips.Dragon's teeth: Dragon's teeth are rows of concrete pyramids built as tank barriers.
quips.Cog railway: Cog railways grip a toothed rack rail to climb slopes that adhesion trains can't.

chapters.text: Name something you plug in

krillion.quip: Hobby Tesla coils turn ordinary mains power into crackling, foot-long sparks.

quips.Theremin: A theremin is played without touching it, by moving your hands near two antennas.
quips.Van de Graaff generator: A Van de Graaff generator builds up static until your hair stands on end.
quips.Neon sign: Neon signs need a high-voltage transformer to light their glowing gas tubes.

chapters.text: Name something with buttons

krillion.quip: A bayan is a Russian chromatic button accordion, played by pressing rows of buttons.

quips.Telegraph key: A telegraph key is a spring-loaded button tapped to send Morse code.
quips.Snowman: A snowman's coal buttons are the classic finishing touch.

chapters.text: Name something that is cold

krillion.quip: Antarctica's Vostok Station recorded the coldest air temperature ever: -89.2°C.

quips.Boomerang Nebula: The Boomerang Nebula, at about 1 K, is the coldest known natural place in the universe.
quips.Oymyakon: Oymyakon in Siberia, the coldest permanently inhabited place, has hit about -67°C.
quips.Large Hadron Collider: The LHC's magnets run at 1.9 K, colder than the vacuum of outer space.
quips.Liquid helium: Liquid helium boils at about -269°C, colder than almost anything on Earth.

chapters.text: Name something that melts

krillion.quip: Gallium melts at about 30°C, so a lump turns liquid in your warm hand.

quips.Wicked Witch of the West: The Wicked Witch of the West famously melts when Dorothy throws water on her.
quips.Dalí's melting clocks: Dalí's 1931 painting The Persistence of Memory made melting clocks famous.
quips.Cesium: Cesium melts at about 28°C, so it can turn liquid on a warm day.
quips.Wood's metal: Wood's metal melts at about 70°C, so a spoon of it dissolves in hot tea.

chapters.text: Name something with a screen

krillion.quip: A fish finder's screen paints sonar echoes into a picture of fish and seabed.

quips.Teleprompter: A teleprompter reflects scrolling text onto glass in front of a camera lens.
quips.Virtual Boy: Nintendo's 1995 Virtual Boy showed red-only 3D graphics and sold poorly.
quips.Game & Watch: Nintendo's Game & Watch handhelds put a tiny LCD game and a clock in one pocket gadget.

chapters.text: Name something you can inflate

krillion.quip: NASA's BEAM module launched folded and inflated like a balloon on the space station.

quips.Barrage balloon: Barrage balloons were tethered over cities in WWII to snag low-flying aircraft.
quips.Echo 1 satellite: Echo 1 (1960) was a 30 m balloon satellite that bounced radio signals worldwide.
quips.Evacuation slide: Aircraft escape slides inflate in about six seconds when the door is opened.

chapters.text: Name something that comes in pairs

krillion.quip: Claves are two hardwood sticks, tapped together to keep Latin rhythm.

quips.Chromosomes: Humans carry 23 pairs of chromosomes in almost every cell.
quips.Cleopatra's Needles: Ancient Egyptian obelisks called Cleopatra's Needles stand in London and New York.
quips.Pillars of Hercules: The Pillars of Hercules are the rocks flanking the Strait of Gibraltar.

chapters.text: Name a word containing "ZZ"

krillion.quip: The mizzenmast is the aft mast on a sailing ship, behind the main mast.

quips.Rizz: Rizz, short for charisma, was Oxford's 2023 Word of the Year.
quips.Gizzard: A gizzard is the muscular stomach birds use to grind food with swallowed grit.
quips.Muezzin: A muezzin is the person who gives the Islamic call to prayer.

chapters.text: Name a compound word starting with "sun"

krillion.quip: The sunbittern flashes sun-like eyespots on its spread wings to startle predators.

quips.Sundog: A sundog is a bright spot on either side of the Sun caused by ice crystals in the air.
quips.Sundew: Sundews are carnivorous plants named for the dew-like drops on their leaves.
quips.Sunquake: A sunquake is a burst of seismic waves rippling out through the Sun after a solar flare.

chapters.text: Name an animal with a three-letter name

krillion.quip: The kea is the world's only alpine parrot, and it loves to shred car rubber.

quips.Moa: The giant moa of New Zealand was a wingless bird up to 3.6 m tall, hunted to extinction.
quips.Ayu: The ayu is a Japanese sweetfish prized for its faint melon-like scent.
quips.Eft: An eft is the juvenile land stage of a newt.

chapters.text: Name something with a handle

krillion.quip: In 1854 John Snow had a Broad Street pump's handle removed to stop a cholera outbreak.

quips.Gavel: A gavel's handle lets a judge rap for order without hurting a hand.
quips.Dibber: A dibber is a pointed gardening tool, handle on top, for poking planting holes.

packs.name: Art & Design
packs.tagline: 21 masterpieces · Frame your rarest guess

chapters.text: Name a famous painting

krillion.quip: Holbein hid a stretched skull in it that only snaps into shape when you view it from the side.

schooler: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
Arrangement in Grey and Black No. 1
A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte
Dance at Le Moulin de la Galette
Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow
Portrait of an Artist (Pool with Two Figures)
Bal du Moulin de la Galette
The Return of the Prodigal Son
The Storm on the Sea of Galilee
rare: The Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Nicolaes Tulp
Self-Portrait with Thorn Necklace and Hummingbird
Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going?
The Problem We All Live With
Ivan the Terrible and His Son Ivan
David with the Head of Goliath
The Feast in the House of Levi
The Great Day of His Wrath
Max Schmitt in a Single Scull
The Daughters of Edward Darley Boit
deepcut: Christ of Saint John of the Cross
Landscape with the Fall of Icarus
Judith and the Head of Holofernes
Who's Afraid of Red, Yellow and Blue

quips.The Scream: Munch made several versions, including pastels and a lithograph.
quips.Water Lilies: Monet painted about 250 of them in his garden at Giverny.
quips.Nighthawks: Hopper based the diner on one in Greenwich Village that no longer exists.
quips.The Night Watch: Its real subject is a civic militia company, and it was trimmed to fit a wall in 1715.

chapters.text: Name a pattern or print

krillion.quip: Kente is woven in narrow strips by Ghanaian weavers, and each colour combination carries its own meaning.

quips.Paisley: Named after the Scottish town that mass-produced the teardrop-shaped Persian boteh motif.
quips.Houndstooth: It began as a woollen check worn by Scottish shepherds.
quips.Argyle: Based on the tartan of Clan Campbell of Argyll, worn on knitted socks.
quips.Toile de Jouy: Named after the French village of Jouy-en-Josas, where it was printed in the 1700s.

chapters.text: Name a font or typeface

krillion.quip: A 2014 redesign of Comic Sans aimed at people who like the casual look but not the reputation.

quips.Helvetica: Released in 1957 as Neue Haas Grotesk, then renamed after the Latin name for Switzerland.
quips.Comic Sans: Vincent Connare designed it in 1994 after seeing a cartoon dog use Times New Roman in a speech bubble.
quips.Times New Roman: Commissioned by The Times of London in 1931.
quips.Johnston: Edward Johnston drew it in 1916 for the London Underground, and it is still in use.

chapters.text: Name an art movement or style

krillion.quip: A short-lived British movement launched in 1914 with a bright pink magazine called BLAST.

quips.Impressionism: The name came from a critic mocking Monet's painting Impression, Sunrise.
quips.Fauvism: Fauves means 'wild beasts', another critic's insult that stuck.
quips.Pointillism: Seurat built whole canvases from tiny dots of pure colour.
quips.De Stijl: Dutch for 'The Style', the movement behind Mondrian's grids.

chapters.text: Name a type of jewellery

krillion.quip: A decorative belt clasp with chains for hanging scissors, keys and watches, worn by Victorian housekeepers.

quips.Cameo: Classic cameos are carved from shells so the pale layer stands proud of a darker background.
quips.Claddagh ring: From a fishing village in Galway, it shows two hands holding a crowned heart.
quips.Mood ring: A 1975 craze in which liquid crystals change colour with your skin temperature.
quips.Torc: A rigid Iron Age neck ring, and the Snettisham hoard in England held dozens of them.

chapters.text: Name a famous sculptor

krillion.quip: Rodin's student and partner whose own work was overshadowed for decades; there is now a museum devoted to her.

quips.Brâncuși: US customs once refused to class his Bird in Space as art and tried to tax it as metal.
quips.Antony Gormley: His Angel of the North has wings 54 metres across, wider than a jumbo jet.
quips.Gutzon Borglum: He carved Mount Rushmore and died months before it was finished; his son completed it.
quips.Alexander Calder: He invented the mobile, and Marcel Duchamp gave it that name.

chapters.text: Name a famous cartoonist or illustrator

krillion.quip: The Finnish creator of the Moomins also drew satirical magazine covers mocking Hitler and Stalin.

quips.Charles Schulz: He drew nearly 18,000 Peanuts strips himself, and the last one ran the day after he died.
quips.Bill Watterson: He refused almost all Calvin and Hobbes merchandise, so most of those car stickers are bootlegs.
quips.Quentin Blake: He was the first Children's Laureate in the UK, in 1999.
quips.Beatrix Potter: She was also a serious mycologist and drew hundreds of studies of fungi.

chapters.text: Name an architectural style

krillion.quip: Portugal's ornate late-Gothic style, carved with ropes, coral, anchors and armillary spheres from the age of sea voyages.

quips.Brutalism: From the French béton brut, meaning raw concrete, not from 'brutal'.
quips.Gothic: The name was an insult from Renaissance critics who thought it barbaric, like the Goths.
quips.Palladian: Based on Andrea Palladio's villas, it spread from the Veneto to English country houses and the White House.
quips.Googie: Named after a Los Angeles coffee shop, it gave the 1950s its boomerangs and starbursts.

chapters.text: Name a part or feature of a building

krillion.quip: The Pantheon's 8.2-metre oculus has been open to the sky for nearly 1,900 years, and rain falls straight onto the floor.

quips.Gargoyle: Strictly, a gargoyle is a water spout, and carvings that don't drain rain are called grotesques.
quips.Keystone: It is the last stone set at the top of an arch, locking all the others in place.
quips.Flying buttress: It let Gothic builders open walls up for huge stained-glass windows.
quips.Muqarnas: Honeycomb-like vaulting cells used in Islamic architecture from Spain to Iran.

chapters.text: Name a famous cathedral, church, mosque or temple

krillion.quip: Reykjavík's church tower was designed to look like basalt columns formed by cooling lava.

rare: Church of the Savior on Spilled Blood
Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe
Cathedral of St John the Divine
deepcut: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace
Church of Saint Francis of Assisi Pampulha
Church of Our Lady before Týn

quips.Sagrada Família: Construction began in 1882 and it is still being finished.
quips.Hagia Sophia: Its dome was the largest in the world for nearly a thousand years.
quips.Cologne Cathedral: It took 632 years to finish, from 1248 to 1880.
quips.Borobudur: The world's largest Buddhist temple, with over 2,600 relief panels and 504 Buddha statues.

chapters.text: Name a type of building or dwelling

krillion.quip: Puglia's dry-stone huts have conical roofs built without mortar, supposedly so they could be taken apart quickly when tax inspectors came.

quips.Igloo: In Inuktitut, iglu just means 'house', whatever it is made of.
quips.Yurt: A Mongolian ger can be taken down and packed onto camels in about an hour.
quips.Hogan: The traditional Navajo home, whose doorway faces east to greet the rising sun.
quips.Broch: These Iron Age stone towers are found only in Scotland, and Mousa Broch still stands 13 metres high.

chapters.text: Name a type of pot, vase or vessel

krillion.quip: A wide, shallow ancient Greek drinking cup, often painted inside so a picture appeared as you drained your wine.

quips.Amphora: Romans dumped so many broken olive-oil amphorae in one spot that they made a whole hill, Monte Testaccio.
quips.Canopic jar: Egyptian embalmers used four of them, each with a different god's head guarding an organ.
quips.Toby jug: Shaped like a jolly seated man in a tricorn hat, first made in Staffordshire around 1760.
quips.Moon jar: Korean potters threw these round white jars in two halves and joined them in the middle.

chapters.text: Name a famous theatre, concert hall or opera house

krillion.quip: Palladio's 1585 theatre in Vicenza still has its original painted stage set of streets in false perspective.

rare: National Centre for the Performing Arts

quips.Sydney Opera House: Its shells came from a 'spherical solution', every curve cut from the surface of one sphere.
quips.Palais Garnier: An underground water tank beneath it inspired the lake in The Phantom of the Opera.
quips.Epidaurus: Its acoustics are so good that a coin dropped on the stage can be heard in the back rows.
quips.Elbphilharmonie: Its main hall is lined with about 10,000 uniquely shaped gypsum panels that scatter sound.

chapters.text: Name a decorative motif or ornament

krillion.quip: Interlaced curving bands, as on banknotes and Fabergé eggs, where engraved guilloche makes forgery much harder.

quips.Acanthus: Legend says the Corinthian capital was inspired by acanthus leaves growing around a basket on a girl's grave.
quips.Green Man: A face made of leaves, carved in hundreds of medieval churches across Europe.
quips.Fleur-de-lis: A stylised lily long used as a symbol of French royalty.
quips.Egg and dart: A classical moulding that alternates egg shapes with arrowheads.

chapters.text: Name an art or design term

krillion.quip: Leonardo's smoky blending of tones with no hard outlines, Italian for 'evaporated like smoke'.

quips.Chiaroscuro: Italian for light-dark, the strong contrast Caravaggio pushed to theatrical extremes.
quips.Pentimento: Italian for repentance: an earlier layer that shows through after the artist changed their mind.
quips.Contrapposto: The relaxed stance with weight on one leg that makes Michelangelo's David look alive.
quips.Kerning: Adjusting the gap between particular pairs of letters, like A and V.

chapters.text: Name an iconic design object

krillion.quip: It was invented in 1932 by George Carwardine, a car-suspension engineer who based its balancing springs on human arm muscles.

quips.Coca-Cola bottle: Designed in 1915 to be recognisable even if felt in the dark or found broken on the ground.
quips.Juicy Salif: Starck's spider-legged lemon squeezer was sketched on a restaurant napkin over a plate of squid.
quips.Panton Chair: The first chair moulded from a single piece of plastic.
quips.London Underground map: Harry Beck drew it in his spare time in 1931, borrowing ideas from electrical circuit diagrams.

chapters.text: Name a famous historic artefact or treasure

krillion.quip: A 2,000-year-old Greek gear-driven device recovered from a shipwreck that predicted eclipses, sometimes called the first computer.

rare: Imperial Crown of the Holy Roman Empire
deepcut: Book of the Dead of Hunefer
Gold seal of King of Na

quips.Rosetta Stone: It carries the same decree in hieroglyphs, Demotic and Greek, which unlocked Egyptian writing.
quips.Lewis Chessmen: Carved mostly from walrus ivory, and some rooks are berserkers biting their shields.
quips.Sutton Hoo: A ship burial in Suffolk, found in 1939 just before the Second World War.
quips.Nebra sky disc: A Bronze Age bronze disc with gold suns, moon and stars, often called the oldest known depiction of the cosmos.

chapters.text: Name a style of neckline, collar, sleeve, cuff or hem

krillion.quip: A wide, flat cape-like collar that was the height of Victorian evening fashion and returned in the 1940s.

quips.Peter Pan collar: Named after the costume Maude Adams wore playing Peter Pan on Broadway in 1905.
quips.Leg-of-mutton sleeve: Puffed huge at the shoulder and tight at the wrist, it peaked in the 1830s and again in the 1890s.
quips.Ruff: Elizabethan ruffs needed starch and hot poking sticks to keep their figure-eight folds.
quips.Raglan sleeve: Named after Lord Raglan, said to have worn the style after losing an arm at Waterloo.

chapters.text: Name a term from heraldry (coats of arms)

krillion.quip: A diagonal band running from the bearer's top left; despite the myth, it was rarely used as a sign of illegitimacy.

quips.Gules: Heraldic red, possibly from an old word for red-dyed fur used on collars.
quips.Ermine: Its black spots stand for the black tail tips of stoat fur.
quips.Martlet: A legless bird, because people once believed swifts and martins never landed.
quips.Pelican in her piety: A pelican pecking its breast to feed its young with blood, a medieval symbol of sacrifice.

chapters.text: Name a famous mural, fresco, mosaic, tapestry or stained-glass work

krillion.quip: A set of seven late-Gothic tapestries, now at The Cloisters in New York, that even shows the plants accurately enough to identify by species.

schooler: My God, Help Me to Survive This Deadly Love
rare: Allegory of Good and Bad Government
Expulsion from the Garden of Eden
deepcut: Dream of a Sunday Afternoon in the Alameda Central

quips.Bayeux Tapestry: It is actually an embroidery, about 70 metres long, stitched in wool on linen.
quips.The Last Supper: Leonardo experimented with tempera on dry plaster, so it began flaking within his lifetime.
quips.Sistine Chapel ceiling: Michelangelo painted it standing on scaffolding he designed, not lying on his back.
quips.Detroit Industry Murals: Diego Rivera painted 27 panels at the Detroit Institute of Arts in 1932-33.

chapters.text: Name a famous designer (graphic, product, interior or type)

krillion.quip: She co-designed with her husband Massimo, but her name was often left off their joint work, including famous Knoll interiors.

quips.Dieter Rams: His ten principles of good design end with 'as little design as possible'.
quips.Milton Glaser: He sketched the I Love NY logo in the back of a taxi and did the job for free.
quips.Harry Beck: He was paid ten guineas for the Tube map that now defines London.
quips.Raymond Loewy: He redesigned the Lucky Strike pack and the Shell logo, and worked on interiors for NASA's Skylab.

packs.name: Cars
packs.tagline: 21 laps · supercars, pit lanes and petrol heads

chapters.text: Name a supercar or hypercar (make and model)

krillion.quip: A 1990s American supercar styled like a fighter jet; only a couple dozen were ever built.

quips.W Motors Lykan HyperSport: Built by a Dubai-based company, it famously jumped between skyscrapers in Furious 7.
quips.Laraki Epitome: A Moroccan hypercar, from a company founded by a yacht designer in Casablanca.
quips.Devel Sixteen: A Dubai-built hypercar that boasts a 5,000-horsepower V16 concept engine.

chapters.text: Name an F1 constructor (team), past or present

krillion.quip: Italian team Life entered 1990 with a W12 engine and never once got past pre-qualifying.

quips.Brawn GP: Raced one season, 2009, and won both world championships before becoming Mercedes.
quips.Andrea Moda: Its boss was arrested at the 1992 Belgian GP, ending one of F1's strangest teams.
quips.Hesketh: A British lord's team that ran without sponsors and gave James Hunt his first F1 win.

chapters.text: Name a Ferrari model (any car Ferrari has built)

krillion.quip: A practical-ish 1980s Ferrari with four seats, often called the least-loved Prancing Horse.

quips.Ferrari Purosangue: Ferrari insists its four-door Purosangue is not an SUV, despite how it looks.
quips.Ferrari FF: Ferrari's first four-wheel-drive car, a V12 shooting brake built for snowy ski trips.
quips.Ferrari F80: Ferrari's 2024 hypercar successor to LaFerrari, limited to 799 cars.

chapters.text: Name a Ford model, past or present

krillion.quip: Meant to replace the Mustang in the late 80s; fan outrage saved the Mustang instead.

quips.Ford Edsel: Launched in 1958 with huge hype, its name became shorthand for a product flop.
quips.Ford Model T: Over 15 million were built; Henry Ford quipped any colour, so long as it's black.
quips.Ford Quadricycle: Henry Ford's very first vehicle (1896), steered with a tiller and riding on bike wheels.

chapters.text: Name a character from the Fast & Furious films

krillion.quip: One of Dom's original crew in 2001, he simply vanished from the series afterwards.

quips.Han Lue: Han first appeared in Tokyo Drift, so his timeline got famously twisted in later films.
quips.Mia Toretto: Dom's little sister, played by Jordana Brewster since the 2001 original.
quips.Abuelita Toretto: Dom's grandmother, played by Rita Moreno in Fast X.

chapters.text: Name a road sign or road marking

krillion.quip: Those striped chevron boxes in the road; drivers should not enter them unless it's safe.

quips.Belisha beacon: The flashing orange globe at UK zebra crossings, named after a 1930s transport minister.
quips.Camel crossing: A real warning sign on UAE and Saudi desert roads; hitting a camel is very dangerous.

chapters.text: Name a motorsport term

krillion.quip: Bits of worn tyre rubber off the racing line; drive on them and grip vanishes.

Lights out: Lights out and away we go

quips.Undercut: Pitting earlier than a rival so your fresh tyres let you leapfrog them.
quips.Porpoising: Ground-effect cars bounced violently at speed in 2022, like a porpoise leaping.
quips.Multi-21: Red Bull's 2013 coded team order that Vettel famously ignored to pass Webber.

chapters.text: Name a Toyota model, past or present

krillion.quip: Japan's hand-built chauffeur limo, used by the Imperial family and rarely sold abroad.

quips.Toyota AE86: The 1980s Corolla hero of Initial D, adored by drifters as the Hachi-Roku (eight-six).
quips.Toyota Hilux: Top Gear famously failed to destroy one, even after parking it on a building that was demolished.
quips.Toyota Land Cruiser 70: Still built decades after launch; a favourite across Gulf deserts and African bush.

chapters.text: Name a Mercedes-Benz or BMW model

krillion.quip: A bubble car with a fridge-style front door; it helped keep BMW afloat in the 1950s.

quips.Mercedes-Benz Unimog: A go-anywhere workhorse truck; the name is a German abbreviation for universal motor device.
quips.BMW 2002: The small sports saloon of 1968 that basically invented the BMW 3 Series formula.
quips.Mercedes-Benz Patent-Motorwagen: Karl Benz's 1886 three-wheeler, widely called the first true automobile.

chapters.text: Name a type of car engine or engine layout

krillion.quip: The rotary engine spins a triangular rotor instead of pistons; Mazda's RX-7 made it famous.

quips.Hemi: Named for its half-sphere combustion chambers; Chrysler's 426 Hemi was nicknamed the Elephant.
quips.W16: Bugatti's W16 is essentially two narrow V8s joined on one crankshaft, with four turbos.
quips.Desmodromic: Ducati's valve system closes valves mechanically instead of using springs.

chapters.text: Name a tyre brand

krillion.quip: A Finnish brand that claims to have invented the winter tyre back in 1934.

quips.Michelin: The Michelin Man is called Bibendum, and the brand's restaurant guide began as a tyre promo.
quips.Hoosier: An American brand that makes grippy racing slicks for drag strips, NASCAR and track days.
quips.Pirelli: Sole tyre supplier to Formula 1 since 2011, colour-coding each compound on the sidewall.

chapters.text: Name a film about racing or driving

krillion.quip: Spielberg's first feature: a driver hunted by a faceless truck, made for TV in 1971.

deepcut: Lamborghini: The Man Behind the Legend
Tucker: The Man and His Dream
The Art of Racing in the Rain

Talladega Nights: Talladega Nights: The Ballad of Ricky Bobby

quips.Ford v Ferrari: Released as Le Mans '66 in the UK, it retells Ford's 1966 one-two-three at Le Mans.
quips.Bullitt: Steve McQueen's Mustang chase through San Francisco set the bar for movie car chases.
quips.The World's Fastest Indian: Anthony Hopkins plays Burt Munro, who set a land-speed record on a 1920 motorcycle.

chapters.text: Name an American muscle car or pony car

krillion.quip: AMC's 1970 muscle car came painted red, white and blue straight from the factory.

deepcut: Ford Mustang King of the Road

quips.Pontiac GTO: Often credited as the first true muscle car (1964); its name was borrowed from Ferrari.
quips.Buick GNX: An all-black turbo V6 Buick from 1987 that out-accelerated many supercars of its day.
quips.Plymouth Superbird: Its huge rear wing and pointed nose were built to win NASCAR superspeedway races.

chapters.text: Name a racing series or motorsport championship

krillion.quip: An annual showdown where F1, rally and NASCAR stars race head to head in identical cars.

quips.Dakar Rally: Born as Paris to Dakar in 1978, it now runs across Saudi Arabia's deserts.
quips.Group B: 1980s rally's wildest era; the cars were so fast the class was banned after 1986.
quips.Lawn mower racing: A real British championship, including a 12-hour endurance race for ride-on mowers.

chapters.text: Name a carmaker that no longer exists

krillion.quip: Preston Tucker's futuristic 1948 sedan had a swivelling third headlight; only 51 were built.

quips.Edsel: Ford's 1958 brand flopped so badly that Edsel became a byword for failure.
quips.Trabant: East Germany's people's car had a body made from Duroplast, a cotton-reinforced plastic.
quips.Saab: Born from a Swedish aircraft maker, Saab even mounted the ignition key between the front seats.

chapters.text: Name a real person a car brand or racing team is named after

krillion.quip: The Mercedes brand is named after the 10-year-old daughter of a Daimler dealer, Emil Jellinek.

quips.Abraham Lincoln: Henry Leland named his Lincoln company after the president he had voted for.
quips.Chief Pontiac: Pontiac cars took their name from an 18th-century Ottawa leader, via the Michigan city.
quips.Antoine de la Mothe Cadillac: Cadillac is named after the French explorer who founded Detroit in 1701.

chapters.text: Name a rally driver, past or present

krillion.quip: An Emirati driver who raced works Ford and Citroen cars in the World Rally Championship.

quips.Mohammed Ben Sulayem: The Emirati won the Middle East Rally Championship 14 times and later became FIA president.
quips.Michele Mouton: In 1981 she became the first woman to win a World Rally Championship round.
quips.Roger Feghali: Lebanon's rally hero, a many-time winner of the Rally of Lebanon.

chapters.text: Name a NASCAR or IndyCar driver, past or present

krillion.quip: In 1977 she became the first woman to race in both the Indy 500 and the Daytona 500.

quips.Wendell Scott: In 1963 he became the first Black driver to win a race in NASCAR's top series.
quips.Shane van Gisbergen: The New Zealander won on his very first NASCAR Cup start, at Chicago's street race in 2023.
quips.Danica Patrick: In 2008 she became the first woman to win an IndyCar race, at Motegi in Japan.

chapters.text: Name a Volkswagen, Audi or Porsche model

krillion.quip: The boxy Type 181 was built for the West German army, then sold in the US as the Thing.

quips.Volkswagen Beetle: More than 21 million original Beetles were built, the last one in Mexico in 2003.
quips.Audi Quattro: Its four-wheel drive revolutionised rallying in the 1980s and gave Audi its famous badge word.
quips.Porsche 917: The 917 won Porsche its first overall Le Mans victory in 1970.

chapters.text: Name a car-modding or car-culture term

krillion.quip: Japanese street styling with towering exhaust pipes, huge spoilers and wild paint.

quips.Hajwala: Gulf street-drifting culture, famous for sedans sliding sideways at highway speed.
quips.Sidewall drifting: A Saudi stunt where passengers change a tyre while the car drives on two wheels.
quips.Sleeper: A plain-looking car hiding huge power, built to surprise everyone at the lights.

chapters.text: Name a classic British car (make and model)

krillion.quip: A wedge-shaped orange 1970s three-wheeler with a lift-up canopy instead of doors.

quips.DeLorean DMC-12: The Back to the Future car was built in Northern Ireland, near Belfast, in the early 1980s.
quips.Peel P50: Built on the Isle of Man, it is the smallest production car ever, with no reverse gear.
quips.Austin Allegro: Infamous for its 'Quartic' square steering wheel and a reputation for rusting.

packs.tagline: 21 toons · drawn out of the deep

chapters.text: Name a Disney princess or heroine

krillion.quip: Eilonwy from The Black Cauldron (1985) is one of Disney's most forgotten princesses.

quips.Kida: Kida Nedakh is a princess in Atlantis: The Lost Empire (2001).

chapters.text: Name a Disney or Pixar villain

krillion.quip: Mim battles Merlin in a wizard's duel in The Sword in the Stone by turning into animals.

quips.Chernabog: Chernabog's mountain-top scene in Fantasia was animated by Vladimir Tytla.

chapters.text: Name a Pixar character

krillion.quip: Riley's imaginary friend Bing Bong is part elephant, part cat, part dolphin, and made of cotton candy.

quips.Boo: Boo's real name is Mary Gibbs.

chapters.text: Name a DreamWorks Animation film

krillion.a: Sinbad: Legend of the Seven Seas

Wallace & Gromit: The Curse of the Were-Rabbit
How to Train Your Dragon: The Hidden World

quips.Antz: Antz (1998) was the first DreamWorks Animation feature.

chapters.text: Name a Hanna-Barbera cartoon or character

krillion.quip: Hong Kong Phooey was a janitor dog who secretly fought crime from a filing cabinet.

rare: Help! It's the Hair Bear Bunch
Captain Caveman and the Teen Angels

quips.Hong Kong Phooey: His secret identity is Penrod Pooch, mild-mannered janitor.

chapters.text: Name a cartoon dog

krillion.quip: Courage lives in the middle of Nowhere, Kansas, and is terrified of nearly everything.

quips.Dogmatix: Dogmatix is Obelix's tiny dog in the Asterix comics.

chapters.text: Name a cartoon cat

krillion.quip: Hanna-Barbera's Mr. Jinks was forever chasing Pixie and Dixie, two talking mice.

quips.Felix the Cat: Felix became one of the first cartoon stars of the silent film era.

chapters.text: Name an animation studio

krillion.quip: This Irish studio made Song of the Sea and Wolfwalkers in hand-drawn style.

quips.Aardman: Aardman is the Bristol studio behind Wallace & Gromit and Shaun the Sheep.

chapters.text: Name a cartoon bird

krillion.quip: Merlin's talking owl in The Sword in the Stone is named Archimedes.

quips.Opus: Opus the Penguin starred in Berkeley Breathed's comic strip Bloom County.

chapters.text: Name a Disney sidekick

krillion.quip: Cri-Kee is Mulan's tiny lucky cricket, who is not quite as lucky as promised.

quips.Pumbaa: Pumbaa's name means 'foolish' or 'simpleton' in Swahili.

chapters.text: Name a character from The Lion King

krillion.quip: Sarafina is Nala's mother and a lioness of the Pride Lands.

quips.Scar: Scar's birth name, revealed later in The Lion Guard, is Taka.

chapters.text: Name a villain from a TV cartoon

krillion.quip: Mumm-Ra the Ever-Living is the mummy sorcerer who hunts the ThunderCats.

quips.Gargamel: Gargamel's cat is named Azrael and he is obsessed with catching Smurfs.

chapters.text: Name a cartoon robot or alien

krillion.quip: Gir is Invader Zim's malfunctioning SIR unit who loves tacos and waffles.

quips.Astro Boy: Astro Boy debuted in manga in 1952 and became Japan's first popular TV anime.

chapters.text: Name a 1980s or 1990s Saturday-morning cartoon

krillion.quip: Bucky O'Hare was a green space-rabbit captain of the starship Righteous Indignation.

rare: Where on Earth Is Carmen Sandiego
Wild West C.O.W.-Boys of Moo Mesa

He-Man: He-Man and the Masters of the Universe
G.I. Joe: G.I. Joe: A Real American Hero
Gummi Bears: Disney's Adventures of the Gummi Bears
Bucky O'Hare: Bucky O'Hare and the Toad Wars

quips.DuckTales: The 1987 DuckTales theme song is one of the most remembered intros in TV history.

chapters.text: Name a character from the Mickey Mouse or Donald Duck universe

krillion.quip: Gyro Gearloose is Duckburg's genius inventor, helped by his tiny Little Helper.

quips.Oswald the Lucky Rabbit: Walt Disney created Oswald before Mickey, then lost the rights and invented Mickey.

chapters.text: Name a character from Peanuts

krillion.quip: Tapioca Pudding is a Peanuts character who shows up in the comic strip's later years.

quips.Woodstock: Woodstock is named after the 1969 music festival and speaks in little tick marks.

krillion.quip: Leatherhead is a mutated alligator who becomes a swamp-dwelling ally of the Turtles.

quips.Krang: Krang is an alien brain who speaks from an android body in the 1987 cartoon.

krillion.quip: Painter Smurf is the village artist who often prefers his own masterpieces to anyone else's.

krillion.quip: Basil is the mouse Sherlock Holmes of Disney's The Great Mouse Detective (1986).

quips.Speedy Gonzales: Speedy Gonzales was once banned in some places for supposed stereotypes, but fans fought to bring him back.

chapters.text: Name a cartoon monster or ghost

krillion.quip: Oblina, from Aaahh!!! Real Monsters, is a striped monster who lives in a city dump.

quips.Casper: Casper first appeared in a 1945 Famous Studios cartoon before getting his own comic series.

packs.name: Planet Earth
packs.tagline: 21 wonders · rock, rain and rumble

chapters.text: Name a geological era, period or epoch

krillion.quip: The last period before the Cambrian, home to the first large complex life.

chapters.text: Name a biome or habitat

krillion.quip: The world's largest land biome, a belt of conifer forest around the far north.

chapters.text: Name a type of precipitation or frozen water

krillion.quip: Soft, crumbly pellets of snow coated in frozen cloud droplets.

chapters.text: Name a metal or alloy

krillion.quip: Heavy, brittle and rainbow-tinted, it is almost as dense as lead but far less toxic.

chapters.text: Name one of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World, or a natural wonder

krillion.quip: About 40,000 interlocking basalt columns formed by an ancient lava flow.

chapters.text: Name a volcano or plate-tectonics term

krillion.quip: A huge basin left when a volcano's magma chamber empties and the summit collapses.

chapters.text: Name a mountain in the Himalayas or Karakoram

krillion.quip: Known as 'Hidden Peak', the 11th-highest mountain in the world.

chapters.text: Name a famous canyon, gorge or valley

krillion.quip: A deep gorge on China's Jinsha River, named for a tiger said to have leapt across it.

chapters.text: Name a plateau, steppe or grassland region

krillion.quip: A vast high Andean plateau shared by Bolivia and Peru, home to Lake Titicaca.

chapters.text: Name a geyser, hot spring or thermal area

krillion.quip: This Icelandic geyser erupts like clockwork every 5 to 10 minutes.

chapters.text: Name a type of soil, sand or sediment

krillion.quip: Fine wind-blown silt that forms some of the world's most fertile farmland.

chapters.text: Name a famous meteorite or impact crater

krillion.quip: The Yucatan crater from the asteroid that helped end the age of the dinosaurs.

chapters.text: Name a famous fossil, fossil site or fossil find

krillion.quip: A Newfoundland cliff holding some of the oldest large complex fossils, around 565 million years old.

chapters.text: Name a polar or ice-related term

krillion.quip: A mountain peak poking up through a surrounding ice sheet, from the Inuit word for 'lonely peak'.

chapters.text: Name a cave formation or karst feature

krillion.quip: A twisting cave formation that seems to ignore gravity, growing in every direction.

chapters.text: Name a famous volcanic eruption or earthquake

krillion.quip: A 1783 Icelandic fissure eruption that darkened skies across Europe and killed a fifth of Iceland's people.

chapters.text: Name an animal that lives in the Arctic or Antarctic

krillion.quip: It can stand on its hind legs and hop like a kangaroo to move fast.

chapters.text: Name an animal that lives in the desert

krillion.quip: The smallest fox, with huge ears that radiate heat and hear prey underground.

chapters.text: Name a mountain pass

krillion.quip: Slovenia's highest road pass, climbing through 50 numbered hairpin bends.

schooler: Col de la Croix de Fer

chapters.text: Name a natural resource that is mined or drilled

krillion.quip: Potassium-rich salts dug from the ground that are crucial for fertiliser.

chapters.text: Name a river delta, estuary or river mouth

krillion.quip: The world's largest mangrove forest sits in this Ganges-Brahmaputra delta.

packs.name: Fashion & Style
packs.tagline: 21 runway riddles · Dress to impress, answer to obscure

chapters.text: Name a piece of jewellery

krillion.quip: An ornamental braided cord with metal tips, worn on military dress uniforms over the shoulder.

quips.Torc: Celtic neck rings of twisted metal were open at the front.
quips.Claddagh Ring: It shows two hands holding a crowned heart, from a fishing village near Galway.
quips.Mood Ring: Mood rings use thermochromic liquid crystals that change colour with temperature.
quips.Netsuke: Small carved toggles that held pouches to the sash of a kimono.

chapters.text: Name a type of coat or jacket

krillion.quip: A loose 19th-century overcoat; its name survives as the everyday French word for a cardigan or coat.

quips.Mackintosh: Named after Charles Macintosh, who patented rubberised waterproof fabric in 1823.
quips.Cardigan: Named after the 7th Earl of Cardigan, who led the Charge of the Light Brigade.
quips.Mackinaw: Named after Mackinac in Michigan, where heavy wool coats were traded in 1811.

chapters.text: Name a pattern or print found on clothing

krillion.quip: Named after the woven seat fabric on London buses and Tube trains, now a cult print.

quips.Paisley: Named after the Scottish town of Paisley, a hub of shawl weaving in the 1800s.
quips.Argyle: Derived from the tartan of Clan Campbell of Argyll in western Scotland.
quips.Gingham: Its name likely comes from the Malay word genggang, meaning striped.

chapters.text: Name a type of top or shirt

krillion.quip: A tightly knitted fisherman's sweater from the Channel Island of Guernsey, nearly windproof.

quips.T-shirt: Named for its T shape; the US Navy issued them as undershirts around 1913.
quips.Henley: Named after the rowing uniforms worn at Henley-on-Thames.
quips.Aran Sweater: From the Aran Islands off Ireland, with cable patterns said to represent fishing ropes.

chapters.text: Name a makeup or beauty product

krillion.quip: Used in ancient Egypt around the eyes, partly to reduce sun glare and deter flies.

quips.Mascara: Modern mascara took off after Maybelline began selling a cake version in 1917.
quips.Lipstick: Ancient Mesopotamians crushed gemstones to colour their lips.
quips.Ceruse: This white lead face paint, worn by Elizabeth I, was quietly poisonous.

chapters.text: Name a style or cut of dress

krillion.quip: An 18th-century gown with the skirt looped up into three puffs, said to be Polish-inspired.

quips.Little Black Dress: Vogue compared Chanel's 1926 black dress to a Ford car for its simplicity.
quips.Delphos Gown: Mariano Fortuny's finely pleated silk gown of 1907 was inspired by ancient Greek statues.
quips.Dirndl: Once Alpine workwear, the apron bow side traditionally signals relationship status.

chapters.text: Name a type of trousers or shorts

krillion.quip: Baggy wide trousers popular with Oxford students in the 1920s, some over 40 inches round the hem.

quips.Jodhpurs: Named after the Indian city of Jodhpur, where the riding style was adopted by British polo players.
quips.Capri Pants: Popularised on the Italian island of Capri in the 1950s.
quips.Bermuda Shorts: Adopted as respectable office wear in Bermuda, worn with knee socks and a blazer.

chapters.text: Name a neckline or collar style

krillion.quip: Starched pleated collars in the 1500s grew so wide that special long spoons were said to be needed to eat.

quips.Peter Pan Collar: Named after the costume worn by Maude Adams in a 1905 Broadway Peter Pan.
quips.Bardot: Named after actress Brigitte Bardot, who often wore off-shoulder tops.
quips.Henley: Named after the rowing uniforms of Henley-on-Thames in England.

chapters.text: Name a type of skirt

krillion.quip: A 1910s skirt so narrow at the ankle that wearers could only take tiny shuffling steps.

quips.Mini Skirt: Mary Quant popularised it in 1960s London and named it after her favourite car, the Mini.
quips.Farthingale: A hooped underskirt from 15th-century Spain that spread across European courts.
quips.Poodle Skirt: Felt circle skirts with poodle appliques were a 1950s American teen craze.

chapters.text: Name a style of beard or moustache

krillion.quip: A wide, full beard with a rounded bottom, named after Italian hero Giuseppe Garibaldi.

quips.Sideburns: Named after Union general Ambrose Burnside; the word was reversed over time.
quips.Van Dyke: Named after 17th-century Flemish painter Anthony van Dyck.
quips.Balbo: Named after Italian aviator Italo Balbo.

chapters.text: Name a scent or ingredient used in perfume

krillion.quip: A waxy substance from sperm whales that can float in the sea for years before washing ashore.

quips.Calone: Discovered by Pfizer in 1966, its sea-breeze smell defined 1990s fresh perfumes.
quips.Orris: Made from iris roots that must be dried for up to five years before use.
quips.Iso E Super: A synthetic woody note so subtle that some people cannot smell it at all.

chapters.text: Name a traditional garment from anywhere in the world

krillion.quip: A long, sheer linen sheath dress worn in ancient Egypt, sometimes pleated.

quips.Gho: Bhutanese men must wear this knee-length robe in schools and government offices.
quips.Barong Tagalog: This sheer embroidered shirt is the national dress of the Philippines, often woven from pineapple fibre.
quips.Lopapeysa: The Icelandic yoked sweater is knitted from unspun lopi wool.

chapters.text: Name a style of sleeve

krillion.quip: A huge leg-of-mutton sleeve of the 1830s and 1890s, named from the French word for a leg of lamb.

quips.Raglan Sleeve: Named after Lord Raglan, who lost his arm at Waterloo and wanted an easier coat sleeve.
quips.Bishop Sleeve: Named for its resemblance to the full sleeves of Anglican bishops' robes.
quips.Kimono Sleeve: It is cut in one piece with the body, with no shoulder seam at all.

chapters.text: Name a hair accessory or hair-styling tool

krillion.quip: Ornamental Japanese hairpins; their style once showed a geisha apprentice's rank and the season.

quips.Scrunchie: Patented in 1987 by singer Rommy Revson, who named it after her poodle Scunchie.
quips.Bobby Pin: Named after the bobbed haircuts of the 1920s that needed holding in place.
quips.Marcel Iron: Parisian hairdresser Marcel Grateau's 1872 heated tongs created the Marcel wave.

chapters.text: Name a sewing, knitting or embroidery stitch

krillion.quip: A laid-and-couched stitch used to fill the figures on the 70-metre Bayeux Tapestry.

quips.French Knot: Despite the name, it was used across Europe and is not especially French.
quips.Opus Anglicanum: Medieval English embroidery so prized that popes collected it.
quips.Smocking: Gathering fabric with stitches let farm workers' smocks stretch without buttons.

chapters.text: Name a type of fastening or closure on clothing

krillion.quip: A looped braided-cord fastener seen on Chinese jackets and military uniforms.

quips.Zip: B.F. Goodrich coined the name 'zipper' in 1923 for rubber boots fastened with it.
quips.Velcro: Invented by George de Mestral after burrs stuck to his dog on a hike.
quips.Aglet: The plastic or metal tip on a shoelace; it stops the end from fraying.

chapters.text: Name a fashion subculture, aesthetic or style movement

krillion.quip: Members of La Sape in Brazzaville and Kinshasa, famed for wearing immaculate, colourful designer suits.

quips.Macaroni: Fashionable 1760s Englishmen with towering wigs, mocked in the song Yankee Doodle.
quips.Incroyables: Post-Revolution Parisian dandies who dropped the letter R from their speech.
quips.Teddy Boy: 1950s British youths revived Edwardian tailoring, hence the name Teddy.

chapters.text: Name something worn on the head that isn't a hat

krillion.quip: A tall, often jewelled Russian headdress whose shape inspired tiaras worn by royal families.

quips.Tiara: The word originally meant a Persian royal headdress.
quips.Gele: Elaborate Nigerian head wraps tied from stiff fabric for weddings and celebrations.
quips.Hennin: A tall cone headdress of 15th-century Burgundy, now the classic fairy-tale princess hat.

chapters.text: Name a part of a piece of clothing

krillion.quip: The opening at a shirt front or cuff, reinforced to hold buttons, from an old word for a slit in a petticoat.

quips.Gusset: A small diamond or triangle of fabric sewn in to add room and strength.
quips.Selvedge: The self-finished edge of woven cloth; 'self-edge' is where the word comes from.
quips.Arcuate: The curved double stitch on Levi's back pockets, used since 1873.

chapters.text: Name something worn around the neck

krillion.quip: A cascade of lace or frills at the throat; judges in some countries still wear one with their robes.

quips.Cravat: Named after Croatian mercenaries whose knotted neckcloths impressed 17th-century Paris.
quips.Woggle: The ring that holds a Scout neckerchief together.
quips.Lei: Hawaiian garlands of flowers, shells or feathers, given as a sign of affection.

chapters.text: Name a fashion word borrowed from French

krillion.quip: Decorative braid, tassels and cord trimmings; the craft has its own Paris guild dating back centuries.

quips.Denim: From serge de Nîmes, a sturdy twill fabric from the French city of Nîmes.
quips.Lingerie: From linge, the French word for linen.
quips.Silhouette: Named after Étienne de Silhouette, a stingy 1759 finance minister linked to cheap paper cut-out portraits.

packs.name: Football
packs.tagline: 21 fixtures · from the terraces to the trophy cabinet

chapters.text: Name a country that has played at a men's World Cup

krillion.quip: Today's Indonesia played one World Cup match in 1938, losing 6-0 to Hungary.

quips.Curacao: The Caribbean island of about 150,000 people qualified for the expanded 2026 World Cup.
quips.Iceland: At Euro 2016 and the 2018 World Cup, its fans' Viking thunderclap became famous worldwide.
quips.Kuwait: At the 1982 World Cup, a Kuwaiti sheikh walked onto the pitch to protest a French goal.

chapters.text: Name a position or role on a football team

krillion.quip: German for 'space interpreter', a role Thomas Muller invented to describe himself.

quips.Libero: Italian for 'free', the libero roamed behind the defence, a role Franz Beckenbauer perfected.
quips.Regista: Italian for 'director': a deep playmaker like Andrea Pirlo who directs the play.
quips.Trequartista: Italian for 'three-quarters', the creator who lives between midfield and attack.

chapters.text: Name a Spanish football club

krillion.quip: Founded in 1889 by British mining workers, it is Spain's oldest football club.

quips.Athletic Bilbao: Famous for fielding only players from the Basque region, yet never relegated from La Liga.
quips.Villarreal: A town of about 50,000 people whose club reached a Champions League semi-final and won the 2021 Europa League.
quips.Eibar: From a Basque town of just 27,000, Eibar spent seven seasons in La Liga.

chapters.text: Name a team from Italy's Serie A, past or present

krillion.quip: Seven-time Italian champions before 1923, from a town of about 45,000 people.

quips.Genoa: Founded by Englishmen in 1893, Italy's oldest club still spells its name the English way.
quips.Chievo: A tiny Verona suburb club nicknamed the Flying Donkeys, it spent 17 seasons in Serie A.
quips.Atalanta: Once a yo-yo club from Bergamo, Atalanta won the Europa League in 2024.

chapters.text: Name the nickname of a national football team

krillion.quip: Lebanon's national team takes its nickname from the cedar tree on the country's flag.

quips.Socceroos: A blend of 'soccer' and 'kangaroo', coined by an Australian journalist in 1967.
quips.Bafana Bafana: Zulu for 'the boys, the boys', the rallying cry of South Africa's team.
quips.Al-Nashama: Jordan's nickname means the gallant ones; the team reached the Asian Cup final in 2024.

chapters.text: Name a famous football manager or coach

krillion.quip: Legend says he cursed Benfica in 1962, saying they'd never win in Europe again without him.

quips.Brian Clough: He won back-to-back European Cups with unfashionable Nottingham Forest in 1979 and 1980.
quips.Walid Regragui: Led Morocco to the 2022 World Cup semi-finals, a first for an African or Arab nation.

chapters.text: Name a club from France or Monaco

quips.Saint-Etienne: Les Verts reached the 1976 European Cup final and still wear famous green shirts.
quips.Olympique Lyonnais Feminin: Lyon's women's team has won the Women's Champions League a record eight times.

chapters.text: Name a famous goalkeeper, past or present

quips.Lev Yashin: The Black Spider is the only goalkeeper to win the Ballon d'Or, in 1963.
quips.Rene Higuita: Famous for his 'scorpion kick' save against England at Wembley in 1995.
quips.Bert Trautmann: Played on in the 1956 FA Cup final with a broken neck and still won.

chapters.text: Name a team from South America's top leagues

krillion.quip: A Bolivian club from La Paz, playing home games about 3,600 metres above sea level.

chapters.text: Name a football competition, cup or league

quips.Homeless World Cup: An annual street-football tournament for people who have experienced homelessness.
quips.Watney Cup: A short 1970s English cup that pioneered the penalty shootout in English football.

chapters.text: Name a club that has appeared in the European Cup or Champions League

krillion.quip: In 2018 the Luxembourg club became the first from its country to reach a European group stage.

quips.Celtic: In 1967 the Lisbon Lions became the first British club to win the European Cup, all born near Glasgow.
quips.Steaua Bucharest: In 1986 Steaua won the European Cup after their keeper saved all four Barcelona penalties.
quips.Sheriff Tiraspol: The Moldovan side stunned Real Madrid 2-1 at the Bernabeu in 2021.

chapters.text: Name a Scottish football team

krillion.quip: A Glasgow club that won the Scottish title in 1904, then went bust in 1967.

quips.Dundee United: Nicknamed the Arabs, after fans joked their sandy pitch in the 1960s looked like a desert.
quips.Queen's Park: Scotland's oldest club stayed amateur until 2019 and still owns Hampden Park's history.
quips.Gretna: A tiny border-village club that reached the Scottish Premier League in 2007, then folded a year later.

quips.Krakoa: Once an X-Men villain, the living island later became a nation for all mutants.
quips.Forge: A mutant inventor who can intuitively build any machine he imagines.
quips.Namor: Often called Marvel's first mutant, debuting all the way back in 1939.

krillion.quip: A Superman foe who believes he is the villain from an old movie serial come to life.

quips.Dex-Starr: A blue house cat who became a Red Lantern after his owner was murdered.
quips.Mister Mxyzptlk: The fifth-dimensional imp vanishes if tricked into saying his name backwards.

chapters.text: Name a superhero sidekick

krillion.quip: A finger-snapping teen who was the Justice League's honorary member in 1960.

quips.Bat-Mite: A magical imp from another dimension who idolises Batman and constantly 'helps'.
quips.Tippy-Toe: Squirrel Girl's squirrel sidekick, wearer of a tiny pink bow.
quips.Woozy Winks: Plastic Man's bumbling sidekick, cursed so that nature itself protects him from harm.

quips.Inferior Five: DC's 1960s parody team, led by Merryman, the self-declared 'weakest man in the world'.

quips.Donald Blake: Thor was first hidden inside a frail doctor who turned into the god by striking his cane.
quips.John Jones: The Martian Manhunter's human cover: a hard-boiled Middletown police detective.
quips.Penrod Pooch: The mild janitor who leaps into a filing cabinet to become Hong Kong Phooey.

krillion.quip: Domino and the Scarlet Witch bend luck itself so the odds break their way.
