quips.Echolocation: Daredevil 'sees' with a radar sense, mapping the room from tiny echoes of sound.
quips.Super breath: Golden Age Superman once blew out a star with a single puff.
quips.Retractable claws: Wolverine's bone claws were coated in unbreakable adamantium by the Weapon X program.

quips.Superman: Its 1978 tagline promised 'You'll believe a man can fly'.

packs.name: Holidays & Traditions
packs.tagline: 21 festive dives · from Krampus to Kanpai

chapters.text: Name something associated with Christmas

krillion.quip: A Catalan log with a painted face that children 'feed' then beat with sticks until it poops out sweets.

quips.Yule Goat: The giant straw Gävle Goat in Sweden has been burned down by vandals dozens of times since 1966.
quips.Caganer: A Catalan nativity figurine shown squatting to relieve himself, hidden in the scene for luck.
quips.Krampus: A horned Alpine figure who punishes naughty children alongside Saint Nicholas.

chapters.text: Name a Halloween costume

krillion.quip: A Welsh horse-skull figure on a pole, traditionally paraded door to door in midwinter rhyme battles.

quips.Turnip Lantern: Before pumpkins, Irish and Scottish children carved scary faces into turnips.
quips.Guising Mask: Scottish 'guisers' went door to door in disguise centuries before American trick-or-treating.
quips.Plague Doctor: The beaked mask was said to hold herbs, though historians doubt it was widely worn.
quips.Day of the Dead Catrina: La Catrina began as a satirical etching by José Guadalupe Posada around 1910.

chapters.text: Name a gift someone might give or receive

krillion.quip: A Norwegian tower of almond rings given at weddings and Christmas, often with a bottle hidden inside.

quips.Red Packet: In China, gift money avoids amounts with the number 4, which sounds like 'death'.
quips.Love Spoon: Welsh suitors carved intricate wooden spoons to show their skill and devotion.
quips.Claddagh Ring: Hands, heart and crown stand for friendship, love and loyalty in this Irish ring.
quips.Orange in the Stocking: Linked to the legend of St Nicholas dropping gold into stockings.

chapters.text: Name something you'd see at a wedding

krillion.quip: At Jewish weddings the couple are hoisted on chairs during the Hora dance, clutching a handkerchief between them.

quips.Breaking the Glass: Jewish grooms stamp on a glass, often said to recall the destruction of the Temple.
quips.Croquembouche: French wedding cake made of a cone of cream puffs bound with caramel.
quips.Jumping the Broom: Popularised among enslaved African Americans when legal marriage was denied to them.
quips.Lazo: A rope or rosary looped around a couple's shoulders in Mexican and Filipino weddings.

chapters.text: Name something associated with Easter

krillion.quip: Polish Easter eggs decorated with wax-resist patterns — the name comes from the word for 'to write'.

quips.Easter Bilby: Australia promotes a chocolate bilby since rabbits are a destructive pest there.
quips.Påskekrim: Norwegians famously read and watch crime thrillers over Easter.
quips.Bells Flying to Rome: In France church bells 'fly to Rome' and return bringing eggs on Easter morning.
quips.Biddenden Dole: A Kent charity has handed out cakes stamped with conjoined twins at Easter for centuries.

chapters.text: Name a food you might serve at a party

krillion.quip: Australian children's party classic: buttered white bread covered in hundreds and thousands.

quips.Cheese Hedgehog: A 1970s British party icon: cheese and pineapple sticks stuck into a foil-wrapped half grapefruit.
quips.Mettigel: A German party dish of raw minced pork shaped like a hedgehog with onion spikes.
quips.Brigadeiros: Brazilian chocolate truffles named after a 1940s presidential candidate, Brigadier Eduardo Gomes.
quips.Devils on Horseback: Bacon-wrapped prunes, the darker sibling of oyster-based angels on horseback.

chapters.text: Name a party decoration or party supply

krillion.quip: Mexican tissue-paper banners cut with chisels into intricate designs — up to 50 sheets at once.

quips.Gragger: A noisemaker spun at Purim whenever the villain Haman's name is read aloud.
quips.Kadomatsu: Japanese New Year arrangement of bamboo and pine placed by doors to welcome spirits.
quips.Rangoli: Coloured powder patterns drawn on floors at Diwali to welcome the goddess Lakshmi.
quips.Diya: Small oil lamps of clay, lit in rows during Diwali, the festival of lights.

krillion.quip: A 16th-century Latin carol that became a surprise UK top-20 hit for Steeleye Span in 1973.

quips.Silent Night: First performed in 1818 in Oberndorf, Austria, with guitar because the organ was broken.
quips.Shchedryk: The Ukrainian New Year song that became the tune of Carol of the Bells.
quips.Six White Boomers: Rolf Harris's Australian carol in which kangaroos pull Santa's sleigh.

chapters.text: Name a dish eaten during a holiday or festival

krillion.quip: Greek New Year cake with a coin baked inside; whoever finds it has luck for the year.

quips.Feast of the Seven Fishes: An Italian-American Christmas Eve dinner of many seafood dishes, from the custom of avoiding meat.
quips.Risalamande: The Danish rice pudding hides one whole almond; the finder wins a prize.
quips.Toshikoshi Soba: Long buckwheat noodles eaten on Japanese New Year's Eve for a long life.
quips.Lutefisk: Dried cod soaked in lye until it turns jelly-like, a Norwegian Christmas staple.

chapters.text: Name a gift-bringer or holiday folklore figure

krillion.quip: A fairy from France's Franche-Comté who brings gifts on a donkey with bells at Christmas.

rare: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come

quips.Befana: An Italian witch who delivers sweets — or coal — on the eve of Epiphany.
quips.Jólakötturinn: Iceland's Yule Cat eats people who didn't get new clothes before Christmas.
quips.Olentzero: A Basque charcoal-burner who comes down from the mountains with Christmas gifts.
quips.Nian: A beast frightened off by red colours and firecrackers, origin of Lunar New Year noise.

krillion.quip: Satoshi Kon's 2003 tale of three homeless people who find an abandoned baby on Christmas Eve.

rare: Beauty and the Beast: The Enchanted Christmas
The Year Without a Santa Claus
Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town
Elf on the Shelf: An Elf's Story
deepcut: Le Père Noël est une ordure

Home Alone 2: Home Alone 2: Lost in New York
The Nightmare Before Christmas: Tim Burton's The Nightmare Before Christmas

quips.Klaus: The 2019 animated film imagines Santa's origin in a feuding Arctic town.
quips.The Irony of Fate: Shown on Russian TV every New Year's Eve since 1976.
quips.Rare Exports: A Finnish horror-comedy in which the real Santa is dug out of a mountain.

chapters.text: Name a good-luck charm or superstition

rare: Getting Out of Bed on the Wrong Side
Pinch Punch First of the Month
Never Say Pig on a Ship

Penny on the Ground: Find a Penny Pick It Up

quips.Glücksschwein: Germans give marzipan pigs at New Year as a symbol of prosperity.
quips.Martenitsa: Bulgarians wear red-and-white threads from 1 March until they see a stork or blossom.
quips.Senbazuru: Folding a thousand paper cranes is said to grant a wish in Japan.

quips.Shivaree: A noisy mock serenade of pots and pans given to newlyweds in rural North America.
quips.Kräftskiva: A Swedish August crayfish party with paper hats, lanterns and drinking songs.
quips.Corroboree: An Aboriginal Australian ceremonial gathering of dance, song and story.
quips.Potlatch: A gift-giving feast of Pacific Northwest peoples, once banned in Canada for decades.

krillion.quip: A wooden barrel-shaped track where motorcyclists ride on vertical walls, a fairground act since the 1910s.

quips.Ferris Wheel: Built for the 1893 Chicago World's Fair to rival the Eiffel Tower.
quips.Coconut Shy: A British fairground game since the 19th century, throwing balls at coconuts on posts.
quips.Ten-in-One: A sideshow tent with ten acts for the price of one ticket.
quips.Zoltar: The fortune-telling machine made famous by the 1988 film Big.

quips.Syttende Mai: Norway's 17 May features children's parades rather than military ones.
quips.Naadam: Mongolia's national festival of wrestling, horse racing and archery.
quips.Tynwald Day: The Isle of Man's parliament meets outdoors on a hill each 5 July, as for over 1,000 years.

chapters.text: Name a traditional garment or festive costume from anywhere in the world

krillion.quip: Norwegian regional folk costumes, worn by most Norwegians on 17 May, each design tied to a valley.

quips.Fez: Named after the city of Fez in Morocco, once the main source of the crimson dye.
quips.Kilt: The modern small kilt is often credited to an 18th-century English industrialist.
quips.Gákti: Sámi garment whose colours and trims reveal the wearer's home region.
quips.Traje de Luces: The 'suit of lights' worn by bullfighters, named for its glittering sequins.

chapters.text: Name a saint with a feast day

krillion.quip: English folklore says if it rains on his feast day, 15 July, it will rain for forty days.

rare: Saint Teresa Benedicta of the Cross

Saint Teresa Benedicta of the Cross: St Teresa Benedicta of the Cross

quips.Saint Lucy: Swedes honour her on 13 December with candle-crowned processions in the darkest season.
quips.Saint Wilgefortis: A legendary saint who prayed to become unmarriageable and grew a beard.
quips.Saint Drogo: Patron saint of coffee-house owners — and of unattractive people.
quips.Saint Fiacre: Patron of gardeners; Paris cabs were called fiacres after an inn bearing his name.

chapters.text: Name a coming-of-age ceremony or rite of passage

krillion.quip: Japan's Coming of Age Day, held each January for young people who have reached adulthood.

quips.Land Diving: On Vanuatu's Pentecost Island, men leap from wooden towers with vines tied to their ankles.
quips.Shinbyu: Burmese boys are dressed as princes before briefly becoming novice monks.
quips.Doljanchi: Korean babies choose objects at their first birthday to 'predict' their future.
quips.Rumspringa: Amish teens get a period of freedom before deciding to be baptised into the church.

quips.Dinner for One: A British comedy sketch shown every New Year's Eve on German TV, though barely known in Britain.
quips.Loony Dook: Edinburgh revellers plunge into the icy Firth of Forth on New Year's Day.
quips.Haft-sin: A Persian Nowruz table of seven items whose names begin with the letter 's'.
quips.Bleigießen: Germans melted lead and read the year ahead in its shapes until EU rules banned it in 2018.

krillion.quip: In Greece, Poland and elsewhere, people celebrate the feast of the saint they're named after with cards and gifts.

deepcut: Día del Amor y la Amistad

quips.Nengajo: Japan Post holds New Year postcards and delivers them all on 1 January.
quips.Galentine's Day: Popularised by the TV show Parks and Recreation in 2010.
quips.Sweetest Day: A Midwestern US holiday in October started by a Cleveland candy committee in 1922.

krillion.quip: Finland's toast; Finns traditionally keep eye contact while clinking, as in much of northern Europe.

deepcut: Arriba Abajo al Centro y pa Dentro
May the Road Rise to Meet You

quips.Sláinte: Irish and Scottish Gaelic for 'health'; the reply is often 'sláinte mhaith', good health.
quips.Skål: Often wrongly said to come from drinking from enemies' skulls — it really means 'bowl'.
quips.Gorko: Russian wedding guests shout 'bitter!' until the couple kiss to sweeten the drink.
quips.Arriba Abajo al Centro y pa Dentro: A Spanish toast: glass up, down, to the centre and then in.

chapters.text: Name an office supply

krillion.quip: A short cord with metal tips for binding punched papers, named after the UK Treasury.

quips.Bulldog Clip: Patented in 1944 by Hunt Manufacturing, though British versions date to the 1900s.
quips.Rolodex: Invented in 1956 by Arnold Neustadter, who also made the Autodex and Swivodex.
quips.Stapler: Early staplers were hand-made for King Louis XV, each staple engraved with his insignia.
quips.Spindle: Spiking paid bills on a desk spindle gave us the phrase 'spike a story'.

chapters.text: Name a job where people wear a uniform

krillion.quip: The Yeoman Warders of the Tower of London still wear Tudor-style red and gold state dress.

quips.Mountie: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police's red serge tunic is now mostly ceremonial.
quips.Swiss Guard: The Vatican's guards have protected the Pope since 1506.
quips.Gondolier: Venice licenses only about 400 gondoliers, and the job was long passed down in families.
quips.Chef: A traditional toque was said to have 100 pleats for 100 ways to cook an egg.

chapters.text: Name a job in a school

krillion.quip: The bursar handles a school's money, from Latin 'bursa', meaning purse.

quips.Proctor: Oxford's proctors still have 'bulldogs', bowler-hatted university constables.
quips.Don: From Latin 'dominus', meaning lord or master.
quips.Gyp: Cambridge college servants were called gyps, possibly from 'gypsy' or Greek 'gyps', vulture.
quips.Beadle: School and parish beadles were minor officials who kept order and ran errands.

chapters.text: Name a job in a hospital (not a type of doctor)

quips.Ocularist: Ocularists hand-paint artificial eyes to match the patient's real iris.
quips.Anaplastologist: Anaplastologists craft lifelike silicone ears, noses and fingers.
quips.Hospital Clown: Clown doctors were pioneered in the 1980s by Michael Christensen of the Big Apple Circus.

quips.Canary: Canaries were used in British coal mines to detect carbon monoxide until 1986.
quips.Hard Hat: Edward Bullard built an early hard hat in 1919 from steamed canvas, glue and black paint.
quips.Plague Doctor Mask: The beak was stuffed with herbs, thought to filter 'bad air'.

quips.Funambulist: A tightrope walker, from Latin 'funis' (rope) and 'ambulare' (to walk).
quips.Vexillologist: Vexillologists study flags; the term was coined by Whitney Smith in 1957.
quips.Campanologist: Bell-ringers who study change ringing are campanologists.

quips.Plongeur: French for 'diver', the dishwasher who plunges hands into the sink.
quips.Aufguss Master: Aufguss masters waft hot air round a sauna with towels, and even hold competitions.
quips.Communard: The cook who makes staff meals in a French kitchen.

quips.Greensman: Greensmen manage all the plants on set, real or fake.
quips.Walla Group: Background actors murmur 'walla walla' to make crowd chatter.

chapters.text: Name a job at sea or on a ship

krillion.quip: An officer who looked after the cargo and trade business on a merchant voyage.

quips.Haenyeo: Korean women divers of Jeju Island free-dive for seafood, some well into their 80s.
quips.Loblolly Boy: A surgeon's assistant on old warships, named after the porridge he served to the sick.
quips.Powder Monkey: Boys who ran gunpowder from the magazine to the guns during battle.
quips.Leadsman: Mark Twain's pen name comes from the leadsman's call meaning two fathoms deep.

chapters.text: Name a job in sport that isn't playing

krillion.quip: Wimbledon's grass is cut to exactly 8mm during the Championships.

quips.Soigneur: Cycling team carers who give massages, hand out food bags and look after riders.
quips.Hawk Handler: Wimbledon uses a Harris hawk named Rufus to scare off pigeons.
quips.Pebbler: Curling ice is sprayed with water droplets to create a pebbled surface the stones grip on.
quips.Bat Dog Handler: Some minor-league baseball teams use dogs to retrieve bats.

chapters.text: Name a farm tool or farm machine

krillion.quip: Two sticks joined by a chain or strap, used for threshing grain by hand for thousands of years.

quips.Mechanical Reaper: Cyrus McCormick patented his horse-drawn reaper in 1834, transforming grain farming.
quips.Caschrom: A Scottish Highland foot-plough used on rocky ground where horses could not go.
quips.Tribulum: An ancient threshing sledge studded with flints, dragged over grain by animals.
quips.Tractor: The word 'tractor' was popularised by the Hart-Parr company in the early 1900s.

chapters.text: Name a job at an airport

krillion.quip: Airports employ people, and even falcons, to keep birds away from runways.

quips.Marshaller: Marshallers guide planes to their stand using lit wands or paddles.
quips.Falconer: Many airports use trained falcons and hawks to scare off flocks of birds.
quips.Redcap: US airport porters were nicknamed redcaps after their red caps, starting in the 1890s.
quips.Pushback Driver: Most jets cannot reverse, so a tug pushes them back from the gate.

chapters.text: Name a word for money you earn from work

krillion.quip: A formal word for pay or profit from employment, from Latin 'emolumentum'.

quips.Salary: Often linked to Roman soldiers' salt allowance, though historians debate it.
quips.Baksheesh: A Persian-origin word for a tip or gift, used across the Middle East and South Asia.
quips.Pittance: Originally a pious gift of food or money to a monastery.

chapters.text: Name a job working with animals

krillion.quip: Chick sexers can sort day-old chicks into male and female at around 1,000 an hour.

quips.Swan Upper: The UK's Swan Upping each July counts the Thames mute swans owned by the Crown.
quips.Mahout: Mahouts often stay with one elephant for most of their working life.
quips.Mine Detection Rat Handler: APOPO's giant pouched rats sniff out landmines in Africa and Asia.
quips.Cormorant Fisherman: In China and Japan, trained cormorants catch fish for their handlers.

chapters.text: Name an old-fashioned job that has mostly disappeared

krillion.quip: Before alarm clocks, knocker-ups tapped on windows with long poles or pea-shooters to wake workers.

quips.Pinsetter: Bowling pins were reset by hand, often by boys, until automatic machines spread in the 1950s.
quips.Tosher: Toshers searched London's sewers for coins and metal scraps.
quips.Human Computer: NASA's human computers, including Katherine Johnson, calculated rocket trajectories by hand.
quips.Pure Finder: Pure finders collected dog droppings, which tanneries used to treat leather.

chapters.text: Name a military rank

krillion.quip: In the British Army a brigadier sits between colonel and major general; it is no longer a 'general' rank.

rare: Master Chief Petty Officer of the Navy
Marshal of the Royal Air Force

quips.Centurion: A Roman centurion commanded a 'century' of roughly 80 men, not 100.
quips.Generalissimo: A rank above general held by only a handful of leaders in history.
quips.Havildar: A rank in the Indian and Pakistani armies equivalent to sergeant.

chapters.text: Name a job in a theatre

krillion.quip: Dressers help actors make costume changes in the wings, sometimes in under 30 seconds.

quips.Claqueur: Paid applauders hired to cheer in 19th-century Paris opera houses.
quips.Orange Girl: Nell Gwyn sold oranges at the Theatre Royal, Drury Lane, before becoming an actress.
quips.Limelight Operator: Limelight was made by heating quicklime, which is where 'in the limelight' comes from.
quips.Thunder Man: Old theatres made thunder by rolling cannonballs down wooden troughs.

chapters.text: Name a job in a courtroom or the law

krillion.quip: A tipstaff is an enforcement officer of the English courts, named after a metal-tipped staff.

quips.Courtroom Sketch Artist: Cameras are banned in many courts, so artists sketch the trial instead.
quips.McKenzie Friend: Named after a 1970 English case, they help people who represent themselves in court.
quips.Silk: Senior barristers 'take silk' because KCs wear silk gowns.
quips.Greffier: The court registrar in French and Channel Islands courts.

chapters.text: Name a job in newspapers, magazines or book publishing

krillion.quip: Compositors set metal type letter by letter, upside down and back to front.

quips.Printer's Devil: An apprentice in a print shop, whose job often involved mixing ink. Benjamin Franklin started as one.
quips.Rubricator: Rubricators added red headings to medieval manuscripts, from Latin 'ruber', red.
quips.Sensitivity Reader: Sensitivity readers check manuscripts for inaccurate or hurtful portrayals.
quips.Copy Taster: Newspaper copytasters skim incoming stories and decide which ones are worth running.

chapters.text: Name a word for a boss or person in charge

krillion.quip: Originally a contraction of 'godfather', gaffer came to mean an old man, then a foreman or boss.

quips.Honcho: Borrowed from Japanese 'hanchō', squad leader, by US soldiers in Korea and Japan.
quips.Tycoon: From Japanese 'taikun', a title foreigners used for the shogun.
quips.Panjandrum: A nonsense word coined by Samuel Foote in 1755, now used for a pompous official.
quips.Laoban: Mandarin for 'boss' or shop owner, very common in everyday Chinese.

chapters.text: Name a piece of office jargon or business buzzword

krillion.quip: Spending ages on trivial details, from Parkinson's example of a committee arguing over a bike shed.

deepcut: At the End of the Day

quips.Yak Shaving: A chain of small tasks you must do before the real one, popularised at MIT in the 1990s.
quips.Skunkworks: Named after Lockheed's secret 1940s design group, itself named after a Li'l Abner comic.
quips.Kaizen: Japanese for 'continuous improvement', central to the Toyota Production System.
quips.Dogfooding: Using your own product internally, from a 1988 Microsoft memo titled 'Eating our own Dogfood'.

packs.name: Middle East & Arab World
packs.tagline: 21 stops · from Beirut to Dubai

chapters.text: Name a city in the Middle East or North Africa

krillion.quip: Chefchaouen is the Moroccan mountain town famous for its blue-washed streets.

quips.Chefchaouen: Chefchaouen's blue walls are said to repel mosquitoes and keep houses cool.

chapters.text: Name a city, town or village in Lebanon

krillion.quip: Deir el Qamar is a perfectly preserved Chouf mountain town that was once Lebanon's capital.

quips.Baalbek: Baalbek's Temple of Jupiter has some of the largest Roman columns ever raised.

chapters.text: Name a mezze dish

krillion.quip: Rakakat are crisp, cigar-shaped pastry rolls filled with melted cheese.

chapters.text: Name an Arabic dessert or sweet

krillion.quip: Karabij are Lebanese semolina pastries stuffed with nuts and drizzled with syrup.

quips.Baklava: Baklava can have 30 or more paper-thin layers of dough.

chapters.text: Name a Lebanese singer or musician

krillion.quip: Marcel Khalife is a Lebanese oud master and composer known for setting poetry to music.

quips.Fairuz: Fairuz has been called the soul of Lebanon and is often played at breakfast time across the Arab world.

chapters.text: Name a footballer from the Arab world

krillion.quip: Mustapha Hadji starred for Morocco at the 1998 World Cup and later played for Aston Villa.

quips.Mohamed Salah: Salah is nicknamed the Egyptian King, and has a place named after him in his hometown, Nagrig.

chapters.text: Name a famous landmark or tourist attraction in the Middle East

krillion.quip: Ait Benhaddou, a fortified Moroccan village, has appeared in Gladiator and Game of Thrones.

quips.Petra: Petra, the 'Rose City', was carved into pink sandstone by the Nabataeans over 2,000 years ago.

chapters.text: Name a place or attraction to visit in the UAE

krillion.quip: Sir Bani Yas Island in Abu Dhabi is a wildlife reserve with giraffes and cheetahs.

quips.Jebel Hafeet: Jebel Hafeet near Al Ain has a mountain road that is a favourite for cyclists and drivers.

chapters.text: Name a neighbourhood or area of Dubai

krillion.quip: Al Mizhar is a quiet residential area in eastern Dubai near Mirdif.

quips.Deira: Deira is the older side of Dubai Creek, home to the gold and spice souks.

chapters.text: Name an Emirati dish or traditional Gulf food

krillion.quip: Margoog is a hearty Emirati stew of vegetables and meat served over thin dough.

quips.Luqaimat: Luqaimat are crisp fried dough balls drizzled with date syrup.

chapters.text: Name an Arabic first name

krillion.quip: Qais is the name of the poet in the legend of Layla and Majnun.

quips.Layla: Layla means 'night' in Arabic, and the name has inspired songs for centuries.

chapters.text: Name an Arabic word or phrase

krillion.quip: Tfaddal is a warm Levantine word for 'please, go ahead' or 'here, take it'.

quips.Yalla: Yalla means 'let's go' and has been borrowed into Hebrew, Turkish, Swedish and more.

chapters.text: Name a traditional drink of the Middle East

krillion.quip: Qamar al-Din is a thick, sweet apricot drink traditionally enjoyed during Ramadan.

quips.Karak chai: Karak chai is strong tea with evaporated milk and cardamom, loved across the Gulf.

chapters.text: Name a traditional garment or accessory from the Arab world

krillion.quip: A bisht is the flowing cloak worn over a thobe on formal and ceremonial occasions.

quips.Keffiyeh: The keffiyeh shields wearers from desert sun and sand and has patterned fabrics in red, black and white.

chapters.text: Name a country or capital city in the Middle East or North Africa

krillion.quip: The Comoros, an island nation off East Africa, is a member of the Arab League.

quips.Sudan: Sudan has more pyramids than Egypt, though they are smaller.

chapters.text: Name a sea, river, desert or mountain range in the Middle East or North Africa

krillion.quip: Iran's Dasht-e Lut has been measured as one of the hottest surface spots on Earth.

quips.Suez Canal: The Suez Canal, opened in 1869, connects the Mediterranean to the Red Sea without sailing around Africa.

chapters.text: Name an Arab singer who is not Lebanese

krillion.quip: Asmahan was a Syrian-born singer and actress of the 1930s and 40s with a famously rich voice.

quips.Umm Kulthum: Umm Kulthum's concerts were broadcast monthly across the Arab world and streets fell quiet to listen.

chapters.text: Name a spice, herb or ingredient common in Middle Eastern cooking

krillion.quip: Mahleb is a ground cherry-stone spice that gives bread and sweets a nutty, floral flavour.

quips.Za'atar: Za'atar is both a wild thyme-like herb and the famous dried mix with sumac and sesame seeds.

chapters.text: Name an animal or plant associated with the Middle East

krillion.quip: The sidr, or Christ's-thorn jujube, grows in the Gulf's deserts and shades goats and travellers.

quips.Arabian oryx: The Arabian oryx was extinct in the wild by 1972 before reintroduction programs brought it back.

chapters.text: Name an ancient civilization, empire or people of the Middle East

krillion.quip: The Nabataeans carved the rose-red city of Petra out of the desert rock.

quips.Phoenicians: The Phoenicians spread an alphabet that is ancestor to Greek, Latin and Arabic scripts.

chapters.text: Name a company or brand from the Gulf region

krillion.quip: Al Rawabi is a UAE dairy brand that produces milk, laban and yoghurt.

quips.Careem: Careem, founded in Dubai, was bought by Uber in 2019 for 3.1 billion dollars.

packs.name: Myths & Legends
packs.tagline: 21 legends · gods, monsters and the stories they live in

chapters.text: Name a deity of ancient Rome

krillion.quip: Romans held the Robigalia each April to beg this god to keep mildew off the wheat.

quips.Janus: Two faces, one looking back and one forward, which is why January carries his name.
quips.Cardea: Goddess of door hinges; Romans honestly had a god for almost everything.
quips.Cloacina: Goddess of the Cloaca Maxima, Rome's great sewer.
quips.Sterquilinus: A god of manure, honoured by farmers for fertile fields.

chapters.text: Name a beast or monster from Greek legend

krillion.quip: The many-headed dragon that coiled around the golden apples of the Hesperides.

quips.Talos: A giant bronze man who circled Crete three times a day hurling rocks at ships.
quips.Laelaps: A hound that always caught its prey, sent to chase a fox that could never be caught.
quips.Teumessian Fox: Zeus ended the unstoppable-hound paradox by turning both animals into stone.
quips.Carcinus: The crab that nipped Heracles mid-Hydra fight became the constellation Cancer.

chapters.text: Name a dragon from myth, legend or fiction

krillion.quip: A winged dragon-serpent that still sits on the coat of arms of Kazan, Russia.

quips.Ladon: Heracles slew him for the golden apples; Hera set him in the sky as Draco.
quips.Wawel Dragon: Tricked into eating a sheep stuffed with sulphur, then drank the Vistula till it burst.
quips.Tarasque: Tamed by Saint Martha with hymns and holy water, says Provençal legend.

chapters.text: Name a witch, wizard or sorcerer from myth, legend or fiction

krillion.quip: The Mistress of the North in Finland's Kalevala, who once stole the sun and moon.

Lord Voldemort: He Who Must Not Be Named

quips.Erichtho: A Thessalian witch in Lucan's epic so terrifying even other witches feared her.
quips.Djedi: An Egyptian magician said to reattach a goose's head and make it waddle again.
quips.Michael Scot: A real 13th-century scholar whom Dante placed in Hell as a sorcerer.

chapters.text: Name a deity from Hinduism

krillion.quip: The Hindu god of love shoots flower-tipped arrows from a bow made of sugarcane.

quips.Ganesha: Writes the Mahabharata as Vyasa dictates, breaking off a tusk to use as a pen.
quips.Vishvakarma: The divine architect, honoured by engineers and craftspeople on Vishwakarma Puja.
quips.Ardhanarishvara: Shiva and Parvati fused into one figure, half male and half female.

chapters.text: Name a character from Homer's Iliad or Odyssey

krillion.quip: Odysseus's old nurse recognises him by a boar-hunt scar while washing his feet.

quips.Argos: After 20 years away, only the old dog recognises Odysseus at once.
quips.Thersites: The ugliest man at Troy, and the only common soldier who dares mock the kings.
quips.Dolon: A Trojan spy in a wolfskin, caught at night by Odysseus and Diomedes.

chapters.text: Name a giant from myth, folklore or a story

krillion.quip: A Welsh giant king whose severed head kept talking and was buried to guard Britain.

quips.Finn McCool: Legend says he built the Giant's Causeway to reach a rival giant in Scotland.
quips.Pangu: In Chinese myth his body became the world: breath the wind, eyes the sun and moon.
quips.Gogmagog: Cornish legend says he was hurled off a cliff by the hero Corineus.

chapters.text: Name a yokai or creature from Japanese folklore

krillion.quip: A one-eyed, one-legged paper umbrella that hops about after turning into a spirit.

quips.Akaname: A yokai that licks the grime in dirty bathrooms; a classic nudge to keep them clean.
quips.Amabie: A beaked mermaid said to ward off epidemics; it went viral in Japan in 2020.
quips.Azukiarai: You hear it washing azuki beans by the river but rarely see it.

chapters.text: Name a ghost, spirit or undead being from folklore

krillion.quip: A Scottish washer-woman spirit seen scrubbing the clothes of those about to die.

quips.Ankou: In Breton lore the last person to die each year collects the dead for the next.
quips.Draugr: Norse undead that guard their burial-mound treasure and can grow to giant size.
quips.Jiangshi: Stiff-armed Chinese corpses that hop; holding your breath supposedly hides you.

chapters.text: Name a legendary weapon, treasure or magical object

krillion.quip: A magic mill in the Kalevala that churns out flour, salt and gold from nothing.

rare: Goose that laid the golden eggs

Sword in the Stone: Sword in the stone of Arthur

quips.Gleipnir: The silk-thin ribbon that bound Fenrir, made from a cat's footstep and a fish's breath.
quips.Skidbladnir: Freyr's ship always has a fair wind and folds up small enough to fit in a pocket.
quips.Lia Fail: The coronation stone at Tara was said to roar when the true king of Ireland stood on it.

chapters.text: Name a legendary lost city, island or kingdom

krillion.quip: A phantom island west of Ireland that kept appearing on sea charts until the 1800s.

quips.Ys: A Breton city below sea level, drowned when princess Dahut opened the dyke gates.
quips.Kitezh: Russian legend says the city sank into Lake Svetloyar to hide from invaders.
quips.Cibola: Spanish explorers chased these seven golden cities across the American Southwest.

chapters.text: Name a figure from Celtic (Irish, Welsh or Scottish) myth

krillion.quip: A Welsh woman conjured from oak, broom and meadowsweet, later turned into an owl.

quips.Scathach: A warrior woman on Skye who trained Cu Chulainn and gave him the spear Gae Bolg.
quips.Salmon of Knowledge: Young Finn burned his thumb cooking it, sucked it, and gained all the world's wisdom.
quips.Fintan mac Bochra: Survived the Flood by living as a salmon, eagle and hawk for thousands of years.

chapters.text: Name a deity from Aztec, Maya, Inca or Mesopotamian mythology

krillion.quip: The Maya god of merchants and cacao, often shown carrying a heavy trader's pack.

quips.Huitzilopochtli: His name means 'hummingbird of the south'; he was the Aztec sun and war god.
quips.Camazotz: A Maya bat god whose name means 'death bat'; he beheaded Hunahpu in the Popol Vuh.
quips.Pazuzu: A demon king of winds, yet Assyrians wore his image as a charm against other demons.

chapters.text: Name a sea monster or water spirit from folklore

krillion.quip: An Aztec dog-like water beast with a hand on its tail for dragging people under.

quips.Jenny Greenteeth: A Lancashire river hag invented, many think, to keep children away from ponds.
quips.Aspidochelone: A whale so vast sailors mistook it for an island and lit fires on its back.
quips.Qalupalik: An Inuit sea creature said to hum and snatch children who wander near the ice edge.

chapters.text: Name someone from Greek myth who was transformed into an animal, plant, star or other thing

krillion.quip: Demeter turned this tattle-tale into a screech owl for reporting on Persephone.

quips.Perdix: Pushed from a tower by jealous Daedalus, Athena caught him and made him a partridge.
quips.Clytie: Pined for the sun god Helios so long she became a flower that follows the sun.
quips.Battus: Broke a promise to Hermes and was turned into a touchstone, a rock that tests gold.

chapters.text: Name a legendary folk hero or outlaw

krillion.quip: Slovakia's Robin Hood, a highwayman said to rob the rich and give to the poor.

Ali Baba: Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves

quips.Joe Magarac: A Pittsburgh steelworker of legend, made of steel himself, who stirred molten metal by hand.
quips.Twm Sion Cati: Wales's answer to Robin Hood, a trickster thief who later married an heiress.
quips.Holger Danske: Danish legend says he sleeps beneath Kronborg Castle until Denmark needs him.

chapters.text: Name a trickster figure from myth or folklore

krillion.quip: The Yoruba messenger who wore a two-coloured hat just to make two friends quarrel.

quips.Maui: Polynesian trickster who fished up islands and lassoed the sun to slow it down.
quips.Iktomi: A Lakota spider trickster whose schemes usually end with himself fooled.
quips.Hermes: Stole Apollo's cattle on his first day alive, walking them backwards to hide the tracks.

chapters.text: Name a type of fairy, elf, goblin or other little folk

krillion.quip: A Swedish farm gnome who expects a bowl of porridge with butter on Christmas Eve.

quips.Heinzelmannchen: Cologne's helper elves did all the town's work at night, until a tailor's wife spied on them.
quips.Menehune: Hawaiian little people said to build fishponds and temples in a single night.
quips.Gremlin: RAF pilots in the Second World War blamed these imps for unexplained engine failures.

chapters.text: Name a famous horse or steed from fiction or legend

krillion.quip: A magic bay horse that could stretch to carry all four sons of Aymon at once.

quips.Incitatus: Roman gossip claimed Caligula planned to make his favourite horse a consul.
quips.Comanche: Survived Custer's Last Stand and lived out his days as a regimental mascot.
quips.Kanthaka: The white horse that carried Prince Siddhartha away from his palace to become the Buddha.

chapters.text: Name an underworld, afterlife or realm of the dead from any mythology

krillion.quip: The Finnish land of the dead, reached across a black river guarded by a swan.

quips.Fiddler's Green: Sailors' heaven, where the fiddle never stops and the dancers never tire.
quips.Nastrond: The Norse 'corpse shore', a hall woven of serpents dripping venom.
quips.Hamistagan: Zoroastrian limbo for souls whose good and bad deeds exactly balance.

chapters.text: Name a cryptid or legendary creature some people claim is real

krillion.quip: A big black cat 'seen' on Cornwall's moors; a 1995 government study found no proof.

Lizard Man: Lizard Man of Scape Ore Swamp

quips.Mothman: Point Pleasant, West Virginia, now holds an annual Mothman Festival in its honour.
quips.Jackalope: A rabbit with antlers, invented as a taxidermy joke in 1930s Wyoming.
quips.Hodag: A horned beast 'captured' in 1893 Wisconsin; it was a hoax, now the town mascot.

packs.name: Ocean & Sea
packs.tagline: 21 depths · sink into the blue

chapters.text: Name a tropical reef fish

krillion.quip: Its neon blue-orange swirls make it one of the most colourful fish on Earth.

chapters.text: Name a mollusc (not a crustacean)

krillion.quip: A living fossil that has barely changed in around 450 million years.

quips.Nautilus: Its chambered shell is the model for the classic spiral in textbooks.

chapters.text: Name a type of seashell

krillion.quip: This big spiral shell has been blown as a trumpet by sea-folk for centuries.

chapters.text: Name a jellyfish, coral or sea anemone

krillion.quip: These stinging jellies trail tentacles several metres long.

quips.Immortal jellyfish: Turritopsis dohrnii can revert to a juvenile state and, in theory, never die.

chapters.text: Name a seabird

krillion.quip: This tubular-nosed bird can spit stomach oil at attackers.

chapters.text: Name a seal, sea lion or other marine mammal (not a whale or dolphin)

krillion.quip: Sailors who saw these grazing sea-cows may have invented mermaids.

chapters.text: Name a deep-sea creature

krillion.quip: It flaps ear-like fins and lives at depths of up to 4,000 metres.

chapters.text: Name a sail, rig or sailing manoeuvre

krillion.quip: Turning the stern through the wind so the boom swings across the boat.

chapters.text: Name a famous beach

krillion.quip: A Seychelles beach lined with giant granite boulders.

chapters.text: Name a bay or gulf

krillion.quip: Its tides rise and fall by up to about 16 metres, the highest in the world.

chapters.text: Name a prehistoric sea creature

krillion.quip: A 6-metre armoured fish with a bite stronger than a modern great white.

chapters.text: Name a water sport or sea activity

krillion.quip: Harnessing a power kite to skim across the waves on a small board.

chapters.text: Name a famous ocean explorer, diver or marine scientist

krillion.quip: Nicknamed 'Her Deepness', she has led over 100 expeditions underwater.

chapters.text: Name a famous lighthouse

krillion.quip: One of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, it stood for about 1,500 years.

chapters.text: Name a film or TV show set at sea or under the sea

krillion.quip: A German submarine drama famed for its claustrophobic, real-feeling tension.

rare: The Old Man and the Sea
Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
Journey to the Center of the Earth
Voyage to the Bottom of the Sea
Pirates of the Caribbean: On Stranger Tides
deepcut: The Curse of the Black Pearl

Master and Commander: Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World
Pirates of the Caribbean: Pirates Of The Caribbean The Curse Of The Black Pearl

chapters.text: Name a fictional character who lives in the sea

krillion.quip: One of the seven mermaid princesses in Disney's The Little Mermaid.

chapters.text: Name a type of warship or naval vessel

krillion.quip: An ironclad with a low deck and a rotating turret, made famous in the American Civil War.

chapters.text: Name a famous shipwreck

krillion.quip: A Great Lakes freighter lost in a Lake Superior storm in 1975, made famous by a song.

chapters.text: Name a port or harbour city

krillion.quip: Chile's tumbling hillside port city of colourful houses and funiculars.

chapters.text: Name a ray, skate or eel

krillion.quip: Also called a torpedo ray, it can zap prey with up to 200 volts.

chapters.text: Name a big game fish or sport fish

krillion.quip: One of the fastest fish in the sea, it can hit around 80 km/h.

packs.name: Weather & the Great Outdoors
packs.tagline: 21 wild prompts · Touch grass, score points

chapters.text: Name a landform or geographical feature

krillion.quip: A wind-sculpted rock ridge shaped like an upturned boat hull; the word comes from Turkic for 'steep bank'.

quips.Tepui: These flat-topped Venezuelan table mountains inspired Arthur Conan Doyle's The Lost World.
quips.Drumlin: Egg-shaped hills left by glaciers; the word comes from Irish 'droim', meaning ridge.
quips.Tombolo: A sand bar that ties an island to the mainland, like the one leading to St Michael's Mount at low tide.

chapters.text: Name a word to describe the weather

krillion.quip: From Latin 'bruma', the winter solstice: it means foggy, misty and wintry all at once.

quips.Dreich: A Scots word for dull, damp and gloomy weather, once voted Scotland's favourite word.
quips.Halcyon: Named after a mythical kingfisher said to calm the seas while it nested in midwinter.
quips.Baltic: British slang for freezing cold, borrowed from the chilly Baltic Sea.

chapters.text: Name a woodland or forest animal

krillion.quip: Madagascar's largest predator looks like a cat but is a cousin of the mongoose, and it hunts lemurs through the trees.

quips.Pudu: The world's smallest deer, from Chile's rainforests, stands only about 40 cm tall.
quips.Okapi: Looks like a zebra-legged horse but its closest living relative is the giraffe.
quips.Binturong: Also called the bearcat, it famously smells like buttered popcorn.

chapters.text: Name a natural disaster or hazard

krillion.quip: In 1986 Cameroon's Lake Nyos suddenly released a huge cloud of carbon dioxide, a rare event called a limnic eruption.

quips.Haboob: A towering wall of dust pushed ahead of a thunderstorm; the name comes from Arabic for 'blowing'.
quips.Dzud: A Mongolian disaster where a severe winter after a dry summer starves livestock.
quips.Seiche: A standing wave that sloshes back and forth across a lake, like water in a bathtub.

chapters.text: Name a food you'd pack for a picnic

krillion.quip: This sandwich from Nice means 'bathed bread': it is pressed so olive oil and tomato juice soak right through.

quips.Scotch egg: London store Fortnum & Mason claims to have invented the Scotch egg in 1738 as a travel snack.
quips.Lamingtons: Australia's chocolate-and-coconut sponge squares are said to be named after a Queensland governor, Lord Lamington.
quips.Zongzi: Sticky rice parcels wrapped in bamboo leaves, eaten during China's Dragon Boat Festival.

chapters.text: Name a creepy-crawly that isn't an insect

krillion.quip: Velvet worms catch prey by squirting jets of sticky slime from glands beside their mouths.

quips.Tardigrade: These microscopic 'water bears' have survived being exposed to outer space.
quips.Peacock spider: The male raises a brightly coloured flap and dances to impress females.
quips.Springtail: Springtails have six legs but are no longer classed as insects, and they leap using a tail-like spring.

chapters.text: Name a word for a stream, pond or other body of water

krillion.quip: In South Africa a vlei is a shallow lake or marsh that fills in the rainy season and may dry out later.

quips.Billabong: An Australian oxbow lake left behind when a river changes course; it appears in Waltzing Matilda.
quips.Force: In northern England 'force' means waterfall, from Old Norse 'fors', as in Aira Force.
quips.Bayou: A slow, marshy stream of the US Gulf Coast; the word may come from Choctaw 'bayuk'.

chapters.text: Name a famous waterfall

krillion.quip: On Norway's Flåm Railway the train stops here in summer, and a performer dressed as a 'huldra' forest spirit dances by the falls.

quips.Angel Falls: The world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall is named after US pilot Jimmie Angel, who crash-landed on top in 1937.
quips.Kaieteur Falls: Guyana's single-drop giant is about four times taller than Niagara.
quips.Reichenbach Falls: Arthur Conan Doyle chose this Swiss waterfall for Sherlock Holmes's 'final' fight with Moriarty.

chapters.text: Name a famous mountain or peak (not a range)

krillion.quip: Bhutan's highest peak is thought to be the tallest unclimbed mountain on Earth, because the country bans climbing its sacred peaks.

quips.Mauna Kea: Measured from its base on the sea floor, Mauna Kea is taller than Everest.
quips.Chimborazo: Because Earth bulges at the equator, Chimborazo's summit is the point farthest from Earth's centre.
quips.Ben Nevis: A weather observatory operated on its summit from 1883 to 1904.

chapters.text: Name a cactus or succulent

krillion.quip: This tiny, slow-growing Mexican cactus is named for its wrinkled ribs, which look like Aztec stone carvings.

quips.Saguaro: A saguaro may not grow its first arm until it is 50 to 70 years old.
quips.Quiver tree: San people hollowed its branches to make quivers for their arrows.
quips.Century plant: It doesn't take a century, but it flowers only once, after 10 to 30 years, then dies.

chapters.text: Name a wildflower or common weed

krillion.quip: Nicknamed the 'meadow-maker', it feeds off grass roots, weakening the grass so other wildflowers can grow.

quips.Dandelion: The name comes from French 'dent de lion', lion's tooth, after its jagged leaves.
quips.Foxglove: It is the source of digitalis, a heart medicine, but the whole plant is poisonous.
quips.Sundew: This tiny bog plant catches insects on sticky, glistening hairs.

chapters.text: Name a named wind (local or regional)

krillion.quip: Each summer this wind blows steadily across Iran's Sistan region for about four months, piling sand into huge dunes.

quips.Chinook: Nicknamed the 'snow eater', a chinook once raised the temperature in Loma, Montana by 57 °C in 24 hours.
quips.Fremantle Doctor: A cooling sea breeze that 'cures' Perth's hot summer afternoons.
quips.Mistral: Van Gogh had to weigh down his easel against the mistral while painting in Provence.

chapters.text: Name a famous hiking trail or long-distance walk

krillion.quip: This roughly 25-day trek across Bhutan's high passes is said to be completed by fewer people each year than summit Everest.

quips.Appalachian Trail: Only about one in four people who attempt a full thru-hike of its roughly 3,500 km actually finish.
quips.Kumano Kodo: It is one of only two pilgrimage routes on the UNESCO World Heritage list; the other is the Camino de Santiago.
quips.Te Araroa: Its name means 'The Long Pathway', and it runs about 3,000 km down the length of New Zealand.

chapters.text: Name a national park outside the USA

krillion.quip: Sweden's Sarek is a true wilderness with no roads, no marked trails and almost no huts.

quips.Banff: Canada's first national park was created in 1885 after railway workers found hot springs there.
quips.Białowieża: Shared by Poland and Belarus, it protects one of Europe's last primeval forests and its wild bison.
quips.Kakadu: Some rock art in Kakadu is thought to be up to 20,000 years old.

chapters.text: Name a retired hurricane, typhoon or cyclone name

krillion.quip: Hawaii's most powerful recorded hurricane hit Kauai in 1992 while Steven Spielberg was filming Jurassic Park there.

quips.Tracy: Cyclone Tracy flattened much of Darwin, Australia, on Christmas Day 1974.
quips.Haiyan: Known in the Philippines as Yolanda, it was one of the strongest storms ever to make landfall.
quips.Patricia: In 2015 Hurricane Patricia set the record for the strongest winds measured in a Western Hemisphere storm.

chapters.text: Name a member of the grass family (cereals and bamboo count)

krillion.quip: This West African grain, nicknamed 'hungry rice', can be ready to harvest in as little as six to eight weeks.

quips.Bamboo: Some bamboo species can grow nearly a metre in a single day.
quips.Teosinte: This scraggly Mexican wild grass is the ancestor of all modern maize.
quips.Marram grass: Its deep roots trap blowing sand and help build coastal dunes.

chapters.text: Name an island in the Pacific Ocean

krillion.quip: Marlon Brando bought this French Polynesian atoll after filming Mutiny on the Bounty in Tahiti.

quips.Pitcairn Island: Home to around 40 people, many descended from the Bounty mutineers who settled there in 1790.
quips.Robinson Crusoe Island: Sailor Alexander Selkirk was marooned here for four years, inspiring Defoe's novel.
quips.Henderson Island: This uninhabited coral island is famous for having one of the highest densities of washed-up plastic on Earth.

chapters.text: Name a glacier

krillion.quip: In 2019 Iceland unveiled a memorial plaque for Okjökull, the first Icelandic glacier lost to climate change.

quips.Taylor Glacier: It is the source of Antarctica's Blood Falls, where iron-rich brine stains the ice red.
quips.Perito Moreno: One of the few glaciers still advancing; it periodically dams a lake and then bursts spectacularly.
quips.Lambert Glacier: Often called the world's largest glacier, it drains about 8% of Antarctica's ice sheet.

chapters.text: Name a river outside Europe

krillion.quip: Colombia's 'river of five colours' turns red, yellow and green when an aquatic plant blooms on its bed.

quips.Amazon: It carries more water than the next several largest rivers combined.
quips.Okavango: Instead of reaching the sea, it fans out and evaporates in the Kalahari, forming a vast inland delta.
quips.Congo: It is the deepest river in the world, with depths of over 220 metres.

chapters.text: Name a famous cave or cave system

krillion.quip: This Romanian cave was sealed off for around 5.5 million years, and its animals live off bacteria that feed on chemicals instead of sunlight.

quips.Son Doong: The world's largest known cave passage has its own jungle and weather system inside.
quips.Lascaux: It was discovered in 1940 by four teenagers after their dog fell down a hole.
quips.Fingal's Cave: Its hexagonal basalt columns inspired Mendelssohn's Hebrides Overture.

chapters.text: Name an island in the Atlantic or Indian Ocean

krillion.quip: Slaves shipwrecked on this tiny French island in 1761 survived for 15 years before the last of them were rescued.

quips.Bouvet Island: About 1,600 km from Antarctica, it is often called the most remote island on Earth.
quips.Socotra: About a third of its plants grow nowhere else, including the umbrella-shaped dragon's blood tree.
quips.Tristan da Cunha: Its main settlement is roughly 2,400 km from the nearest inhabited land, Saint Helena.

packs.name: Plants & Gardens
packs.tagline: 21 seedlings · dig up the rare ones

chapters.text: Name a nut (or something sold as a nut)

krillion.quip: Seed of an Australian conifer whose cones can weigh more than a bowling ball.

quips.Coco de mer: Its seed is the biggest in the plant kingdom, weighing up to 25 kg.
quips.Brazil nut: Brazil nut trees only fruit well in wild rainforest where orchid bees live.
quips.Cashew: Cashews grow hanging below a fleshy 'cashew apple'.
quips.Ivory nut: Tagua seeds are so hard they were carved into buttons before plastic.

chapters.text: Name a climbing plant or vine

krillion.quip: Its pipe-shaped flowers trap flies overnight so they carry its pollen.

quips.Kudzu: Kudzu can grow about 30 cm in a single day in summer.
quips.Vanilla: Vanilla pods come from a climbing orchid that is hand-pollinated on farms.
quips.Dodder: Dodder has almost no chlorophyll and sniffs out host plants by scent.
quips.Rattan: Rattan furniture comes from spiny climbing palms.

chapters.text: Name a poisonous plant

krillion.quip: Even standing under this Caribbean tree in rain can blister your skin.

quips.Castor bean: Castor seeds contain ricin, though castor oil itself is safe.
quips.Gympie-gympie: Its glassy stinging hairs can cause pain that lasts for months.
quips.White snakeroot: Milk from cows that ate it is thought to have killed Abraham Lincoln's mother.
quips.Yew: Almost every part of a yew is toxic except the red flesh of the berry.

chapters.text: Name a shrub or bush

krillion.quip: Its fluffy seed plumes make the whole shrub look wrapped in pink smoke.

quips.Creosote bush: One Mojave creosote ring called King Clone is thought to be about 11,700 years old.
quips.Tumbleweed: Tumbleweeds snap off at the base and roll to scatter thousands of seeds.
quips.Burning bush: Its leaves turn a blazing scarlet in autumn.

chapters.text: Name a bean, pea, lentil or other legume

krillion.quip: Almost every part of this tropical legume is edible, from leaves to roots.

quips.Peanut: Peanuts flower above ground, then push their pods into the soil to ripen.
quips.Tamarind: Tamarind is a legume: its sour pulp grows inside a brown bean pod.
quips.Carob: Carob seeds were so uniform they gave us the word 'carat'.
quips.Rooibos: Rooibos tea comes from a South African legume shrub.

chapters.text: Name a plant with an animal in its name

krillion.quip: A succulent whose mother rosette is ringed by little offset 'chicks'.

quips.Dandelion: 'Dandelion' comes from French 'dent de lion', meaning lion's tooth.
quips.Snapdragon: Squeeze a snapdragon flower and its 'jaws' open and shut.
quips.Bee orchid: The bee orchid's flower mimics a female bee to lure in males.
quips.Monkey puzzle: Its spiky branches were said to be a puzzle even a monkey couldn't climb.

chapters.text: Name a garden feature or structure

krillion.quip: A sunken wall that keeps livestock out without spoiling the view.

quips.Ha-ha: Named, the story goes, for the surprised laugh of visitors who spotted it.
quips.Folly: Follies are fake ruins or towers built purely for decoration.
quips.Fernery: Victorian Britain went so fern-mad the craze got a name: Pteridomania.
quips.Pinery: Pineapples were such status symbols that Georgians built heated pits to grow them.

chapters.text: Name a tea or herbal tea

krillion.quip: Green tea rolled into tiny pellets that burst open in hot water.

quips.Earl Grey: Earl Grey gets its citrus taste from bergamot orange oil.
quips.Lapsang souchong: This black tea is dried over burning pine, giving it a campfire smell.
quips.Pu-erh: Some aged pu-erh cakes are decades old and sell for thousands.
quips.Butter tea: Tibetan butter tea is churned with yak butter and salt.

chapters.text: Name a plant that grows from a bulb, corm, tuber or rhizome

krillion.quip: Its bulbs smell so musky that gardeners plant them to drive away moles.

quips.Titan arum: Its giant corm can weigh over 100 kg and its flower smells of rotting meat.
quips.Banana: A banana 'tree' is really a giant herb growing from an underground corm.
quips.Saffron crocus: Each saffron crocus gives just three red threads, all picked by hand.
quips.Potato: Potatoes are stem tubers, so their 'eyes' are really buds.

chapters.text: Name a chilli pepper variety

krillion.quip: Most are mild, but roughly one in ten is fiery: a tapas lottery.

deepcut: Pimiento de Fresno de la Vega

quips.Carolina Reaper: It held the world's-hottest record from 2013 until Pepper X took over in 2023.
quips.Paprika: Paprika powder is just dried, ground mild chillies.
quips.Chipotle: A chipotle is a ripe jalapeño that has been smoke-dried.
quips.Ancho: An ancho is a dried poblano, wrinkled and almost raisin-sweet.

chapters.text: Name a water or pond plant

krillion.quip: It rises to the surface to flower in summer and sinks to the bottom for winter.

quips.Victoria water lily: Its giant pads can hold the weight of a small child.
quips.Lotus: Lotus leaves are so water-repellent that the 'lotus effect' is studied by engineers.
quips.Bladderwort: Bladderworts suck in tiny prey with one of the fastest traps in nature.
quips.Duckweed: Duckweed is one of the smallest flowering plants in the world.

chapters.text: Name a garden pest or plant disease

krillion.quip: The virus that striped the costly 'broken' tulips of Dutch Tulip Mania.

quips.Dutch elm disease: This beetle-spread fungus killed tens of millions of elms across Europe and North America.
quips.Clubroot: Clubroot spores can survive in soil for 20 years.
quips.Ergot: Ergot fungus on rye may explain medieval outbreaks of 'St Anthony's fire'.
quips.Noble rot: This 'good' mould shrivels grapes to make famously sweet dessert wines.

chapters.text: Name a plant used in herbal medicine or remedies

krillion.quip: Willow bark's salicin pointed chemists toward the invention of aspirin.

quips.Cinchona: Quinine from cinchona bark is why tonic water tastes bitter.
quips.Madagascar periwinkle: This pink flower gives vincristine, a key childhood leukaemia drug.
quips.Pacific yew: Its bark gave the cancer drug paclitaxel, also known as Taxol.
quips.Sweet wormwood: Its compound artemisinin won a 2015 Nobel Prize for fighting malaria.

chapters.text: Name a type of orchid

krillion.quip: Dracula simia's flowers look uncannily like a tiny monkey's face.

quips.Vanilla: Vanilla is the only orchid grown as a major food crop.
quips.Darwin's orchid: Darwin predicted a moth with a 30 cm tongue would pollinate it; one was found decades later.
quips.Underground orchid: This Australian orchid lives and flowers entirely underground.
quips.Bee orchid: The bee orchid mimics a female bee, though in Britain it mostly pollinates itself.

chapters.text: Name a fern, moss or other spore-bearing plant

krillion.quip: It can shrivel up brown for months, then turn green again within hours of rain.

quips.Bracken: Bracken may be the most widespread fern on Earth, found on every continent but Antarctica.
quips.Horsetail: Horsetails are living fossils whose relatives grew as tall as trees 300 million years ago.
quips.Luminous moss: Goblin gold glows emerald in dark caves because its cells focus faint light like lenses.
quips.Silver fern: New Zealand's silver fern shows a white underside that Maori used to mark night trails.

chapters.text: Name a seaweed or alga

krillion.quip: A single-celled alga shaped like a tiny wine glass that can grow several centimetres tall.

quips.Giant kelp: Giant kelp can grow up to half a metre in a single day.
quips.Asparagopsis: Fed to cows in tiny amounts, this red seaweed sharply cuts their methane burps.
quips.Prochlorococcus: This microbe may be the most abundant photosynthetic organism on Earth.
quips.Agar: Agar from red seaweed is the jelly that microbiologists grow bacteria on.

chapters.text: Name a carnivorous plant

krillion.quip: A rootless aquatic cousin of the Venus flytrap that snaps up tiny water fleas.

quips.Venus flytrap: In the wild, Venus flytraps grow only within about 120 km of Wilmington, North Carolina.
quips.Rajah pitcher plant: Its pitchers can hold over three litres and have caught small rats.
quips.Bat pitcher plant: This Bornean pitcher feeds on droppings from bats that roost inside it.
quips.Bladderwort: A bladderwort trap sucks in prey in under a thousandth of a second.

chapters.text: Name a palm or palm-like plant

krillion.quip: It flowers once after decades, with the largest flower cluster of any plant, then dies.

quips.Coco de mer: The coco de mer grows the world's heaviest seed, up to 25 kg.
quips.Quindío wax palm: Colombia's national tree is the tallest palm on Earth, reaching about 60 m.
quips.Tahina palm: Discovered in 2007, this Madagascan palm flowers so hard that it kills itself.
quips.Rattan: Rattans are climbing palms that hook onto trees with whip-like barbed tendrils.

chapters.text: Name a plant whose name ends in "-wort"

krillion.quip: Folklore claimed this little fern could pull the shoes off horses and open locks.

quips.Liverwort: '-wort' is Old English for plant; liver-shaped liverworts were thought to treat the liver.
quips.Squinancywort: Its odd name comes from 'quinsy', a throat infection it was meant to cure.
quips.Lungwort: Its spotty leaves looked like diseased lungs, so herbalists used it for chest complaints.
quips.Sneezewort: Dried sneezewort leaves were once used as snuff to make people sneeze.

chapters.text: Name a plant used to make fibre, rope, cloth, paper or baskets

krillion.quip: Filipino piña cloth is woven from pineapple leaf fibres, fine enough for formal wear.

quips.Papyrus: The word 'paper' comes from papyrus, the Egyptian sedge.
quips.Cork oak: Cork oaks are stripped of their bark every nine years without being cut down.
quips.Harakeke: Maori weavers used harakeke flax for everything from cloaks to fishing nets.
quips.Kozo: Most Japanese washi paper is made from kozo, the paper mulberry shrub.

chapters.text: Name a famous botanist, gardener or garden designer

krillion.quip: The first woman known to sail round the world, disguised as a man to collect plants.

quips.Gregor Mendel: Mendel cracked the rules of heredity by breeding about 28,000 pea plants.
quips.Carl Linnaeus: Linnaeus gave us two-part Latin names like Homo sapiens.
quips.Capability Brown: He earned his nickname by telling clients their land had 'capabilities'.
quips.Claude Monet: Monet spent decades building the Giverny water garden he painted over 250 times.

packs.name: School & Childhood
packs.tagline: 21 lessons · Ring the bell, then dive for the answers nobody else remembers

chapters.text: Name a school subject or class

krillion.quip: Its name means 'triangle measuring' in Greek, and it was born from astronomy, not geometry homework.

quips.Latin: Latin is technically a 'dead' language, yet it's still the official language of Vatican City.
quips.Phonics: Phonics teaching dates back to the 1500s, when John Hart argued English spelling should match sounds.
quips.Calligraphy: In China, calligraphy has long been ranked alongside poetry and painting as a high art.
quips.Elocution: Elocution lessons were once a staple for anyone hoping to 'lose' a regional accent.

chapters.text: Name something you'd find in a classroom

krillion.quip: Some primary schools in Japan still teach the soroban abacus, and expert users can calculate faster than a calculator.

quips.Slate: Victorian pupils wrote on slates because paper was too expensive to waste on practice sums.
quips.Inkwell: Desks had holes for inkwells until ballpoint pens took over in the 1950s and 60s.
quips.Cuisenaire Rods: Invented by Belgian teacher Georges Cuisenaire, each length of rod has its own colour.
quips.Blu Tack: Blu Tack was originally made white, but it was dyed blue so kids wouldn't mistake it for chewing gum.

chapters.text: Name something you might find in a pencil case

krillion.quip: Thermochromic ink 'erases' because friction heats it above about 60°C and the colour vanishes — pop it in the freezer and it can come back.

quips.Ink Eradicator: The 'ink killer' pen bleaches royal-blue fountain ink with a sulphite solution, then rewrites in an ink it can't erase.
quips.Biro: Hungarian László Bíró patented the ballpoint in 1938 after noticing newspaper ink dried quickly.
quips.Chinagraph Pencil: Its wax lead writes on glass, porcelain and photo film — hence the name.
quips.Slide Rule: Apollo astronauts carried Pickett slide rules as backup calculators.

chapters.text: Name a food you might find in a school lunchbox

krillion.quip: Japanese rice balls are wrapped in nori, and convenience-store versions use a clever three-step film to keep the seaweed crisp.

quips.Fairy Bread: Australian party staple: buttered white bread covered in hundreds-and-thousands sprinkles.
quips.Tiffin: Mumbai's dabbawalas deliver about 200,000 tiffin lunches a day with famously few mix-ups.
quips.Bento: Some Japanese parents make 'kyaraben' — bentos shaped like cartoon characters.
quips.Cornish Pasty: The thick crimped crust may have been a handle for tin miners with dirty hands.

chapters.text: Name a playground or outdoor children's game

krillion.quip: A South Asian tag game where the raider must chant 'kabaddi' on a single breath while in enemy territory.

deepcut: In and Out the Dusty Bluebells

quips.Conkers: The World Conker Championships have been held in Northamptonshire since 1965.
quips.Knucklebones: Ancient Greeks and Romans played jacks with real sheep ankle bones.
quips.Gaga Ball: Played in an octagonal pit, it's thought to have spread via Israeli summer camps.
quips.Hopscotch: Roman soldiers reportedly ran hopscotch-like courts over 100 feet long in full armour.

chapters.text: Name a word for a baby animal

krillion.quip: A baby llama or alpaca is a cria — Spanish for 'baby' or 'offspring'.

quips.Puggle: A baby echidna or platypus is a puggle — and it hatches from a leathery egg.
quips.Leveret: Leverets are born furry with eyes open, unlike rabbit kits which are born blind and bald.
quips.Cygnet: Cygnets can ride on their parents' backs, tucked between the wings.
quips.Eyas: Falconers call a hawk taken from the nest an eyas — from the French 'niais'.

chapters.text: Name a sound an animal makes

krillion.quip: Crickets 'sing' by stridulating — rubbing a scraper on one wing against a toothed file on the other.

quips.Prusten: Tigers greet friends with 'prusten', a soft puffing snort through the nose.
quips.Chuff: Big cats that can't purr, like lions, chuff instead.
quips.Belling: Red deer stags 'bell' — a deep roar during the autumn rut.
quips.Bray: A donkey's hee-haw can be heard up to 3 km away.

chapters.text: Name a word with a silent letter

krillion.quip: Its silent M comes from Mnemosyne, the Greek goddess of memory and mother of the Muses.

quips.Colonel: Pronounced 'kernel' because English borrowed both the French 'coronel' sound and Italian 'colonnello' spelling.
quips.Debt: Scholars added the B in the 1500s to mimic Latin 'debitum' — it was never pronounced.
quips.Island: The S was inserted by mistake to look like Latin 'insula'; the word actually comes from Old English 'iegland'.
quips.Coxswain: Rowers say 'coxun' — the swain was a boy servant who steered the cock-boat.

chapters.text: Name a maths term you'd learn at school

krillion.quip: That horizontal bar in a fraction, or over a repeating decimal, has a name: the vinculum, Latin for 'bond'.

quips.Fibonacci: Leonardo of Pisa used the sequence to model rabbit breeding in his 1202 book Liber Abaci.
quips.Algebra: From Arabic 'al-jabr', 'restoring broken parts', in a 9th-century book by al-Khwarizmi.
quips.Hypotenuse: Greek for 'stretching under' — the side that stretches under the right angle.
quips.Bus Stop Method: Short division gets this nickname because the sign looks like a bus shelter.

chapters.text: Name a musical term used in music class

krillion.quip: That eye-like symbol over a note tells you to hold it as long as you (or the conductor) like — Italians also call it a 'bird's eye'.

quips.Hemidemisemiquaver: A 64th note — Britain's longest everyday music term, worth one sixteenth of a crotchet.
quips.Tierce de Picardie: Ending a minor-key piece on a major chord; nobody knows what Picardy has to do with it.
quips.Volti Subito: Printed at the bottom of a page: 'turn quickly!' — the next bit starts at once.
quips.Tacet: Latin for 'it is silent' — John Cage's 4'33" is three movements marked Tacet.

chapters.text: Name a period, age or era from history

krillion.quip: Roughly 200 years of relative peace across the Roman Empire, starting with Augustus in 27 BC.

quips.Bronze Age Collapse: Around 1177 BC several Mediterranean civilisations fell within decades — historians still argue why.
quips.Heroic Age of Antarctic Exploration: From 1897 to 1922, it included Scott, Amundsen and Shackleton's expeditions.
quips.Axial Age: Karl Jaspers' name for c. 800–200 BC, when Confucius, Buddha and Socrates all lived.
quips.Little Ice Age: Londoners held Frost Fairs on the frozen Thames during this cold spell.

chapters.text: Name a famous painting

krillion.quip: Van Eyck signed it on the wall: 'Jan van Eyck was here, 1434' — and appears himself in the convex mirror.
