quips.The Night Watch: It got its name because darkened varnish made it look like night — it's actually a daytime scene.
quips.Mona Lisa: It became truly world-famous after being stolen from the Louvre in 1911.
quips.Nighthawks: Hopper said the diner was inspired by one on Greenwich Avenue in New York.
quips.The Ninth Wave: Aivazovsky painted around 6,000 works, most of them seascapes.

chapters.text: Name a mammal

krillion.quip: One of the very few venomous mammals — it delivers toxic saliva through grooves in its lower teeth.

quips.Platypus: It lays eggs, has a duck bill and males carry venomous ankle spurs.
quips.Naked Mole-rat: They can survive 18 minutes without oxygen and rarely get cancer.
quips.Olinguito: Discovered as a new species in 2013 — the first new carnivore in the Americas for 35 years.
quips.Vaquita: The world's rarest marine mammal, with only around ten left in the Gulf of California.

chapters.text: Name an animal that lays eggs

krillion.quip: A female echidna lays a single egg straight into her pouch, where it hatches after about ten days.

quips.Kiwi: A kiwi egg can be about 20% of the mother's body weight — one of the largest relative to body size.
quips.Hoatzin: Hoatzin chicks have claws on their wings to clamber back up if they fall from the nest.
quips.Malleefowl: Malleefowl incubate eggs in a compost mound and test its temperature with their beaks.
quips.Horn Shark: Its corkscrew-shaped egg case gets wedged into rock crevices by the mother.

chapters.text: Name a figure of speech or literary device

krillion.quip: One verb doing two jobs: 'She lost her keys and her temper.'

quips.Chekhov's Gun: Chekhov advised that a rifle hung on the wall in act one must go off by act three.
quips.Mondegreen: Named after a misheard ballad line: 'laid him on the green' heard as 'Lady Mondegreen'.
quips.Spoonerism: Named after Oxford don William Spooner, credited with 'a well-boiled icicle' for 'well-oiled bicycle'.
quips.Tom Swifty: A pun on an adverb: 'I dropped the toothpaste,' said Tom, crestfallen.

chapters.text: Name a grammar term

krillion.quip: A verb wearing a noun costume: in 'Swimming is fun', swimming is a gerund.

quips.Fronted Adverbial: A favourite of UK primary SATs: 'Before breakfast, the cat yowled.'
quips.Pluralia Tantum: Nouns that only exist in the plural, like scissors, trousers and tongs.
quips.Interrobang: The ‽ mark was invented by adman Martin Speckter in 1962.
quips.Comma Splice: Joining two full sentences with just a comma — a classic red-pen favourite.

chapters.text: Name a treaty or peace agreement from history

krillion.quip: The Egyptian–Hittite pact of c. 1259 BC is often called the oldest known peace treaty; a copy hangs at the UN.

quips.Treaty of Tordesillas: In 1494 Spain and Portugal split the non-European world with a line down the Atlantic.
quips.Treaty of Waitangi: Signed in 1840, its English and Māori versions differ in key ways still debated today.
quips.Antarctic Treaty: Since 1959 it has kept the whole continent for peace and science.
quips.Treaty of Wuchale: A translation difference over one verb in this 1889 treaty helped lead to war between Ethiopia and Italy.

chapters.text: Name a landform or geographical feature

krillion.quip: An egg-shaped hill moulded under a moving glacier; clusters of them are nicknamed 'basket of eggs' topography.

quips.Tepui: Venezuela's flat-topped tepuis inspired Arthur Conan Doyle's 'The Lost World'.
quips.Tombolo: St Michael's Mount in Cornwall is linked to the mainland by a tombolo you can walk at low tide.
quips.Pingo: An Inuit word: an ice-cored hill that can grow up to 70 m high in the Arctic.
quips.Billabong: An Australian oxbow lake — the swagman in 'Waltzing Matilda' camped by one.

chapters.text: Name a part of a plant or flower

krillion.quip: When petals and sepals look identical, as in tulips and lilies, botanists call them tepals.

quips.Elaiosome: A fatty snack attached to some seeds that tempts ants into carrying and planting them.
quips.Pollinium: Orchids glue whole packets of pollen, called pollinia, onto visiting insects.
quips.Pneumatophore: Mangrove roots that grow upwards out of the mud to breathe.
quips.Velamen: The spongy white coating on orchid air roots soaks up water like blotting paper.

chapters.text: Name a physics term you'd learn at school

krillion.quip: Newton's first law in a word: objects keep doing what they're doing unless a force says otherwise.

quips.Brownian Motion: Botanist Robert Brown spotted pollen grains jiggling in water in 1827; Einstein explained it in 1905.
quips.Hooke's Law: Robert Hooke first published it as an anagram, 'ceiiinosssttuv', to claim credit secretly.
quips.Absolute Zero: At −273.15 °C, it is the coldest temperature theoretically possible.
quips.Red Shift: Light from distant galaxies is stretched to redder wavelengths, showing the universe is expanding.

chapters.text: Name a word that can be both a noun and a verb

krillion.quip: Originally a noun for gas lamps, it became a verb after the 1944 film 'Gaslight' about psychological manipulation.

quips.Bulldoze: Originally 1870s American slang meaning to intimidate with a 'bull's dose' of a whipping.
quips.Shepherd: Shepherds herd sheep; you can also shepherd a group of kids across the road.
quips.Hijack: Possibly from 1920s bootlegger slang, though nobody is quite sure.
quips.Mushroom: As a verb it means to grow rapidly — like mushrooms after rain.

packs.name: Outer Space
packs.tagline: 21 orbits · beyond the edge of the map

chapters.text: Name something you'd see in the night sky

krillion.quip: A faint cone of sunlight bounced off space dust, seen after dusk far from cities.

quips.Gegenschein: German for 'counter-glow': a faint patch of light directly opposite the Sun.
quips.Earthshine: Sunlight bounced off Earth that dimly lights the dark part of a crescent Moon.
quips.STEVE: A purple ribbon of sky glow named by aurora chasers before scientists studied it.

chapters.text: Name a film or TV series set in space

krillion.quip: 1972 film where Earth's last forests drift in greenhouse domes out near Saturn.

schooler: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
rare: Valerian and the City of a Thousand Planets
Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
deepcut: It! The Terror from Beyond Space
Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
Caravan of Courage: An Ewok Adventure

chapters.text: Name a fictional spaceship

krillion.quip: Powered by the Infinite Improbability Drive in The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy.

chapters.text: Name a fictional planet

krillion.quip: Capital of Asimov's Galactic Empire: one city covering an entire planet.

chapters.text: Name a space agency or spaceflight company

krillion.quip: Dubai's space centre led the Hope probe, which reached orbit around Mars in 2021.

CASC: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation
Khrunichev: Khrunichev State Research and Production Space Center

quips.Glavkosmos: The Soviet Union's commercial space agency, set up to sell launches abroad.
quips.Space Adventures: The company that sent the first paying space tourists to the ISS, starting in 2001.

chapters.text: Name a word with STAR hidden inside it

krillion.quip: Cu-STAR-d: a pudding sauce smuggling a star right through the middle.

chapters.text: Name a song with 'moon' or 'star' in the title

krillion.quip: 1962 instrumental by The Tornados, named after a TV satellite; first UK band US No. 1.

schooler: When You Wish Upon a Star
rare: By the Light of the Silvery Moon

chapters.text: Name an alien species from film, TV, books or games

krillion.quip: Purring furballs from Star Trek that are born pregnant and overrun a starship.

chapters.text: Name a space telescope or observatory

krillion.quip: Puerto Rico's 305 m dish beamed a message to the stars in 1974, then collapsed in 2020.

chapters.text: Name a type of star or other astronomical object

krillion.quip: A theorised star with a neutron star hidden at its core, swallowed by a red supergiant.

quips.Kilonova: The flash from two neutron stars merging, a big source of the universe's gold.
quips.Magnetar: A neutron star whose magnetic field could wipe a credit card from 100,000 km away.
quips.Hycean planet: A proposed world with a hydrogen-rich atmosphere over a global ocean.

chapters.text: Name a spaceflight or rocketry term

krillion.quip: The moment in a launch when aerodynamic stress on the rocket peaks.

quips.Rapid unscheduled disassembly: Rocket-engineer slang for when a vehicle blows up.
quips.Hoverslam: Lighting the engine at the last moment so the rocket stops right at the ground.

chapters.text: Name a galaxy or nebula

krillion.quip: A near-perfect ring galaxy: a yellow core inside a detached blue ring of young stars.

chapters.text: Name a comet, asteroid or meteor shower

krillion.quip: A tiny near-Earth asteroid that may be a chip knocked off our own Moon.

chapters.text: Name a science fiction author

krillion.quip: His 1937 novel Star Maker imagined a cosmos so vast it inspired Arthur C. Clarke.

chapters.text: Name an astronomer or astrophysicist

krillion.quip: Her rule for pulsing Cepheid stars gave astronomers a ruler to measure the universe.

chapters.text: Name a named feature on the Moon or Mars

krillion.quip: The Martian region home to the 'Face on Mars', which sharper photos showed is just a hill.

chapters.text: Name an animal (a species or a famous individual) that has been to space

krillion.quip: In 1963 this French street cat became the first and only cat to fly to space and return.

chapters.text: Name a space station from real life or fiction

krillion.quip: Secret Soviet military stations disguised as Salyuts; one even carried an aircraft cannon.

chapters.text: Name a zodiac sign or astrology term

krillion.quip: The 'thirteenth sign': the Sun really passes through it, but astrology leaves it out.

quips.Saturn return: Astrology's name for your late twenties, when Saturn circles back to its birth spot.
quips.Big three: Your Sun, Moon and rising signs together.

chapters.text: Name a game where you fly a spaceship or explore space

krillion.quip: A tiny solar system stuck in a 22-minute time loop that ends when the Sun explodes.

schooler: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic

chapters.text: Name a superhero or supervillain who comes from another planet

krillion.quip: A giant alien starfish from DC Comics that mind-controls people by clamping onto their faces.

quips.Ch'p: A Green Lantern who is a chipmunk-like alien from the planet H'lven.
quips.Mogo: A Green Lantern who is an entire living planet.

packs.name: Tech & Gadgets
packs.tagline: 21 circuits · rarer answers, bigger bytes

chapters.text: Name a key on a computer keyboard

krillion.quip: The Break key once sent a signal that literally interrupted the telegraph line.

quips.Caps Lock: Google's Chromebooks replaced Caps Lock with a Search key in 2011.
quips.Escape: Bob Bemer added the Escape key in 1960 so programs could switch between codes.
quips.Insert: Insert toggles overtype mode, the culprit behind countless mysteriously deleted words.
quips.Copilot Key: In 2024 Microsoft added the first new Windows keyboard key in nearly 30 years.

chapters.text: Name a computer part or peripheral

krillion.quip: Once a separate chip linking CPU to memory, it was swallowed into the processor itself around 2010.

quips.Mouse: Douglas Engelbart's first mouse in 1964 was carved from a block of wood.
quips.Floppy Drive: The save icon is still a floppy disk, decades after most people last touched one.
quips.Trackball: The trackball predates the mouse, built for a Canadian naval radar system in 1952.
quips.Kensington Lock: That tiny slot on laptops is for a steel cable lock, named after the company that invented it.

chapters.text: Name something you can plug into a USB port

krillion.quip: Novelty USB foam-dart launchers were a real office craze in the late 2000s.

quips.Security Key: A YubiKey stops phishing because it checks the real website address before signing in.
quips.Raspberry Pi: The Raspberry Pi was designed to get British schoolkids coding and has sold over 60 million units.
quips.Lava Lamp: Cloudflare uses a wall of lava lamps to help generate random numbers for encryption.

chapters.text: Name something that has a touchscreen

krillion.quip: Wacom's pen display lets artists draw straight onto the screen they're looking at.

quips.IBM Simon: Released in 1994, IBM Simon was the first touchscreen smartphone, with a stylus and a one-hour battery.
quips.PLATO IV Terminal: This 1972 educational terminal used a grid of infrared beams to sense fingers on its plasma screen.
quips.HP-150: HP sold a touchscreen PC in 1983, but arm fatigue made it a curiosity.
quips.Washlet: Japan's high-tech toilet seats often come with touch control panels on the wall.

chapters.text: Name a gadget that runs on batteries

krillion.quip: Bandai's 1996 digital pet sold over 90 million units and needed feeding even during school.

quips.Speak & Spell: Texas Instruments' 1978 Speak & Spell was one of the first gadgets to use a single-chip speech synthesiser.
quips.Pokewalker: This 2009 Pokemon pedometer let you walk your Pokemon in real life to level them up.
quips.Game & Watch: Gunpei Yokoi got the idea for Game & Watch after watching a bored commuter fiddle with a calculator.
quips.Avalanche Beacon: Skiers carry these transmitters so rescuers can find them under snow on 457 kHz.

chapters.text: Name a famous robot (real or fictional)

krillion.quip: Westinghouse's 1939 robot could walk, talk and smoke cigarettes at the New York World's Fair.

quips.Shakey: Shakey, built at Stanford in 1966, was the first robot able to reason about its own actions.
quips.Talos: In Greek myth, the bronze giant Talos circled Crete three times a day guarding its shores.
quips.Unimate: Unimate became the first industrial robot, joining a General Motors line in 1961.
quips.Gakutensoku: Japan's first robot, built in 1928, could change its facial expression with air pressure.

chapters.text: Name a famous website (not a social network)

krillion.quip: The original Space Jam movie site stayed online untouched for over 20 years.

quips.Million Dollar Homepage: A British student sold one million pixels of this page at one dollar each in 2005 to pay for university.
quips.GeoCities: At its peak GeoCities hosted around 38 million user-built pages before closing in 2009.
quips.Zombo.com: Since 1999 this site has promised you can do anything, and still does nothing at all.
quips.Ask Jeeves: The butler Jeeves was retired in 2006 and the site simply became Ask.com.

chapters.text: Name a famous invention from before 1900

krillion.quip: This Greek bronze gearbox from around 100 BC predicted eclipses and is called the first analogue computer.

quips.Jacquard Loom: Its punched cards for weaving patterns directly inspired early computer programming.
quips.Aeolipile: Hero of Alexandria spun a steam-powered ball around 50 AD, nearly 1,700 years before steam engines caught on.
quips.Difference Engine: London's Science Museum finally built Babbage's design in 1991 and it worked perfectly.

chapters.text: Name a file extension

krillion.quip: Stata's data file format, beloved by economists and almost nobody else.

quips..gif: Its creator Steve Wilhite insisted it is pronounced with a soft g, like the peanut butter brand.
quips..zip: Phil Katz created the ZIP format in 1989 and released it for anyone to use.
quips..exe: Every Windows .exe still begins with the letters MZ, the initials of engineer Mark Zbikowski.
quips..wad: Doom's level files are called WADs, short for Where's All the Data.

chapters.text: Name an operating system

krillion.quip: One programmer built this entire OS alone, including its own language, compiler and games.

quips.Plan 9: Bell Labs named it after the famously bad sci-fi film Plan 9 from Outer Space.
quips.Red Star OS: North Korea's national operating system is a Linux distribution made to look like macOS.
quips.Haiku: Haiku is a volunteer-built revival of BeOS, the OS Apple nearly bought instead of NeXT.
quips.Windows ME: Windows Millennium Edition lasted barely a year before XP replaced it in 2001.

chapters.text: Name a type of cable, plug or connector

krillion.quip: The 50-pin 'Centronics' printer plug was really an Amphenol design borrowed for computers.

quips.Scart: Scart was made mandatory on French TVs in 1980 and its name comes from a French manufacturers' syndicate.
quips.Vampire Tap: Early Ethernet tapped thick coax by literally piercing the cable with a metal tooth.
quips.Type G Plug: The British plug's fuse and shuttered sockets come from post-war copper shortages and safety rules.
quips.Lightning: Apple replaced Lightning with USB-C on iPhones in 2023 after an EU law.

chapters.text: Name a piece of software or desktop app (not a game or social network)

krillion.quip: Its blue two-panel file manager from 1986 still has fan clones like Midnight Commander.

quips.VisiCalc: VisiCalc, the first spreadsheet, was the 'killer app' that made people buy Apple IIs.
quips.HyperCard: Apple's 1987 HyperCard inspired the first wiki and the game Myst.
quips.Winamp: Winamp's startup sample famously promised it really whips the llama's behind.

chapters.text: Name a famous computer scientist or tech pioneer

krillion.quip: She led the software team for Apollo 11 and helped coin the term 'software engineering'.

quips.Grace Hopper: Hopper popularised the word 'debugging' after her team taped a real moth into a logbook in 1947.
quips.Hedy Lamarr: The film star co-invented frequency hopping, an ancestor of Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.
quips.Tommy Flowers: Flowers built Colossus, the first programmable electronic computer, partly with his own money.
quips.Percy Ludgate: An Irish clerk who designed an analytical engine in 1909, working entirely alone.

chapters.text: Name a type of computer threat or cybersecurity term

krillion.quip: Hammering one row of memory chips can flip bits in the row next to it, enough to hijack a computer.

quips.ILOVEYOU: This 2000 email worm infected tens of millions of PCs within days by posing as a love letter.
quips.Creeper: Creeper, from 1971, just displayed 'I'm the creeper, catch me if you can!' and Reaper was written to delete it.
quips.Elk Cloner: A 15-year-old wrote Elk Cloner in 1982, one of the first viruses spread in the wild, as a prank.
quips.Kill Switch: WannaCry was halted when a researcher registered a nonsense domain name hidden in its code.

chapters.text: Name a computing acronym

krillion.quip: Garbage In, Garbage Out: a 1950s warning that computers can't fix bad data.

quips.PEBKAC: Problem Exists Between Keyboard And Chair: tech support's polite way to blame the user.
quips.WYSIWYG: Pronounced 'wiz-ee-wig', it means What You See Is What You Get.
quips.CAPTCHA: It stands for Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart.
quips.NaN: Not a Number is so odd that in most languages NaN is not even equal to itself.

chapters.text: Name a unit or measurement used in tech or electronics

krillion.quip: A unit of information named after Claude Shannon, equal to one bit of surprise.

quips.Jiffy: In Linux a jiffy is one tick of the system timer, often a hundredth or thousandth of a second.
quips.Nibble: Half a byte is a nibble, and some jokers call two bits a crumb.
quips.Shake: A shake is 10 nanoseconds, coined by Manhattan Project scientists from 'two shakes of a lamb's tail'.
quips.Twip: A twip is a twentieth of a printer's point and is used inside Microsoft Word files.

chapters.text: Name a type of sensor

krillion.quip: Your phone's compass is a tiny magnetometer that can be confused by a fridge magnet.

quips.Electronic Nose: Electronic noses can sniff out spoiled food, gas leaks and even some diseases.
quips.SQUID: A SQUID is so sensitive it can detect the magnetic fields made by the human brain.
quips.Cliff Sensor: Robot vacuums use downward-facing cliff sensors so they don't tumble down the stairs.
quips.Star Tracker: Spacecraft find their orientation by photographing stars and matching them to an onboard map.

chapters.text: Name a famous historical computer or calculating machine

krillion.quip: Konrad Zuse's 1941 Z3 was the first working programmable computer, built in Berlin.

quips.Colossus: Colossus was kept secret until the 1970s, so for decades ENIAC was wrongly called the first electronic computer.
quips.MONIAC: MONIAC modelled the UK economy using coloured water flowing through tanks and pipes.
quips.Galaksija: Galaksija was a Yugoslav home computer people built themselves from instructions printed in a magazine.
quips.Setun: Setun, built in Moscow in 1958, ran on ternary logic using three states instead of two.

chapters.text: Name an electronic component

krillion.quip: Predicted in 1971 as the missing fourth basic component, a working one was only built by HP in 2008.

quips.Nixie Tube: Nixie tubes glow orange numbers using neon gas and are prized for retro clocks today.
quips.Cat's Whisker Detector: Early crystal radios used a fine wire touching a galena crystal to pick up broadcasts.
quips.Williams Tube: The first stored-program computer kept its memory as dots on a TV-like screen.
quips.555 Timer: The 555 timer, designed in 1971, may be the most-produced chip in history, billions per year.

chapters.text: Name an internet protocol, standard or format

krillion.quip: Gopher was a menu-based rival to the web in 1991, named after the University of Minnesota mascot.

quips.Finger: The 1971 Finger protocol let you check if someone was logged in and read their 'plan' file.
quips.Morse Code: The ship-to-shore Morse distress call SOS was chosen because it is easy to send, not as an acronym.
quips.IPFS: IPFS fetches files by what they contain rather than where they are stored.
quips.RSS: RSS lets you subscribe to sites, and a 14-year-old Aaron Swartz helped write version 1.0.

chapters.text: Name a data structure or algorithm

krillion.quip: Bogosort shuffles a list randomly until it happens to be sorted, possibly forever.

quips.Spaghetti Sort: Spaghetti sort cuts uncooked spaghetti to each number's length, then lowers your hand on them.
quips.Sleep Sort: Sleep sort starts a timer per number and prints each one when its timer runs out.
quips.Fisher-Yates Shuffle: This 1938 shuffling method was first done by hand with pencil, paper and a random number table.
quips.Timsort: Tim Peters wrote Timsort for Python in 2002, and Java and Android later adopted it.

packs.name: Toys & Childhood
packs.tagline: 21 toy boxes · dig through the playroom

chapters.text: Name a LEGO theme or product line

krillion.quip: LEGO Rock Raiders (1999) sent minifigure miners to dig for energy crystals underground.

quips.Technic: LEGO Technic launched in 1977 and added gears, motors and pneumatics to bricks.

chapters.text: Name a doll or action figure line

krillion.quip: Rainbow Brite dolls, introduced in 1983 by Hallmark, came with colour kids and a horse called Starlite.

G.I. Joe: G.I. Joe: A Real American Hero

quips.Barbie: Barbie debuted at the New York Toy Fair in 1959 and is named after creator Ruth Handler's daughter.

chapters.text: Name a classic toy

krillion.quip: Cup-and-ball toys date back centuries and are still sold as 'kendama' in Japan.

quips.Slinky: The Slinky was invented by accident in 1943 when a naval engineer dropped a tension spring.

chapters.text: Name a playground or schoolyard game

krillion.quip: In Ghost in the Graveyard, one hider waits for the others to sneak up and shout 'ghost!'

quips.Pooh sticks: Pooh sticks comes from A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh books and has its own world championship.

chapters.text: Name a toy company or toy brand

krillion.quip: Melissa & Doug began in 1988 and became known for classic wooden toys and puzzles.

quips.LEGO: The name LEGO comes from the Danish 'leg godt', meaning 'play well'.

chapters.text: Name a famous teddy bear, plush toy or stuffed-animal brand

krillion.quip: Rilakkuma is a Japanese plush bear who loves lounging so much he is named for 'relax bear'.

quips.Teddy bear: The teddy bear is named after US President Theodore 'Teddy' Roosevelt after a 1902 hunting trip.

chapters.text: Name a toy craze or fad

krillion.quip: Crazy Bones were tiny collectible figures that took over playgrounds around 1998.

quips.Pet Rock: The Pet Rock sold over a million units in 1975 and was literally a rock in a cardboard box.

chapters.text: Name an outdoor toy or backyard game

krillion.quip: Swingball is a ball-on-a-string tennis game played around a pole in the garden.

quips.Frisbee: The Frisbee was inspired by pie tins from the Frisbie Baking Company that students tossed around.

chapters.text: Name a building or construction toy

krillion.quip: Rokenbok is a building system whose remote-controlled vehicles load and haul blocks.

quips.Lincoln Logs: Lincoln Logs were invented in 1916 by John Lloyd Wright, son of architect Frank Lloyd Wright.

chapters.text: Name a toy car or toy vehicle brand

krillion.quip: Choro-Q are tiny Japanese pull-back toy cars with big chubby proportions.

quips.Hot Wheels: Hot Wheels launched in 1968 as Mattel's answer to Matchbox cars.

chapters.text: Name a Transformers character

krillion.quip: Wheeljack is the Autobot inventor, known for explosive experiments in his lab.

quips.Optimus Prime: Optimus Prime has been voiced by Peter Cullen since the original 1984 cartoon.

chapters.text: Name a trading card game or collectible card brand

krillion.quip: Cardfight!! Vanguard started as a Japanese anime and card game in 2011.

quips.Magic: The Gathering: Magic: The Gathering launched in 1993 and is generally credited as the first modern trading card game.

chapters.text: Name an electronic toy or handheld

krillion.quip: Big Trak was a programmable toy tank from 1979 that you steered with a keypad.

quips.Simon: Simon was invented in 1978 by Ralph Baer, the 'father of video games', and Howard Morrison.

chapters.text: Name a toy franchise from the 1980s

krillion.quip: Sectaurs were Coleco's insect-riding action figures and toy line from 1985.

He-Man: He-Man and the Masters of the Universe
G.I. Joe: G.I. Joe: A Real American Hero

quips.Cabbage Patch Kids: In 1983 Cabbage Patch Kids sparked store scuffles as parents scrambled to find one.

chapters.text: Name a toy or game that tests your balance, aim or steady hands

krillion.quip: In Pop-Up Pirate you poke swords into a barrel until someone launches the pirate out.

quips.Jenga: Jenga comes from the Swahili word for 'to build'.

chapters.text: Name a ride-on or wheeled toy

krillion.quip: The Space Hopper, a giant inflatable bouncing ball with ears, was a 1960s craze.

quips.Big Wheel: The Big Wheel, a low plastic trike, first rolled out in 1969 and became a backyard icon.

chapters.text: Name something you'd find at a children's birthday party

krillion.quip: In Pass the parcel, a gift wrapped in many layers is handed around until the music stops.

schooler: Pin the tail on the donkey

Pin the tail on the donkey: Pin the Tail on the Donkey

quips.Pin the tail on the donkey: Pin the tail on the donkey has been a party staple since the early 1900s.

chapters.text: Name a creative or craft toy

krillion.quip: Spirograph, from 1965, uses toothed rings to draw looping geometric patterns.

quips.Silly Putty: Silly Putty came from a failed attempt to make synthetic rubber in the 1940s.

krillion.quip: Doctor Foster went to Gloucester in a shower of rain and stepped in a puddle up to his middle.

quips.Humpty Dumpty: Nowhere in the original rhyme is Humpty Dumpty described as an egg.

chapters.text: Name a fairy tale, fable or traditional children's story

krillion.quip: In this Grimm tale, tiny elves secretly make shoes for a struggling cobbler each night.

rare: The Town Mouse and the Country Mouse

East of the Sun and West of the Moon: East of the Sun West of the Moon

quips.Cinderella: Versions of Cinderella exist worldwide; one of the earliest is a Chinese tale from around 850 CE.

chapters.text: Name a Mr. Men or Little Miss character

krillion.quip: Mr. Topsy-Turvy does everything the wrong way round, like walking on his hands.

quips.Mr. Tickle: Roger Hargreaves created Mr. Tickle in 1971 after his son asked what a tickle looks like.

packs.name: Languages & World Cultures
packs.tagline: 21 tongues & tables · say hello, eat well, borrow boldly

chapters.text: Name a way to say "hello" in another language

krillion.quip: The everyday Burmese greeting, literally wishing you something auspicious.

quips.Kia ora: Māori greeting that also means thank you and literally wishes good health.
quips.Aloha: Hawaiian word that covers hello, goodbye and love.
quips.Grüß Gott: Southern German and Austrian hello meaning 'God greet you'.
quips.Yá'át'ééh: The Navajo greeting, literally 'it is good'.

chapters.text: Name a word English borrowed from Spanish

krillion.quip: Cowboy slang for jail, from Spanish 'juzgado', a courtroom.

quips.Cockroach: English speakers mangled Spanish 'cucaracha' into cock + roach.
quips.Vamoose: Wild West rendering of Spanish 'vamos', let's go.

chapters.text: Name a Chinese dish

krillion.quip: 'Buddha jumps over the wall', a Fujian soup so fragrant a monk supposedly leapt a wall for it.

quips.Chop suey: Largely an American-Chinese invention, though its roots trace to Taishan.
quips.Fortune cookies: Most likely Japanese-American in origin, and almost unknown in China.
quips.Century egg: Preserved for weeks in clay, ash and lime, not a century.
quips.Ants climbing a tree: Sichuan glass noodles whose minced pork bits resemble ants on branches.

chapters.text: Name a way to say "thank you" in another language

krillion.quip: The polite Thai thanks when said by a man; women end it with 'ka'.

quips.Mahalo: Hawaiian thanks; 'mahalo nui loa' means thank you very much.
quips.Diolch: Welsh thanks; 'diolch yn fawr' is the big version.
quips.Miigwech: Ojibwe word of thanks used across the Great Lakes.
quips.Eskerrik asko: Basque, a language unrelated to any other living language.

chapters.text: Name a Mexican dish or food

krillion.quip: Toasted grasshoppers, a crunchy Oaxacan snack with lime and chilli.

quips.Huitlacoche: Corn smut fungus, prized as the 'Mexican truffle'.
quips.Escamoles: Ant larvae, sometimes called insect caviar.
quips.Chile en nogada: Green, white and red, matching the Mexican flag.

chapters.text: Name a country whose flag has green on it

krillion.quip: Its flag shows a Sisserou parrot, making it one of the only national flags with purple.

quips.Libya: Until 2011 its flag was plain green, the only single-colour national flag.
quips.Mauritania: Added red stripes in 2017 to honour those who fought for independence.
quips.Mozambique: The only national flag featuring a modern rifle, an AK-47.
quips.Brazil: Its starry globe shows the sky over Rio on the morning of 15 November 1889.

chapters.text: Name a way to say "goodbye" in another language

krillion.quip: Irish for 'safe home', said to someone heading off.

quips.Sayonara: Literally 'if it must be so' in Japanese.
quips.Adieu: French for 'to God', a farewell for a long time.
quips.Tschüss: Possibly descends from Spanish 'adiós' via Low German 'adjüs'.
quips.Aloha ʻoe: Hawaiian farewell song written by Queen Liliʻuokalani.

chapters.text: Name a word English borrowed from German

krillion.quip: A cosy, warm, sociable feeling that English never quite managed to translate.

quips.Kindergarten: Coined by Friedrich Fröbel in 1840, literally 'children's garden'.
quips.Hamster: From Old High German 'hamustro', a grain weevil.

chapters.text: Name a word English borrowed from Arabic

krillion.quip: From Arabic 'gharrāfa', a drinking vessel, travelling via Spanish and Italian.

quips.Checkmate: From Persian/Arabic 'shāh māt', the king is helpless.
quips.Admiral: From Arabic 'amīr al-', commander of the.
quips.Betelgeuse: Many star names are Arabic; this one is a mangled 'hand of al-Jawzā'.

chapters.text: Name a Middle Eastern dish

krillion.quip: Jordan's national dish: lamb cooked in fermented dried yogurt called jameed.

quips.Tahdig: The crispy golden crust at the bottom of a pot of Persian rice, fought over at the table.
quips.İmam bayıldı: Turkish for 'the imam fainted', supposedly from sheer delight.
quips.Shakshuka: Eggs poached in spiced tomato sauce, popular from Tunisia to Israel.

chapters.text: Name a type of dumpling from anywhere in the world

krillion.quip: Georgian soup dumplings; you hold the knot, sip the broth, and leave the knot on the plate to count.

quips.Pelmeni: Siberian hunters froze them in snow for long winter trips.
quips.Momo: Tibetan and Nepali dumpling, usually served with a fiery tomato achar.
quips.Cepelinai: Lithuanian potato dumplings named for their resemblance to Zeppelin airships.
quips.Modak: Sweet dumpling said to be the Hindu god Ganesha's favourite food.

chapters.text: Name a word English borrowed from Italian

krillion.quip: A quarantine station, named after a Venetian island hospital.

quips.Paparazzi: Named after a pushy photographer called Paparazzo in Fellini's La Dolce Vita.
quips.Quarantine: From Venetian 'quaranta giorni', forty days of isolation for ships.
quips.Influenza: Italian for 'influence', once blamed on the stars.
quips.Ballot: From Italian 'ballotta', a little ball used to vote in Venice.

chapters.text: Name a word English borrowed from Hindi, Urdu or Sanskrit

krillion.quip: British army slang for going mad, from the Deolali transit camp near Mumbai.

quips.Shampoo: From Hindi 'chāmpo', to press or massage the head.
quips.Thug: From the Thuggee bandits of colonial India.
quips.Bungalow: From Hindi 'banglā', a house in the Bengal style.

chapters.text: Name a street food from anywhere in the world

krillion.quip: Sri Lankan chopped flatbread stir-fry, made with a rhythmic clatter of metal blades on a griddle.

quips.Bunny chow: A hollowed loaf of bread filled with curry, born in Durban.
quips.Balut: A fertilised duck egg boiled and eaten from the shell in the Philippines.
quips.Rolex: Ugandan chapati rolled around an omelette: rolled eggs, say it fast.
quips.Currywurst: Invented in Berlin in 1949 when a snack-bar owner swapped ketchup for curry powder.

chapters.text: Name a word English borrowed from Dutch

krillion.quip: An old word for a big knife, from Dutch 'steken of snijden', to stab or cut.

quips.Cookie: From Dutch 'koekje', little cake, via New Amsterdam.
quips.Boss: From Dutch 'baas', master, popular in early America to avoid saying 'master'.
quips.Yacht: From 'jacht', short for 'jachtschip', a hunting ship.

chapters.text: Name a word English borrowed from an Indigenous language of the Americas

krillion.quip: Chinook Jargon for food; 'high muckamuck' came to mean a self-important boss.

quips.Caucus: Possibly from an Algonquian word for counsellor.
quips.Axolotl: Nahuatl for 'water dog', named for the god Xolotl.

chapters.text: Name an everyday English word that comes from Old Norse

krillion.quip: An old division of an English shire, named for the weapon-brandishing used to approve decisions.

quips.Sky: Old Norse 'ský' meant cloud; English 'heaven' lost ground to it.
quips.Egg: Replaced the native Old English 'ey' after a long tussle in the 1400s.
quips.They: English borrowed even its plural pronouns from the Vikings.

chapters.text: Name a Latin word or phrase used as-is in English

krillion.quip: Latin 'what now?', an old word for a nosy gossip always after the latest news.

quips.Alibi: Latin for 'elsewhere', which is exactly what you claim with one.
quips.Recipe: Latin for 'take!', the first word of old prescriptions.
quips.Quorum: Latin 'of whom', from the wording of old commissions.

chapters.text: Name a currency or coin that is no longer in use

krillion.quip: Hyperinflation reached the point where a 100 trillion dollar note was printed in 2009.

quips.Doubloon: Spanish gold coin worth two escudos, hence 'doblón', a double.
quips.Farthing: A quarter of a penny, from Old English for 'fourth part'.
quips.Assignat: Paper money of the French Revolution, backed by seized church lands.
quips.Sestertius: Roman coin; prices in Pompeii graffiti are often given in them.

chapters.text: Name a language that is extinct or no longer spoken natively

krillion.quip: An Alaskan language whose last native speaker, Marie Smith Jones, died in 2008.

quips.Manx: Last native speaker Ned Maddrell died in 1974, but the language is being revived.
quips.Cornish: Declared extinct in the 1700s, it was revived and recognised again in 2002.
quips.Ubykh: Had around 84 consonants; its last fluent speaker died in 1992.
quips.Norn: A Norse language once spoken in Orkney and Shetland.

chapters.text: Name a French dish

krillion.quip: Cheesy mashed potato from the Aubrac plateau, stretched into long elastic ribbons at the table.

deepcut: Tripes à la mode de Caen

quips.French toast: Called 'pain perdu', lost bread, in France, a way to rescue stale loaves.
quips.Croissant: Its ancestor was the Austrian kipferl, brought to Paris in the 1800s.
quips.Welsh rarebit: A northern French bistro staple in Lille, despite the Welsh name.
quips.Tablier de sapeur: Lyonnaise breaded tripe named after a sapper's leather apron.

packs.name: Dinosaurs & Prehistoric Life
packs.tagline: 21 fossils · dig up the deep past

chapters.text: Name a meat-eating dinosaur

krillion.quip: A tiny Jurassic cousin of T. rex from Siberia, its name means 'lizard' in a local Khakas language.

quips.Mei: Its full name, Mei long, means 'soundly sleeping dragon' - it was fossilised curled up like a napping bird.
quips.Yi: Yi qi had bat-like skin wings, and its one-syllable name is among the shortest of any dinosaur.
quips.Deinocheirus: Known for decades only from 2.4 m arms, it turned out to be a humpbacked, duck-billed giant.
quips.Balaur: This island raptor from Romania had two big sickle claws on each foot instead of one.

chapters.text: Name a long-necked dinosaur (sauropod or prosauropod)

krillion.quip: Its name means 'a giant thunderclap at dawn' in Sesotho - a 12-tonne early giant from South Africa.

quips.Brontosaurus: Sunk into Apatosaurus for a century, it was revived as its own genus in 2015.
quips.Nigersaurus: Its 500-odd teeth were replaced as often as every 14 days, like a vacuum-cleaner mouth.
quips.Zby: Named after palaeontologist Georges Zbyszewski, it has one of the shortest dinosaur names.
quips.Mamenchisaurus: Its neck could make up half its total body length.

chapters.text: Name a prehistoric animal that is NOT a dinosaur

krillion.quip: The 'Tully monster' is so weird that scientists still argue whether it was a fish, a worm or a mollusc.

quips.Dimetrodon: That sail-backed 'dinosaur' was actually closer to mammals and lived 40 million years before the first dinosaurs.
quips.Pterodactyl: Pterosaurs flew alongside dinosaurs but were a separate branch of reptiles.
quips.Arthropleura: This Carboniferous millipede grew over 2 metres long.
quips.Helicoprion: Its teeth grew in a spiral 'buzz-saw' whorl in the lower jaw.

chapters.text: Name an Ice Age (Pleistocene) animal

krillion.quip: A rodent the size of a bull from Uruguay - the largest rodent ever known.

quips.Woolly mammoth: The last mammoths survived on Wrangel Island until about 4,000 years ago - after the pyramids were built.
quips.Glyptodon: This armadillo relative was the size of a small car, and early humans may have sheltered in its shell.
quips.Irish elk: Its antlers spanned up to 3.6 metres - and it wasn't only Irish, nor an elk.
quips.Short-faced bear: Standing upright it may have topped 3 metres.

chapters.text: Name a dinosaur movie, TV show, game or book

krillion.quip: The silent film adaptation of Conan Doyle's novel used stop-motion dinosaurs by Willis O'Brien, later of King Kong fame.

schooler: Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs
rare: Harry and His Bucket Full of Dinosaurs
Journey to the Center of the Earth
Baby: Secret of the Lost Legend
deepcut: Harry and the Bucketful of Dinosaurs

quips.Gertie the Dinosaur: Winsor McCay's 1914 cartoon is one of the first animated films ever to star a character.
quips.Chrome Dino: The offline T. rex game in Google Chrome is codenamed 'Project Bolan' after T. Rex singer Marc Bolan.
quips.Primal Rage: This 1994 fighting game used stop-motion dinosaur models digitised for the arcade.
quips.Prehistoric Planet: Its dinosaurs were narrated by David Attenborough and many were shown with feathers.

chapters.text: Name a dinosaur body part or feature

krillion.quip: Belly ribs - a basket of floating bones under the gut that helped dinosaurs like T. rex breathe.

quips.Thagomizer: The name for a stegosaur's tail spikes comes from a 1982 Far Side cartoon by Gary Larson.
quips.Gastroliths: Some sauropods swallowed stones to help grind plants in their gut.
quips.Quill knobs: Bumps on Velociraptor's forearm show where its big wing feathers attached.
quips.Sclerotic ring: These bony eye rings help scientists guess whether a dinosaur was active by night.

chapters.text: Name a geological period, era or epoch

krillion.quip: The first period of the Mesoproterozoic, named from the Greek for 'cover' because platform rocks blanketed older ones.

quips.Carboniferous: Named for the coal (carbon) beds formed from its vast swamp forests.
quips.Jurassic: Named after the Jura Mountains on the France-Switzerland border.
quips.Cretaceous: From the Latin 'creta', meaning chalk - think of the White Cliffs of Dover.
quips.Meghalayan: The current age of the Holocene, named after a cave in the Indian state of Meghalaya.

chapters.text: Name a pterosaur (flying reptile)

krillion.quip: A sparrow-sized pterosaur from China with grasping feet, possibly a tree-dweller.

quips.Quetzalcoatlus: With a wingspan near 10 m it was as wide as a small plane, yet it probably hunted on foot like a giant stork.
quips.Pterodaustro: Its hundreds of bristle-like teeth filtered food like a flamingo - and it may even have been pink.
quips.Dearc: Found on Scotland's Isle of Skye, it is the largest known Jurassic pterosaur.
quips.Thapunngaka: Australia's largest pterosaur had a 7 m wingspan and a spear-like jaw crest.

chapters.text: Name a marine reptile from the age of dinosaurs

krillion.quip: A Triassic sea reptile with a zipper-like, hammer-shaped jaw for grazing seaweed.

quips.Mosasaurus: Mosasaurs weren't dinosaurs at all - they were giant seagoing lizards related to monitors and snakes.
quips.Elasmosaurus: Its neck held 72 vertebrae, and Edward Drinker Cope first put its head on the wrong end.
quips.Archelon: The largest sea turtle ever, about 4.6 m long.
quips.Shonisaurus: Nevada's state fossil was an ichthyosaur as long as a bus.

chapters.text: Name a horned dinosaur (ceratopsian)

krillion.quip: Named after fossil hunter Wendy Sloboda, whose discoveries in Alberta led to it.

quips.Triceratops: Its frill could be over a metre wide, and baby Triceratops had tiny stubby horns that changed as they grew.
quips.Kosmoceratops: With 15 horns it has the most ornate skull of any known dinosaur.
quips.Psittacosaurus: One fossil preserved its colour pattern: dark on top, pale below, for camouflage.

chapters.text: Name an armoured dinosaur (ankylosaur or stegosaur)

krillion.quip: So well preserved it looks like a statue - it even kept its stomach contents and reddish colour.

quips.Stegosaurus: T. rex lived closer in time to us than to Stegosaurus.
quips.Zuul: Named after the monster in Ghostbusters, its whole tail club and skin were preserved.
quips.Spicomellus: The oldest ankylosaur known, with spikes fused directly onto its ribs.
quips.Minmi: Named after Minmi Crossing in Queensland, it was long the shortest dinosaur genus name.

chapters.text: Name a duck-billed or beaked plant-eating dinosaur (ornithopod or pachycephalosaur)

krillion.quip: A dwarf hadrosaur from an ancient Italian island, nicknamed 'Antonio'.

quips.Iguanodon: Its thumb spike was first reconstructed as a horn on its nose.
quips.Maiasaura: Its name means 'good mother lizard' - it was found with nests of babies.
quips.Parasaurolophus: Its hollow crest worked like a trombone to make deep calls.
quips.Leaellynasaura: Named after the daughter of its discoverers, it lived in polar forests with months of darkness.

chapters.text: Name a famous fossil site or rock formation

krillion.quip: A North Dakota site that may preserve fish killed within hours of the asteroid impact 66 million years ago.

quips.Burgess Shale: Found by Charles Walcott in 1909 high in the Canadian Rockies, it preserves soft-bodied Cambrian animals.
quips.Messel Pit: This German pit preserved fossil birds with feather colours and mammals with their last meals.
quips.Solnhofen: Every good Archaeopteryx skeleton comes from these fine limestone quarries in Bavaria.
quips.Lark Quarry: Its 3,000-plus footprints were once thought to record a dinosaur stampede.

chapters.text: Name a palaeontologist or famous fossil hunter

krillion.quip: A Canadian fossil hunter who found her first important fossil as a teenager and has a ceratopsian named after her.

quips.Mary Anning: She found her first ichthyosaur skull around age 12 on the cliffs at Lyme Regis.
quips.Roy Chapman Andrews: His 1920s Gobi expeditions found the first widely recognised dinosaur eggs - and he may have inspired Indiana Jones.
quips.Barnum Brown: He discovered the first Tyrannosaurus rex skeleton in 1902.
quips.Franz Nopcsa: This Transylvanian baron worked out that dwarf dinosaurs lived on islands.

chapters.text: Name a prehistoric sea creature that is not a reptile

krillion.quip: A 2-metre Ordovician filter-feeder, one of the largest animals of its time.

quips.Anomalocaris: This Cambrian top predator had grasping head appendages and a pineapple-ring mouth.
quips.Dunkleosteus: Instead of teeth this armoured fish had self-sharpening bony blades.
quips.Leedsichthys: Possibly the largest bony fish ever, it was a gentle plankton-eater.
quips.Livyatan: Named after the biblical Leviathan and Herman Melville, this whale had teeth 36 cm long.

chapters.text: Name a prehistoric plant or plant group

krillion.quip: Its fossil leaves on India, Africa, Australia, South America and Antarctica helped prove continental drift.

quips.Wollemi pine: Known only from fossils until a park ranger found living trees in an Australian canyon in 1994.
quips.Lepidodendron: These 'scale trees' grew 40 m tall in coal swamps and were related to tiny clubmosses.
quips.Prototaxites: An 8-metre 'tree trunk' of the Devonian that was actually a giant fungus.
quips.Cooksonia: One of the earliest land plants, just a few centimetres tall with no leaves.

chapters.text: Name a feathered dinosaur

krillion.quip: A small Siberian plant-eater with feathers - evidence that fuzz may go back to the earliest dinosaurs.

quips.Yutyrannus: Its name means 'beautiful feathered tyrant' - a 9 m tyrannosauroid covered in filaments.
quips.Microraptor: It had flight feathers on all four limbs, and its plumage was iridescent black like a crow.
quips.Caihong: Its name means 'rainbow' - fossil pigment cells suggest a shimmering head.
quips.Archaeopteryx: The famous 'Berlin specimen' was found just a year or two after Darwin's Origin of Species.

chapters.text: Name a dinosaur discovered in China

krillion.quip: A small troodontid from Liaoning whose name means 'Chinese sinus nose'.

quips.Mamenchisaurus: Named after Mamenxi ferry crossing in Sichuan, where workers found it while building a road.
quips.Sinosauropteryx: The first dinosaur ever found with fuzzy feathers, and its ginger-and-white striped tail was later reconstructed.
quips.Lingwulong: This Jurassic diplodocoid showed the group reached Asia earlier than thought.
quips.Shantungosaurus: At around 15 m long it is one of the largest duck-billed dinosaurs.

chapters.text: Name an animal that lived before the dinosaurs (Palaeozoic era)

krillion.quip: A 375-million-year-old 'fishapod' with a neck and wrist bones - a snapshot of fish moving onto land.

quips.Dimetrodon: Often mistaken for a dinosaur, it is actually more closely related to you than to T. rex.
quips.Meganeura: This Carboniferous griffinfly had a 70 cm wingspan, helped by oxygen-rich air.
quips.Lystrosaurus: After the Great Dying, this pig-sized plant-eater was found almost everywhere on Earth.
quips.Hylonomus: One of the earliest known reptiles, found fossilised inside a hollow tree stump in Nova Scotia.

chapters.text: Name a dinosaur discovered in South America

krillion.quip: A Patagonian sauropod that survived a volcanic crisis 180 million years ago by switching to tougher plants.

quips.Carnotaurus: Its arms were so tiny they make T. rex's look long, and it had bull-like horns.
quips.Thanos: This Brazilian abelisaur really is named after the Marvel villain - and the Greek word for death.
quips.Maip: Named after an evil spirit of local Tehuelche legend, it was a 9 m megaraptoran.
quips.Eoraptor: One of the earliest dinosaurs, a fox-sized hunter from Argentina's Valley of the Moon.

chapters.text: Name a prehistoric mammal from before the Ice Age

krillion.quip: An Oligocene dolphin that hunted like an orca - a whale lineage that evolved apex predation twice.

quips.Paraceratherium: A hornless rhino relative about 5 m tall at the shoulder - one of the largest land mammals ever.
quips.Andrewsarchus: Known only from one giant skull found in Mongolia in 1923, it was probably related to hippos and whales.
quips.Darwinius: Nicknamed 'Ida', this 47-million-year-old primate was so complete its last meal was preserved.
quips.Perucetus: This Peruvian whale may have been the heaviest animal ever, rivalling the blue whale.
